# REOPENED 2026-08-13 — automatic triage never fires where tasks are filed

Reported by Mike during the E-1958 brainstorm: triage "takes fucking forever."
A task an agent files sits `untriaged` long enough that the agent surfaces the
state to Mike instead of the routing quietly resolving it. Five defects, all in
code this task landed. Fix them here rather than in a new task.

Fix them IN ORDER — Fix 1 activates a race that Fix 2 must already cover.

## Fix 1 — `inline_suppressed()` is over-broad (the primary cause)

`triage.inline_suppressed()` suppresses file-time triage whenever
`config.gated_worktree_root()` is non-None and the resolved config dir is the
main one — i.e. `--db main` from inside a self-dev worktree. That is exactly how
every agent session in this repo is told to file, and agents file ~99% of tasks.
So in endless's own repo the inline path never runs and everything waits on the
sweep.

The rationale it copied is E-698's, in `internal/jobs/suppress.go`
(`suppressedWithReason`): candidate code must not write the real ledger. Correct
THERE — the Claude hooks invoke `<worktree>/bin/endless-go`. Not true here.
Under `--db main` from a worktree:

- the child `spawn_detached` launches is `sys.argv[0]`, the `endless` shim,
  which `just install` points at the MAIN checkout's editable source;
- that child writes through `event_bridge._resolve_endless_go()`, which prefers
  the worktree binary ONLY under `--db sandbox` and otherwise falls back to the
  PATH-resolved global.

Both halves are already landed code. Confirmed empirically: the justfile's
`verify` recipe runs `endless --db sandbox task verify` — the global shim — and
only the `test` recipe's `uv run pytest` resolves worktree Python.

The correct rule is a pair, not one condition:

| binary    | DB      | verdict                       |
|-----------|---------|-------------------------------|
| candidate | sandbox | fine — this IS the test       |
| candidate | real    | forbidden — the E-698 hazard  |
| landed    | real    | fine — this is triage         |

**Do:** gate on the resolved CLI/binary path lying outside the worktree, NOT on
`self_dev`. Do not merely delete the clause — path-gating stays correct if
anyone later runs `uv run endless` from a worktree, which today nobody does.
Leave the `ENDLESS_NO_TRIAGE` opt-out untouched.

## Fix 2 — the inline path takes no lease (PREREQUISITE of Fix 1)

Sweep-vs-sweep is already safe: `internal/jobs` claims with a CAS lease (single
conditional UPDATE, SQLite's clock for every due/expiry comparison), so the N
`session monitor` instances across N tmux windows that each call `jobs.RunDue`
contend and exactly one wins. `triagejob`'s Schedule sets `LeaseTTL` explicitly
as `batchLimit * perTaskTimeout + leaseHeadroom`, NOT derived from Interval, so
shortening the interval does not shrink the lease.

The gap is inline-vs-sweep. `triage.spawn_detached` runs `endless triage run
--task N` directly — it never enters the jobs runner and takes no lease at all:

1. task filed; inline child begins a model call (up to `CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`)
2. the sweep fires meanwhile and selects N, still `untriaged` because the child
   has not written yet
3. both call the model for the same task

Python re-reads the row and guards the write, so state does not corrupt — but
the re-read happens AFTER the model call, so the spend is already doubled.

This is latent TODAY only because Fix 1's bug means the inline path never runs
in a worktree. Unsuppressing it makes the window real; shortening the interval
widens it. Mike: "IT WILL HAPPEN, so we can't assume a longer delay will solve
it."

**Do:** take a per-task claim BEFORE the model call, honored by both paths, so
a second attempt from either skips a task already in flight. Must survive a
crashed claimant (time-boxed like the job lease, not an OS lock). Land this
with or before Fix 1.

## Fix 3 — child failures must reach the user, not DEVNULL

`triage.spawn_detached` sends stdin, stdout and stderr to DEVNULL. `triage.run`
is already fail-open by design (timeout, missing `claude`, non-zero exit,
unparseable verdict all silently leave the task `untriaged`), so DEVNULL on top
makes a crash indistinguishable from a considered no-verdict, recorded nowhere.
Some share of the reported latency may be the child dying unseen.

**Do:** surface failures where a user actually sees them — `session monitor`,
per Mike — not merely a log file. Keep fire-and-forget semantics: the parent
still must not block on the child. Logging is the floor; the monitor is the
requirement.

Mike's standing rule, stated here because this violated it: code must not
silently ignore errors.

## Fix 3b — a worktree's stale hook binary fails invisibly, the same defect one layer out

Added 2026-08-13 at Mike's direction. Same root as Fix 3 (a failure nobody can
see), different subsystem — scope it with Fix 3's monitor work rather than as
separate plumbing.

Observed: `session goto 1808 --resume` opened a live Claude session in
`.endless/worktrees/e-1808` that endless could not see at all. Sibling panes
could not resolve it; the DB row still read `state=ended`, `process=''`.

Cause: that worktree's `.claude/settings.json` pins every hook to its OWN
`bin/endless-go`, built Jul 29. Run read-only it fails immediately —

    resolve project: task_types integrity check: tasktype: id=1 slug mismatch:
      enum="task", table="todo"

— the E-1659 `task`→`todo` / `bug`→`bugfix` rename. The binary carries the old
enum, every current DB carries the new value, so the integrity check aborts the
process before it does anything. SessionStart therefore never registers the pane,
and the failure goes to hook stderr, which nobody reads.

Why the pin exists: E-998, "so spawned sessions test the worktree's hook." The
alternative it replaced was repointing the global symlink, which put every other
live session on the machine onto the unverified build. That rationale holds for
an ACTIVE worktree with candidate hook code. It does not hold for a dormant
worktree resumed weeks later, where there is no candidate worth verifying and
the pin only costs a working session.

Scale: every worktree pins its own binary, and any schema or enum change in main
invalidates every un-rebuilt one. There are 137 worktrees; each dormant since
before E-1659 will present exactly this way the moment it is resumed.

E-1662 already ruled that a MISSING worktree binary must fail loudly rather than
silently fall back to the global. This is its sibling: the binary is present and
stale, and "loudly" means stderr nobody sees.

**Do:** route hook failures to `session monitor`, the same destination Fix 3
uses. A hook that cannot start is strictly more serious than a triage child that
dies, because the session then runs untracked for its whole life.

Consider additionally, as a smaller and separate judgment for the implementer to
raise rather than decide: whether a worktree binary that fails its integrity
check should fall back to the global binary with a visible warning, given that
E-1662's no-silent-fallback rule was written about a MISSING binary, not a stale
one, and the failure modes differ.

## Fix 4 — sweep interval

`triagejob`'s `interval` constant is 15 minutes. Not specified by Mike.

Correction to an earlier claim: interval does NOT trade against model spend. The
sweep selects `untriaged` rows first, so an empty queue costs one query; spend is
proportional to tasks filed, not to polling frequency.

**Do:** 5 minutes. Not 1 — with many `session monitor` instances live, tighter
polling buys latency that Fix 2's per-task claim should be providing instead.

## Fix 5 — the reset message offers an undo instead of naming a cost

In `task_cmd`'s update path, the E-1845 auto-untriage note (E-1845's code,
folded in here because it is the same user-visible symptom) prints:

    E-NNNN was 'ready'; description changed → status set to untriaged (the
    description is the spec that triage and approval were judged against; pass
    --keep-status to suppress for a typo/formatting-only edit).

The status render already shows `Status: ready -> untriaged`. The trailing
`pass --keep-status to suppress` reads as an undo offered after the fact, which
invites an agent to relay a completed, correct transition to the user as a
decision to accept. Observed four times in one session.

Do NOT simply delete the clause. `--keep-status` is a spend control, not a
status convenience: every re-triage is a model call, and a filer who already
knows the edit was cosmetic should skip it. Reframe so the decision it offers is
about cost rather than about whether the status was right:

    → untriaged; re-triage will run (one model call). Pass --keep-status on a
    typo- or formatting-only edit to skip it.

**Do:** reframe along those lines and keep the "why" short.

## Why one task, not five

They share a root: a filing (or a reset) that cannot self-resolve becomes a state
someone has to narrate. Fixes 1 and 4 are why it does not self-resolve, 2 is the
race that unblocking 1 exposes, 3 is why nobody can see when it silently failed,
and 5 is what turns the residue into a question for the user. Fixing only the
message leaves the latency; fixing only the latency leaves the message inviting
undo offers on the paths where triage legitimately cannot run.

## Explicitly out of scope

The justfile's `verify` recipe runs main's Python, not the worktree's, so a
Python-side change is verified against landed code while a Go-side change is
verified against candidate. Real asymmetry, but Mike has ruled it WONTFIX: the
fix is complex and Python is slated for a port to Go, so fixing it in Python
only delays the port.

## Naming

`unsettled`, not `unlanded`. ED-1540 defines unsettled as the union (modified OR
unlanded); `unlanded` names only one of the two sub-states and would be actively
wrong for a worktree that is unsettled purely because of uncommitted changes.
Under `task` (4 chars) as requested, and it pairs with the existing `task landed`.

## The predicate already exists -- explain it, don't reimplement it

`taskWorktreeDirty` (internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go:334) is what drives the ◆:

  1. `git -C <wt> status --porcelain` non-empty            -> modified
  2. else `git -C <wt> rev-list main..HEAD --count` > 0    -> unlanded
  3. no worktree, or any git error                         -> settled (fail-open)

It considers neither remote state nor the `task_landings` rows. The new command
must report these exact signals so the marker and its explanation cannot
disagree. Build it as a diagnostic over that predicate, not a second copy.

`AnnotateSessionStatusDirty` (reap_worktrees.go:316) is the fan-out; the reaper
inverts the same two signals at reap_worktrees.go:188-207 ("never reap unsettled").

## Reuse

- `internal/monitor/worktree_anomalies.go` -- finer-grained probes
  (`WorktreeAnomaliesAt`, line 91) already split user dirt from auto-managed via
  `AutoManagedStatusGlobs` (line 37). Read `.endless/plans/E-1758.md` before
  touching the anomaly core.
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py:637` `_git_status_partition` -- returns
  (auto_commit_files, user_work_files); the Python mirror of the same split.
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py:783` `_guard_dirty_worktree` -- land-time refusal
  with separate messages for auto-managed vs user dirt; same message shapes apply.

## Where the code goes

- Register in `src/endless/cli.py` immediately after `task_landed` (~line 1393),
  same decorator set (`item_id` optional TASK_ID, --project/--all/--limit/--llm/
  --json) and the same lazy `from endless.task_cmd import ...` inside the body.
- Implement `unsettled_list` / `unsettled_item` in `src/endless/task_cmd.py`
  alongside `landed_list` (line 1551) / `landed_item` (line 1635); mirror its
  three output modes (json / llm / human table).

## Sequencing risk

E-1825 ("Replace union-sense 'dirty' with 'unsettled'") is `unverified` and
renames exactly these identifiers across exactly these files. Either sequence
this after E-1825 lands or expect to touch the same symbols.

# Route closed tasks to ⇥ instead of ⁇

## Why

Under `endless session status --all`, an ordinary done task renders with `⁇` — the glyph
`classify()` reserves for "a status slipped through unhandled" — and the legend then
advertises `⁇ unknown` for a perfectly normal row. `declined` and `obsolete` tasks never
land, so they hit this **always**; so does anything confirmed/assumed whose work never went
through `worktree land`.

The cost is not cosmetic: `⁇` is load-bearing as a diagnostic. Firing it on the most ordinary
rows in the ledger means a genuinely unhandled status would be invisible in the noise.

See this task's `--analysis` for the reproduction and the full derivation.

## Design (settled — do not re-litigate)

**New action `actDone`, glyph `⇥` (U+21E5 RIGHTWARDS ARROW TO BAR), label `closed`.**
Measured at display width 1 with `go-runewidth`, same as every other glyph in the table, so
the fixed 13-column prefix and its alignment are unaffected. "Arrow to bar" reads as a
terminus, which is what a terminal status is, and it is visually distinct from `▶ do` and
`↩ from`.

**Column 1 stays a verb column.** `✓` was considered and rejected: the phase column (column 4)
already renders `✓` for every terminal status, so `✓` in column 1 would state the same fact
twice. Blank was also considered and rejected — a row with no glyph reads as a rendering
failure rather than a classification.

**`⏚` wins over `⇥`.** A row that is both landed and terminal renders `⏚ landed`. This needs
NO reordering: `classify()` already checks `r.Landed` before the status switch, so adding the
terminal case to the switch delivers this for free. `⇥` therefore appears only on a closed
task whose work never merged — which is the informative case. Pin it with a test so a future
refactor cannot silently swap the precedence.

**Decorations still win over both.** `IsFocal`/`IsParent`/`IsFrom`/`InFlight` are checked
first, so a done parent keeps `↑`. Unchanged; just make sure the new cases do not disturb it.

**Enum position: append `actDone` AFTER `actUnknown`.** Enum order is both legend order and
sort rank (`sortRows` ranks on the enum), so appending leaves every existing rank untouched —
the same trick E-1750 used when it added `actUnknown`. The resulting order is deliberate:
closed rows sort last under `--all`, below the `⁇` anomaly rows, which is right — an
unhandled status deserves more prominence than a finished task.

**Legend reads `⇥ closed` AND keeps `✓ done`.** They are not redundant: `✓` is the phase-column
marker and still appears on *decorated* done rows (a focal, parent, or landed task can be
terminal), where column 1 shows `●`/`↑`/`⏚` rather than `⇥`. Two entries, deliberately.

## Change

All of it is in `internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go` (the action enum is not consumed
anywhere else — `tree.go` takes a separate render path):

1. Add `actDone` to the `action` const block, after `actUnknown`, with a comment explaining
   the append-don't-insert rule and the `⏚`-wins precedence.
2. Add `actDone: {"⇥", "closed"}` to `actionMeta`. `buildLegend` iterates `actionMeta` by
   index, so the legend picks it up with no further change.
3. In `classify()`'s status switch, route terminal statuses to `actDone` by calling the
   existing `isTerminal(r.Status)` helper — do NOT re-list the five statuses inline, or the
   list and `isTerminal` will drift. A `switch` case cannot call a function, so this goes in
   as an `if isTerminal(r.Status) { return actDone }` immediately before the `switch r.Status`
   (after the `r.Landed` check, which must keep winning).

Adjacent, trivial, same change: `internal/monitor/session_status.go:36` still documents
`Landed` as routing "a landed non-terminal task to the catch-all ⁇ bucket". That has been
wrong since E-1750 split `⁇` into `⏚ landed` + `⁇ unknown`; `classify()` returns `actLanded`.
Fix the comment.

## Explicitly out of scope

`TestClassify` pins `Status: "blocked"` as its "unrecognized status is unknown" case, while
the guide's status table documents `blocked` as a real status (and the lifecycle diagram says
blocking is a relation, not a state). That contradiction is a separate question about whether
the status exists at all — it is NOT a terminal status and does not belong in this change.
Leave the test case as-is. Captured in this task's `--analysis` under Decisions #2; do not
file a new task for it without asking.

## Verify

Add `tests/tasks/e-1871-verify.sh`, modeled on `tests/tasks/e-1707-verify.sh` (same harness:
build → the rule's own unit tests as a fail-fast gate → full suites → end-to-end against a
seeded temp DB). Fold this task's tests into that one script; hand the user exactly one
command.

Unit tests in `internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status_test.go`:

- `TestClassify`: each of the five terminal statuses (`confirmed`, `assumed`, `declined`,
  `obsolete`, `completed`) → `actDone`.
- `TestClassify`: terminal + `Landed: true` → `actLanded` (⏚ wins — the precedence pin).
- `TestClassify`: terminal + `IsFocal` → `actThis`, terminal + `IsParent` → `actParent`
  (decorations still win).
- `TestClassify`: no terminal status yields `actUnknown` any more.
- `TestActionIcons`: `actDone` → `⇥`, and `displayWidth("⇥") == 1`.
- `TestBuildLegend`: an undecorated terminal, unlanded row yields BOTH `⇥ closed` and
  `✓ done`, and NOT `⁇ unknown`; a terminal *landed* row yields `⏚ landed` + `✓ done` and
  NOT `⇥ closed`.
- `TestSortRows`: a closed row sorts after an `actUnknown` row and after every open row.

End-to-end through the worktree binary, against a temp DB seeded from
`internal/schema/schema.sql` (see e-1707-verify.sh §4 for the exact fixture pattern —
an epic with children, rendered with `--task <epic> --all`, plus a `task_landings` row to
drive the landed case; note the column is `merge_commit_sha`, not `landed_sha`):

- a `confirmed` child with no landing renders `⇥`, and `⁇` appears nowhere in the output;
- a `confirmed` child WITH a `task_landings` row still renders `⏚`;
- a `declined` and an `obsolete` child both render `⇥`;
- the legend line contains `⇥ closed` and `✓ done` and not `⁇ unknown`;
- the id column does not shift (glyph is width 1).

Run the project-wide regression before handing off: `just build`, `just test-go`, `just test`,
`just guide-check`.
fields.analysis:
## Symptom

In `endless session status --all`, an ordinary done task renders with the ⁇ glyph, and the
legend then advertises "⁇ unknown". ⁇ is the renderer's should-never-happen marker — the
comment on `actUnknown` says its appearance "flags an unhandled status slipping through" —
so it reads as a bug in the tool on a row that is in fact perfectly normal.

## Reproduce

Seed an epic with done children (one landed, one not) and render with `--all`:

```
● this  ⏚ landed  ⁇ unknown  ✓ done
● T E-900  1 the epic I am on
⏚ T E-905  ✓ child: confirmed AND landed
⏚ T E-907  1 child: ready AND landed
⁇ T E-901  ✓ child: confirmed, never landed
⁇ T E-902  ✓ child: declined
```

E-901 and E-902 are unremarkable — one confirmed, one declined — but both get the
"something is wrong here" glyph.

## Why

`classify()` (internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go) switches on status and has NO
case for any of the five terminal statuses — `confirmed`, `assumed`, `declined`, `obsolete`,
`completed`. They fall through to `default:` → `actUnknown` (⁇).

A row hits this whenever ALL of these hold:
  - status is terminal, AND
  - it is not focal / parent / from / in-flight (those decorations are checked first and win), AND
  - it has no `task_landings` row (a landed task is caught one branch earlier → `actLanded` ⏚).

Terminal rows are filtered out of the view unless `--all` is passed, which is why this stays
hidden day to day. But under `--all` the affected set is not marginal:
  - `declined` and `obsolete` tasks never land by definition, so they are ALWAYS ⁇;
  - so is anything confirmed/assumed whose work never went through `worktree land`.

## Why it matters

⁇ is load-bearing as a diagnostic: it is supposed to mean "classify() met a status it does
not know about." Firing it on the most ordinary rows in the ledger destroys that signal —
a genuinely unhandled status would now be invisible in the noise.

## Decisions the fix needs

1. What should a terminal, non-landed row render as? Options: its own action + glyph
   (e.g. ✓/done, distinct from ⏚ landed), or fold into `actLanded` (wrong — "landed" and
   "done" are not the same claim, and ⏚ would then lie about a declined task), or a new
   `actDone`. Needs a call.
2. Whether `blocked` belongs in the same cleanup. `TestClassify` currently pins
   `Status: "blocked"` as the "unrecognized status is unknown" case, yet `blocked` is a
   documented status in the guide's status table — so the test encodes the same gap.
3. Sort rank: wherever the new action lands in the `action` enum determines where done rows
   sort under `--all` (`sortRows` ranks on the enum). Today they sort last, as ⁇.

## Adjacent (same change, trivial)

internal/monitor/session_status.go:36 still documents `Landed` as routing "a landed
non-terminal task to the catch-all ⁇ bucket". That has been wrong since E-1750 split ⁇ into
⏚ landed + ⁇ unknown; classify() returns `actLanded`. Fix the comment while in here.

## Provenance

Found while reproducing E-1707 (a non-focal `completed` + ◆ row rendered `⁇ T◆E-NNN ✓ …`),
and deliberately fenced out of it — E-1707 changed only dim/bold, never classification.
No test covers this: `TestClassify` has no terminal-status case, and `TestBuildLegend`'s
terminal case sets `IsFocal`, so it exits classify() at the first decoration and never
reaches the switch.

# E-1872 — Document the guide's memory-only conventions in one pass

Consolidates E-1873, E-1874, E-1875 and E-1885 (all obsoleted into this task)
and adds the task-proliferation rule.

Items 1–5 are each a convention a session is expected to follow that appears
nowhere in `endless guide`, so it silently breaks for a fresh session — the same
class of gap E-1870 fixed for the commit step. Item 6 is the inverse: a claim the
guide *does* make about `land` that is false. All six are edits to `docs/guide/`,
so they are **one** review, not six.

## The gaps

### 1. Commit-message convention

Branch commits ride into `main` via `worktree land`, and git history's de-facto
form is `E-<id>: <verb-first summary>` (e.g. `b6dd933e`, `fd28a75d`). Nothing in
the guide states it, so every session invents its own subject line.

**Where:** `orchestration.md`, in the "Committing your work" section E-1870 added.

### 2. Do not land or drop without asking

Every handoff template carries "Don't run `endless worktree land`/`drop` without
asking." The guide's "Landing the work" section says the opposite by omission:
"When the task is verified (or you're using `assume`): `endless worktree land
<id>`." The only trace in the guide is `orchestration.md:284` — a sentence
*describing what the handoff template carries*, not a rule a session reading the
Landing section would ever see. A session that re-reads the guide after a context
compaction will land unasked.

**Where:** `orchestration.md`, "Landing the work" — as a rule, not a description
of a template.

### 3. File-don't-fix for drive-by discoveries (`--cleans-up`)

Exists only as `orchestration.md:284` and a bare flag mention in `tasks.md:85`'s
comment block. There is no prose rule, so a session working from the guide alone
fixes drive-bys inline and inflates the diff.

**Where:** `tasks.md`, alongside the relation flags.

### 4. `FULL STATUS` escape hatch

Lives only in `internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/_close.tmpl`: the user
typing `FULL STATUS` licenses **one** unconstrained response, not a sticky mode.
Absent from `docs/guide/` entirely, so a session whose context is compacted
either ignores the keyword or misreads it as a mode switch.

**Where:** `tasks.md`, alongside "Reporting to your user".

### 5. Lean toward FEWER tasks — user directive, 2026-08-04

When filing discovered work, prefer **one** task over several whenever one is
reasonable.

Every filed task costs the user review, prioritization, and scheduling attention.
Five tasks cost roughly **3x** the attention of one task covering the same
ground. Endless exists to **save** the user time, not to manufacture busy work —
for this user or for any downstream Endless user.

Split into separate tasks only when the items genuinely need different reviewers,
different decisions, or different land timing. Same file + same kind of edit +
same reviewer = one task.

This session's own E-1872..E-1875 — four near-identical "document X in the guide"
items — is the anti-pattern. Folding them into this one task is the pattern.

**Where:** `tasks.md`, in the section covering `task add` / filing discovered
work. This one is load-bearing enough to state as a rule with the cost rationale
attached, not a passing aside — an agent that does not know *why* will re-split.

### 6. `land` does not remove the worktree (absorbed from E-1885)

`orchestration.md`'s "Landing the work" step 4 says `land` "Removes the
worktree." It never has: `land_worktree()` records the landing and leaves the
directory and branch in place, and the E-1337 reaper deletes them once they pass
`worktree_ttl` (`.endless/config.json`, default 14d). `index.md` already
described the true behavior, so the two guide pages contradicted each other —
and the false one sits in the same step-list a session reads before landing.

Retention is also what makes re-landing a follow-up commit work, which the
corrected step should say.

**Where:** `orchestration.md`, "Landing the work" — the same section item 2
edits, hence the same review and the same land.

Filed separately as E-1885 during implementation, then folded back in here on the
user's instruction: same file, same section, same reviewer — the rule item 5
documents. E-1885 is `obsolete`, replaced by this task.

## Verification

`tests/tasks/e-1872-verify.sh` — for each of the six, assert the rule is present
in the rendered `endless guide <section>` output (not merely on disk), and that
the `land`-without-asking rule sits inside the "Landing the work" section rather
than in the handoff-template description. For item 6, assert the section carries
the retention wording and no longer carries "Removes the worktree.", and pin both
to the source they describe (`worktree_cmd.py`'s "Worktree dir and branch stay",
`cli.py`'s "default 14d"). Fold in `tests/test_guide_map.py` and `just
guide-check` as the fail-fast first check.

# E-2095 — Plan

Make it visible whether a task's work has reached the project's default branch,
and whether its record is still authoritative. Four parts, one problem: a reader cannot see the facts that
decide whether to trust a row.

## Scope

**In:** parts 1, 2, 4, 5 of the analysis, plus a data-repair pass (§6).

**Out:** part 3 (record supersession automatically when an excision deletes
another task's landed files). It is blocked on a recording change that does not
exist: `task_landings` stores a merge SHA but no base, so a landing's commit
range cannot be reconstructed, and `task_files` stopped recording 2026-07-11.
Its full spec stays in this task's `--analysis`; file a successor when the
recording change is actually wanted rather than parking a speculative task in
the backlog (ED-1550 rule 1).

**Depends on E-2087**, which has landed. It shipped the content-based probe this
task consumes — do not write a second one.

## Decisions already taken (do not relitigate)

- Landedness is measured by CONTENT, not SHA. E-2087's `unlandedCommits`
  short-circuits on `countRevs` when HEAD is an ancestor of base, and only then
  runs `git range-diff`. Reuse it; never reach for `git cherry`.
- Branch names are DERIVED from the task id, never read from a column. E-2108
  retires `task_landings.branch`; anything here that reads it lands broken.
- The base branch is RESOLVED, never assumed. No surface in this task may write
  the word `main` into a message, a query or a rev-range. Call
  `monitor.DefaultBranch` (Go) or `worktree_cmd._default_base_branch` (Python),
  which E-1940 built for exactly this after two probes hardcoded `main` and
  "exit 128 forever" on any repo that used another name. `unlandedCommits`
  already takes `base` as a parameter, so the probe is clean — the risk is
  reintroducing the bug in the RENDERING, which is where this task lives.
- No date-scoped filter anywhere. An earlier draft proposed excluding tasks
  created before the project's first landing record. That is Endless's own
  biography, not product behaviour, and it would have hidden real unlanded work.
  §2's two sections replace it.
- New verb, not a flag. `task landed --not-on-main` reads as a contradiction.
- Part 4's banner follows E-2097's shipped shape exactly.

---

## 1. `task show` states landedness instead of implying it

Today the `Landed:` line renders only when a `task_landings` row exists, so
"landed before landings were recorded" and "the branch still holds the work"
both render as nothing. Absence is doing work it cannot do.

For a task in a terminal status, always render a landing line, one of:

```
Landed:     2026-08-30 10:16 pm  421726c            (40)
Landed:     never                                   (17)
Landed:     never — 320 unlanded commits            (42)
Landed:     unknown — cannot resolve the base branch  (54)
```

This line is a SUMMARY and must never wrap. It carries neither the branch name
nor the base branch, and the reason is NOT length:

- **The branch name is derivable from the id.** E-2108 (`unverified`, implements
  ED-1587) renames worktree branches to `task/<id>` with no title slug, "so a
  branch name is derivable from the id instead of looked up", and RETIRES
  `task_landings.branch`. Once that lands, printing the branch in a task's own
  detail view repeats the `ID:` line three rows above it. Do not read
  `task_landings.branch` and do not render a branch name here; derive it where
  one is needed. The full breakdown — `Branch:`, `Worktree:`, verdict, and the
  commits themselves — already belongs to `task unsettled <id>`.

  (Length reinforces this but does not decide it. Under today's slug branches
  the long form is 103 characters and wraps; under E-2108's convention it is 68
  and fits. The redundancy argument holds either way, which is why it is the one
  stated here.)
- **The base branch is named once per report, never per row.** `task unsettled`
  already sets the precedent with its `Unlanded — N commit(s) not on <base>`
  section header. §2's report does the same in its header, which is what keeps
  the claim falsifiable without paying for the name on every line.
- **`unlanded` is the load-bearing word** and it is a defined term as of E-2087:
  a commit with no counterpart on the resolved base. It carries "not on the base
  branch" without spelling it, which is why the short form loses no meaning.

`never` stays in BOTH negative cases on purpose, rather than being dropped from
one. It is the VALUE of the field; the clause after the dash is a qualifier on
it. A reader scanning a column of these matches one word to learn the verdict
and only then reads the detail — and the two cases must not look like different
verdicts when they are the same one.

Cost: the third case needs the probe, the first two do not. E-2087's
short-circuit makes the common case a `rev-list --count`; only a branch that
genuinely differs pays for `range-diff`. Do NOT add an opt-in flag to request
the probe — an opt-in probe is one nobody remembers to pass.

Edge cases that must render distinctly rather than collapsing into "clean":

- **No branch** (reaped, or never created). The probe cannot run. Say "no
  landing recorded", never "nothing outstanding".
- **Base branch unresolved.** `DefaultBranch` returns
  `ErrDefaultBranchUnresolved` rather than guessing, because "substituting
  `main` here is exactly the bug this resolver exists to remove". Render that as
  its own state — the landedness of this task is unknown, not clean — and name
  the remedy: set `default_branch` in the project's `.endless/config.json`.
- **Probe failure.** `unlandedCommits` returns a `gitProbeError` naming the git
  command. Surface that, do not swallow it into a clean reading.
- **Uncommitted changes are a different axis** and belong to `task unsettled`.
  This line reports commits only.

## 2. `endless task unlanded`

A sibling verb to `task landed`, sharing one implementation.

**Wiring.** Put the query in `task_cmd.py` beside `landed_list`, and register
two Click commands that differ only in the mode they pass. Bundle the shared
options with a decorator the way `rowcap.limit_options_for` already does — its
own docstring gives the reason: "One factory so the two flags cannot appear on
one command and not another, and so their help text is written once." E-967's
`task_cmd.add_command(task_show, name="detail")` is the precedent for a second
name over one callback. Nothing is duplicated; there is no Click obstacle.

**Two sections, because they need different actions.** Measured 2026-09-06:
109 shipped-terminal tasks have no landing row, 3 have a branch at all, and 1
holds anything main lacks.

- **Unlanded work** — a branch exists and the probe reports commits the base
  branch lacks. Actionable: land it, or reset the branch in place. This is the
  list that should be driven to zero.
- **No landing record** — no branch, or the branch holds nothing. Nothing to
  land; the record is missing. Not actionable by landing.

Rank the first section above the second and label both. Collapsing them into one
count would report ~109 outstanding items when 1 is actionable.

**Help text must contrast with its neighbour.** `task unlanded` and
`task unsettled` sit adjacent and look alike. Each opens by naming the
difference: `unsettled` asks whether a WORKTREE is modified or unlanded;
`unlanded` asks whether a TASK claims to be done while its work has not reached
the base branch.

**Reuse `--project`, `--all`, `--llm`, `--json` and the row cap.** Match
`task landed`'s option set exactly — that is the point of the shared decorator.

## 3. `project status` claim

One attention claim, counting the **first** section only. The second section is
a standing historical count and would become permanent furniture.

```
 ⊘ 3 unlanded (Run: task unlanded)
```

Glyph and one-word label join the legend beside the existing claims. Suppress
the row entirely at zero.

Keep this coupling THIN. `project status` is heading for major revisions in
another session; specify the claim (count, glyph, drill-down verb) and leave the
rendering to that work rather than designing a row about to be replaced.

## 4. The authority banner

`task show`, `decision show` and their siblings lead with a banner when the
record is not straightforwardly authoritative. The status line is already on
screen and is demonstrably not enough — it is read as provenance, not caveat.

**Triggers.** Task: `obsolete`, `declined`, or carrying a `replaced_by` or
`duplicated_by` relation. Decision: `rejected`, `superseded`, or `proposed`.
Current volume: of 1391 tasks, 270 are obsolete/declined, 84 replaced, 3
duplicated; of 179 decisions, 124 accepted, 36 proposed, 18 rejected, 1
superseded. Roughly one record in four triggers, so three in four stay clean and
the banner keeps meaning something.

**Two kinds, named as such.** "Not ever" (obsolete, declined, rejected,
replaced, superseded) and "not yet" (proposed). The wording must distinguish
them; a proposed decision is not a retired one.

**Shape follows E-2097, which has shipped.** Its rule: emit ONE dense line as
both the FIRST and LAST line, identical, not split, so whichever end survives a
`head -N` or `tail -N` is sufficient alone.

**Audience: agent-facing only.** Gate the whole banner on
`agent_help.agent_facing()`, which is `agent_env.present() or _AGENT_VIEW` — an
agent is reading, or a human passed `--agent-view` to see what one sees. Use
that function; do not re-spell the question. E-1966, E-2006 and E-2097 each
folded a separate spelling of it back into one place, and a fourth would undo
that.

A human running `task show` sees NOTHING new. The banner is not a caveat a human
needs — the status line and the `Replaced by:` link are already on screen and a
person reads them as the qualifiers they are. It exists because an agent does
not: it quotes the row as authoritative. So the banner is agent output, and a
human reaches it only by asking, with `--agent-view`, for debugging.

This is stricter than E-2097's split, and deliberately. There, the underlying
message is a REFUSAL that a human must see or the command fails silently, so
only the bracketing is agent-gated. Here there is no underlying message a human
is owed — the banner is additive — so the whole thing is gated.

Machine formats: `--json` carries the fact as a key rather than a repeated line,
since nothing truncates JSON by lines. `--llm` gets the bracketed form.

## 5. Guide

One paragraph next to §1's rendering, in the tasks section: a task status
answers "what did we decide about this work", never "where is the code". Point
at `task unlanded` for the latter, and at `task unsettled` for worktree state.

## 6. Data repair, same session

Fold this in rather than filing it (ED-1550 rule 2). Of the 109 shipped-terminal
tasks with no landing row, **20 have a commit on main attributed to them** and
should carry a landing record; 89 have no identifiable SHA and stay as they are.

Record each with `worktree land <id> --record-only --sha <sha>`.

**Verify every SHA before recording it.** The attribution came from grepping
commit messages, which over-credits: E-1048 was credited to a commit that merely
mentions it in the body while implementing E-1047. The bar is the one E-1150
met — its own description named the commit, and that commit is on main. A SHA
that cannot be verified to that standard is left unrecorded. Writing a
heuristic SHA into the table this report reads is the failure the report exists
to prevent.

This shrinks §2's second section. It does not affect the first.

## Verification

- `task show` on a terminal task with a landing row, without one and without a
  branch, and without one but with a branch holding commits — three distinct
  lines, no case rendering as blank.
- `task show` on a task whose branch is gone, and one whose probe errors —
  neither reads as clean.
- `task unlanded` sections ranked correctly, and `task unlanded --json` /
  `--llm` carrying the same split.
- `task unlanded --help` and `task unsettled --help` each name the other.
- On a repo whose default branch is NOT `main`, every rendering names that
  branch and none reports a false all-clear. `git grep -n '"main"'` over the
  code this task touches returns nothing.
- Banner appears on an obsolete task, a replaced task, a proposed decision, and
  a rejected decision; is absent on an accepted decision and a confirmed task;
  survives both `| head -3` and `| tail -3`.
- After §6, the 20 tasks appear under `task landed` and have left `task
  unlanded`'s second section.

The only trace of the rule in the guide is orchestration.md:284, a sentence *describing what the handoff template carries* — not a rule a session reading the Landing section would see. # E-1898 — liveness is observed, never inferred

## The one-sentence change

Delete the reaper. Give every pane binding an identity that is unique across
tmux server lifetimes, observe liveness into a temp table per unit of work, and
JOIN. No code path may conclude a session is dead by looking at tmux and then
writing that conclusion to the `sessions` table.

## Why the previous plan was replaced

The prior plan guarded the destructive write with an escalating series of gates
(server-uuid gate, peer-server enumeration, ordering guarantees, forced
override). Every gate was an inference about whether the pane set in front of
the process was the right one to judge by, because no row recorded which tmux
server it was bound to. Stacking gates narrows the window; it cannot close it,
and each gate added edge cases and un-mockable tmux tests.

Recording the binding's server identity removes the need for every one of those
gates. This plan is shorter than the one it replaces because the complexity was
compensation for a missing column, not essential difficulty.

## Invariants — these are the acceptance criteria

**I1 — No inferred destructive write.** No code path writes `state='ended'`, or
clears a pane binding, based on an observation of tmux. Only reported facts (a
`SessionEnd` hook) and explicit operator action close a session. There is no
sweep, no reaper, no mass UPDATE.

**I2 — Bounded blast radius.** A failed or incomplete observation may affect at
most the rows it actually observed. `unknown` is NEVER converted to `dead` by
any consumer. An unreachable server costs zero rows.

**I3 — Identity unique across server lifetimes.** A tmux pane id reused by a new
server can never match a binding made against the old one.

**I4 — Tests need no tmux server.** Liveness is a JOIN against a table; tests
seed that table directly. No private tmux servers, no socket enumeration, no
seam counters.

Verification drives each invariant explicitly. I1 and I2 are the ones this task
exists for; a change that satisfies I3 but not I1 has not fixed anything.

## Model

Multiplexer-agnostic. tmux is one populator; cmux and herdr add their own
without touching consumers.

```
process_kinds(id, slug)          -- tmux | pid | ...   (mirrors session_kinds)

processes(                       -- DURABLE identity. A fact, kept forever.
  id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  kind_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES process_kinds(id),
  server_uuid   TEXT,            -- tmux @server_uuid; NULL for kind=pid
  address       TEXT NOT NULL,   -- tmux pane id '%414'; or the pid as text
  first_seen_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  last_seen_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE(kind_id, server_uuid, address)
)

sessions.process_id -> processes.id     -- replaces sessions.process

TEMP live_processes(kind_id, server_uuid, address, command)
TEMP observed_servers(kind_id, server_uuid)   -- which servers we actually reached

UNIQUE(kind_id, ifnull(server_uuid,''), address)   on live_processes
UNIQUE(kind_id, ifnull(server_uuid,''))            on observed_servers
```

`processes` is append-mostly: a row is created the first time a session binds to
an address on a server, and is never deleted by observation. A tmux restart
mints a new `@server_uuid`, therefore a new `processes` row, therefore I3 holds
structurally — not by a guard that could be wrong.

## The identity rule applies to the OBSERVATION tables too

Added 2026-08-13, after this shipped without it.

`processes_identity` indexes (kind_id, ifnull(server_uuid,''), address), and the
plan explains why the ifnull() is required: SQLite treats every NULL as
distinct, so a plain UNIQUE would not bind. That reasoning was written down for
the durable table and then not applied to the observation tables one section
below, which expressed the same identity and enforced nothing.

It was not theoretical. `tmux list-panes -a` lists a LINKED window's panes once
per tmux session the window is linked into — measured on the real machine hours
after land, 442 rows for 245 distinct panes, every pane exactly twice. Since
session_liveness LEFT JOINs live_processes, a pane recorded N times multiplied
its session's row N times: `list-live` returned 114 rows for 57 sessions, and
`esu` refused with "Multiple sibling Claude panes in this window", blocking
worktree entry by session entirely.

Both observation tables now carry the same expression-based unique index as the
durable one, and the snapshot inserts with OR IGNORE — a repeat within one
snapshot is the same observation, not a conflict. `observed_servers` gets it too
even though only one socket answers @server_uuid today: it had the identical
gap and merely happened not to be exercised.

**The rule, stated once so it is not re-derived per table:** a table that
expresses this identity enforces it, durable or temporary.

## Liveness — three-valued, derived at read

```sql
CASE
  WHEN o.server_uuid IS NULL  THEN 'unknown'  -- server not reached
  WHEN l.address IS NULL      THEN 'dead'     -- reached; address absent
  ELSE                             'live'
END
FROM sessions s
JOIN processes p             ON p.id = s.process_id
LEFT JOIN observed_servers o USING (kind_id, server_uuid)
LEFT JOIN live_processes  l  USING (kind_id, server_uuid, address)
```

Expose as a view (`session_liveness`) so no consumer re-derives it.

Liveness is now PURELY OBSERVATIONAL: "is this address present on a server we
actually reached?" There is no remaining inference in it. That is the property
that makes I1 and I2 checkable rather than argued.

`unknown` is the safe branch: render last-known, condemn nothing. Per I2, no
consumer may map it to `dead`. The site that needs care is the spawn/claim
ownership guard — under `unknown` it must assume STILL OWNED and refuse. A
wrong refusal is an annoyance; the inverse steals a live worktree.

### Why the shell test is NOT part of liveness

The previous plan's death test was "address absent OR the pane runs a known
shell", to catch a killed harness whose pane survives. It is dropped from
liveness, because it is an inference and it can be wrong about a LIVE session:

- Verified 2026-08-09: a live Claude pane reports its version string
  (`2.1.220`) as `pane_current_command`, even mid-Bash-tool-call. So it does
  not collide with the shell set during normal operation.
- But **Ctrl+Z** puts the shell back in the foreground. A suspended-but-alive
  Claude session's pane reports `zsh`. Under the shell test that session reads
  `dead`, which drops its status line to the placeholder and — the part that
  matters — lets the spawn/claim ownership guard treat its task as free and
  hand the worktree to another session.

Cost of dropping it: a harness killed with its pane still open (SIGKILL, no
SessionEnd) leaves a stale-`live` row until the pane closes. That is a wrong
read in the SAFE direction — a refusal, never a theft — and E-1807's actual
case had a dead pane, which address-absence still catches.

`live_processes.command` is still collected, but is used ONLY for the cosmetic
"pane is running Claude but has no session row" status-line hint. An inference
is acceptable for a hint that misleads nobody and owns nothing; it is not
acceptable for liveness. That line is the rule, and the code must not blur it.

## Snapshot population

Refresh at the start of each **unit of work** — a CLI/hook invocation, an HTTP
request, a monitor repaint — inside the transaction that reads it, so a single
statement never sees two different observations.

For tmux: list sockets in `dirname $(tmux display-message -p '#{socket_path}')`;
for each, read `@server_uuid` and, when present, one
`tmux -S <sock> list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_current_command} #{pane_pid}'`.
Each successfully-read server contributes a row to `observed_servers`.

Enumeration stays, but is no longer load-bearing for safety: a server we cannot
reach (`tmux -S` outside the socket dir, relocated `TMUX_TMPDIR`) yields
`unknown` for its rows, not a verdict. This is the entire difference from the
previous plan's peer-enumeration gate, which had to be complete to be safe.

## Binding: where server_uuid comes from

The hook runs inside the pane. It reads `@server_uuid`; if absent it generates
and stamps one, exactly as `tmux init` does. Every binding therefore carries a
real server identity, and the previous plan's "refuse when uninitialized" gate
is unnecessary — identity is always present rather than sometimes checked.

## Deleted

- `monitor.ReapDeadTmuxPanes` and `internal/monitor/reap.go`, including the
  `len(alive) == 0` mass-UPDATE that ended every tmux row in one statement.
- `runInit`'s `runReset(nil)` call — the documented trigger for the 37-row batch.
- `endless tmux reset` ENTIRELY — the Go verb (`internal/tmuxcmd/reset.go`,
  its `tmux.go` dispatch), the Python wrappers (`cli.py` `tmux_reset`,
  `tmux_cmd.py` `run_reset`), the remedy line in `task_cmd.py:3304` that tells
  users to run it, and the assertion on that line in
  `tests/test_check_task_ownership.py:91`. No read-only replacement is
  introduced: `endless session list` and `endless sql` already read the view,
  and the ownership guard can no longer refuse over a gone pane — the snapshot
  shows it gone — so the remedy it advertised has nothing left to remedy.
- `TouchSession`'s collision invalidation. A reused pane is a different
  `processes` row, so the pane-reuse case cannot arise; a genuine same-server
  collision leaves both rows and the reader orders by `last_activity`.
- From the previous plan: D1, D2, D5, D6, D9 and their tests. D3's insight is
  kept as a read-time classifier; D7 and D8 survive as below.

## Kept from the previous plan

- **D7** — `runInit` no longer reaps (now: there is nothing to reap).
- **D8** — `runStatusLine` records a fault instead of silently rendering the
  placeholder on error. One correction to that decision: because
  `faults.Bind` is wired to `monitor.DB` (main.go:144) and `faults.Record`
  swallows its own DB failure by contract, this covers the non-DB fail-closed
  exits, not all of them. Worth doing; do not claim full coverage.
- The **ledger-safety assertion** in the verify suite.

## Migration

1. Create `process_kinds`, `processes`, add `sessions.process_id`.
2. Backfill, in TWO steps.

   2a. One `processes` row per distinct non-null `sessions.process`, with
   `server_uuid = NULL` (the binding server is not knowable retroactively) and
   `kind` derived from the string shape (`%N` -> tmux, `pid:N` -> pid).

   2b. ADOPT what is observable: for every pane live on the running tmux
   server, repoint the non-ended session bound to that address onto that
   server (`monitor.AdoptPaneBindings`).

   **Step 2b was missing from the first cut, and its absence took the board
   down on 2026-08-10.** This plan claimed the NULL-server rows would
   "self-heal on the session's next hook" and that live sessions would
   "recover within seconds without any repair verb". That is true only for
   sessions that FIRE hooks. An idle window fires none, and idle is the normal
   state, so every pre-existing session became unresolvable at once and STAYED
   unresolvable — the pane lookup matches on (current server uuid, address),
   and a NULL-server row matches no server at all. Measured on the real ledger
   when it bit: 64 sessions bound, 1 healed (the one firing hooks), 63 dark.

   Adoption is an observation, not a repair heuristic: a pane in the live set
   exists on the named server NOW. Two guards keep it honest — it refuses any
   address claimed by more than one non-ended session (that ambiguity is
   exactly what E-1898 exists to stop resolving by guesswork), and it creates
   a NEW row rather than stamping a server onto the shared NULL-server record,
   which the backfill deduplicates by address and which therefore carries
   history from every server that ever issued that pane.

   Panes that are not live, and every binding when no tmux server is
   reachable, keep `server_uuid` NULL and read `unknown` — never `dead`. On
   the measured ledger that left exactly one row: a genuine leftover from a
   dead server, which is precisely the case where `unknown` is the true
   answer. No repair verb is needed, but the reason is adoption, not healing.
3. Convert the ~35 call sites comparing `process` to a raw pane id. The type
   changes, so a missed site is a COMPILE ERROR — the property that made this
   safe to do where string-encoding `<uuid>:<pane>` would not have been.
4. Drop `sessions.process`.

`channels` is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE and keeps its string key; see E-1936.
It becomes the last consumer of the old key, deliberately, pending that
brainstorm's decision on whether it should exist at all.

## Tests — `tests/tasks/e-1898-verify.sh`

**Layer A — liveness truth table (FAIL-FAST, pure SQL fixtures, no tmux).**
Includes duplicate-observation coverage: the same address seeded twice must
still yield one row per session, and likewise a repeated server.

These INSERT directly rather than going through `SetTestTmuxObservation`, and
that is load-bearing. The seam takes a `map[string]string` of address ->
command, which cannot hold one address twice, so every fixture built on it was
structurally incapable of reproducing the defect. The seam that makes liveness
exhaustively testable without tmux is the same seam that hid this. A test
written through it would restate the blind spot instead of closing it.

Seed `processes`, `sessions`, `live_processes`, `observed_servers` directly and
assert every cell: server unobserved -> `unknown`; observed + address present ->
`live`; observed + address absent -> `dead`. Same pane id under two different
`server_uuid`s resolves independently (I3). Assert a pane running a shell reads
`live` while its session row stands — pinning that the shell inference is NOT in
the liveness path and cannot be reintroduced without failing this test.

**Layer B — invariants as tests, not as prose.**
- **I1:** grep the tree for any write of `state='ended'` or a binding clear
  outside the SessionEnd path; assert zero. Then drive a full hook cycle against
  an EMPTY `live_processes` (the exact 2026-08-05 shape: observer sees nothing)
  and assert **zero rows changed**. This is the regression test for the incident.
- **I2:** with `observed_servers` empty, assert no row reads `dead` and the
  ownership guard refuses rather than freeing.
- **I4:** the whole of A and B runs with `tmux` absent from `$PATH`.

**Layer C — one E2E** against a private tmux server (`-f /dev/null`, throwaway
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) proving the populator fills the snapshot from a real server.
Exactly one, because the logic under test is now SQL, not tmux plumbing.

**Layer D — project-wide regression:** `go test ./...`, `just test`, `just build`.

**Ledger-safety assertion (mandatory).** Count non-ended sessions holding a
binding in the REAL database before and after the suite; they must be equal.

## Out of scope

- `channels` and the `endless-channel` MCP server (E-1936).
- Idle-timeout / session-duration truthfulness. Positive observation covers
  "Claude died, pane lives" without inferring death from silence.
- Non-tmux (`pid:`) liveness. The model has a slot for it; no populator ships here.
- Repairing rows damaged on 2026-08-05. Repaired by hand; migration step 2
  heals the rest on the next hook.

# Analysis — the dead-pane reaper can destroy live pane bindings project-wide

## Two defects, both required for the damage

### 1. The reaper trusts an ambient tmux view it never validates

`monitor.ReapDeadTmuxPanes` (internal/monitor/reap.go) decides liveness with:

    exec.Command("tmux", "list-panes", "-a", "-F", "#{pane_id}")

It inherits whatever `$TMUX` the calling process has. Any caller running under a
DIFFERENT tmux server — a private `tmux -L <socket>` server started by a test or
a verify script — sees only that server's panes. Every real pane then looks dead
and the whole project is reaped. There is no check that the observed pane set is
plausible for the rows about to be ended.

The `len(alive) == 0` branch is the sharpest edge: it nulls `process` for EVERY
non-ended tmux-format row in the project in one statement. Its comment treats an
empty pane set as proof that everything is dead; it is equally consistent with
"I am looking at the wrong server."

`internal/tmuxcmd/reset.go` already guards its own entry point (refuses when
`$TMUX` is empty, calling it "a footgun"). The SessionStart caller in
`internal/hookcmd/claude.go` has no such guard, and that is the one that fires
constantly.

### 2. TouchSession cannot undo it

    process = COALESCE(NULLIF(?, ''), process)
    state   = CASE WHEN sessions.state = 'ended' THEN 'needs_input' ELSE state END

A later hook firing with an EMPTY `TMUX_PANE` flips the row back to
`needs_input` but leaves `process` NULL. The row now reads as alive and resolves
to nothing, permanently — pane lookup keys on `process`. Only a hook that fires
WITH a pane can heal it, which is why sessions actively running tools recovered
and idle ones did not.

## Observed damage (2026-08-05)

- 27 live Claude panes had their session row at `state='ended'`, `process` NULL,
  while the pane was demonstrably alive and working in that task's worktree.
- 59 of 61 tmux windows rendered a blank status line simultaneously.
- Only 3 sessions were intact — exactly the ones firing hooks with `TMUX_PANE`
  set at the time.
- Reap batches are visible in the ledger by minute, including one batch of 37.

The blank bar is invisible by construction: `runStatusLine` maps every failure
to the same placeholder (E-1895), so this destroyed state for hours with no
diagnostic anywhere.

## Absorbed from E-1895: the failure was invisible by construction

`internal/tmuxcmd/status_line.go` `runStatusLine` maps EVERY error from
`monitor.GetPaneStatus` to `placeholder()` and stays silent on stderr:

    status, err := monitor.GetPaneStatus(pane)
    if err != nil {
        // Real error (DB unreachable, etc.). Render placeholder; stay
        // silent on stderr to avoid log spam during interactive use.
        fmt.Print(placeholder())
        return
    }

`monitor.DB()` alone has ~7 fail-closed exits behind that single `err` (the
schema apply, five enum VerifyIntegrity gates, guardWorktreeDBContext). All of
them render as the same dim dot as "this pane has no Endless context", and write
nothing anywhere. That is why the 2026-08-05 incident destroyed state for hours
with no diagnostic, and why three separate hypotheses had to be eliminated
experimentally before the cause was found.

The stderr silence is CORRECT and must stay: the bar re-execs this binary once
per pane every `status-interval` (2s across ~14 panes), so logging would be a
firehose painted over a live TUI. `faults.Record` is the right shape instead —
it dedupes an open incident in place, so a bar blanking every 2s across every
pane raises ONE incident. `cmd/endless-go/main.go` already calls `faults.Bind`
for every subcommand, so the recorder is available with no new wiring.

Scope note: this is NOT E-1884 (converting 42 `log.Printf` sites that write too
noisily). This is the inverse — a site that writes nothing when it should.

## Directions (not locked — this needs a plan)

- Refuse to reap on an implausible pane set: if `alive` is empty, or disjoint
  from every stored `process` for the project, treat it as "wrong server" and
  no-op rather than reaping.
- Pin the server identity: record which tmux server a session belongs to
  (socket path) and only reap rows for that server.
- Make the damage recoverable: reviving `ended` to `needs_input` while leaving
  `process` NULL should not be possible — either restore both or neither.
- Consider whether SessionStart is the right trigger at all, given it fires from
  contexts whose `$TMUX` is not the user's server.


# Absorbed tasks (E-1642, E-1468, E-1408)

This task became the umbrella for session<->pane binding integrity. Three
pre-existing tasks were folded in and marked obsolete; their content is
preserved below so nothing is re-derived.

## From E-1642 — close sessions on idle-timeout instead of mass-end sweeps

Original description: SessionEnd/EndSession rarely fires (the harness is killed,
not cleanly exited), so sessions linger until a later reaper/collision sweep
marks a batch 'ended' at one shared instant. last_activity is bumped far past
real life, durations span days, and duration stops being a usable "real session"
signal. End sessions on last_activity + idle-timeout rather than wall-clock
sweep time.

CORRECTION, from the 2026-08-05 incident: E-1642's plan opens with a "Recon
correction" asserting there is NO reaper and that clustered mass-end timestamps
come from bulk/collision events only. That is wrong. monitor.ReapDeadTmuxPanes
IS a reaper; it is not periodic but fires on EVERY SessionStart
(internal/hookcmd/claude.go:185) and mass-ends by design — the `len(alive) == 0`
branch ends every tmux-format row in the project in a single UPDATE. The batch
of 37 rows sharing one timestamp is that branch, not a bulk event. Any plan
carried forward from E-1642 must be re-read against this.

E-1642's plan as filed, preserved verbatim:

# E-1642 — Close sessions on idle-timeout (there is no reaper today)

**Independent.** · **Layer:** Go (`internal/monitor/session.go`) + a trigger

## Recon correction
There is **NO periodic reaper**. Sessions reach `ended` only via `EndSession` on `SessionEnd`
(`session.go:511-523`, rarely fires — harness is killed, not cleanly exited) or collision-
invalidation (`session.go:280-292`, inert when `process` is empty). So real dead sessions linger
`working`/`idle` indefinitely; the clustered "mass-end" timestamps come from bulk/collision
events, not a reaper. The fix is to **add** truthful idle-timeout ending.

## Why it matters
`duration` is currently a lie (a real session can span days), so it can't signal "the real
session." E-1645's resolver and the dashboard both want reliable `state` + `last_activity`.

## Approach
1. **Idle-timeout sweep:** any session in `working`/`idle`/`needs_input` whose `last_activity` is
   older than a configurable window (e.g. 60-90 min; align with the ~1h bg idle) → mark `ended`
   with end == **`last_activity`, not `now()`** (don't bump the timestamp). `EndSession` today
   updates `last_activity` (511-523) — the idle path must NOT.
2. **Trigger** (no daemon exists): BOTH (a) a cheap project-scoped stale-sweep piggybacked inside
   `TouchSession` (runs every hook event → self-heals during activity), and (b) an explicit
   `endless session sweep [--dry-run]` for manual/cron/tmux use.
3. **Config:** idle window in `.endless/config.json` (go-cfgstore) with a sane default.

## Risks
- Don't end a session legitimately parked on `needs_input` — longer timeout/exemption for it.
- Harness resumes on wake (v2.1.142+); base the decision on `last_activity` heartbeats, not
  wall-clock since spawn, so a machine-sleep gap doesn't end a live session.

## Verification — create a per-task verify script
Create `tests/tasks/e-1642-verify.sh` in the `e-1624-verify.sh` shape (bash, `set -u`, the
`section`/`report_*`/`summary` helpers, `cd` repo root, ensure `go.work`, exit 0/1/2). Drive the
REAL code path via Go tests in `internal/monitor` plus the `endless session sweep` CLI.

The script asserts (named checks):
- `internal/monitor` compiles.
- A Go test drives a `working`/`idle` session whose `last_activity` is older than the timeout and
  asserts it flips to `ended` with end == the **historical** `last_activity` (NOT `now()`).
- A recent (within-timeout) session is left untouched.
- A `needs_input` session honors its longer leniency (not ended at the short timeout).
- `endless session sweep --dry-run` lists **exactly** the stale sessions it would end (seed via
  fresh ids); `internal/monitor` full suite stays green.

Re-runnability (sandbox NOT wiped between runs):
- Derive seeded ids/`session_id`/`short_id` from freshly-allocated ids each run; set
  `last_activity` relative to a computed "now minus N" each run, never a fixed timestamp.
- Capture seeding output; `exit 2` loudly on any setup/seed error (never /dev/null).
- Run the script at least TWICE before declaring it done.

**Verify-handoff — tell the user to verify with (only) this:**
```
esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1642-verify.sh
```




## From E-1468 — collision invalidation ends rows with no liveness check

internal/monitor/session.go collision invalidation sets state='ended' for every
other sessions row sharing the incoming process (pane) string, with no liveness
check. When two Claude session identities share one physical tmux pane (e.g. a
worktree-keyed session and a main-checkout-keyed session during a land run from
main), the live session is falsely marked ended. Repro: E-1459 land run from the
main checkout spawned queue-operation session a27e5710 on pane %203, flipping
live session 510 to ended. Proposed fix: verify the prior occupant is actually
stale (tmux list-panes / last_activity recency / project-dir match) before
invalidating.

Note its description is partly stale: it says "TouchSession upserts never
restore state", but E-1686 has since added the ended -> needs_input revive. The
liveness-check principle still stands, and is the SAME principle the reaper
needs — which is why these belong together.

## From E-1408 — SessionStart must not silently capture an empty TMUX_PANE

The SessionStart hook reads TMUX_PANE via os.Getenv and writes it to the
companion file; PaneID has json:omitempty so an empty value drops out of the
JSON entirely. Downstream, sibling detection never matches and `endless task
bind` fails. Mike's directive on that task: silent degradation is unacceptable —
the hook MUST fail when it cannot capture pane_id, and subsequent hooks should
keep failing until resolved. Evidence then: TMUX_PANE='' in both the Claude env
and the parent shell env despite TMUX being set.

This is the upstream cause of the incident's unrecoverability: TouchSession
writes `process = COALESCE(NULLIF(excluded.process,''), sessions.process)`, so a
hook firing with an empty TMUX_PANE revives `state` while leaving `process`
NULL — the row then reads alive and resolves to nothing, permanently.

## Related, NOT absorbed

E-1395 (unverified) fixed the Python `_tmux_window_pane_ids` running `tmux
list-panes` without `-t`. Same bug class as the reaper's ambient view; precedent
for the fix, no action needed here.

## Post-land defect: every live session is returned twice

Found 2026-08-13, hours after land, when `esu` refused to resolve with
"Multiple sibling Claude panes in this window" listing the SAME pane twice —
identical session id, pane, uuid and worktree. `session-query list-live` returns
114 rows for 57 sessions: every session duplicated exactly 2x.

Root cause is `live_processes`, not the pane bindings this task fixed:

- `tmux list-panes -a` lists a LINKED window's panes once per tmux session the
  window is linked into. Measured here: 442 rows for 245 distinct pane ids.
- `refreshLiveness` inserts one `live_processes` row per returned pane, and that
  temp table has no uniqueness constraint.
- `session_liveness` LEFT JOINs `live_processes` on
  (kind_id, server_uuid, address), so a pane recorded N times multiplies its
  session's row N times — and every consumer of the view inherits it.

Not the servers: only one socket in the dir answers `show-options -gv
@server_uuid`, so `observed_servers` holds a single row. The multiplier is
purely the pane snapshot.

The identity is already stated for the durable table — `processes_identity`
indexes (kind_id, ifnull(server_uuid,''), address) precisely because SQLite
treats each NULL as distinct. The observation table expresses the same identity
and does not enforce it. A pane seen twice in one snapshot is one pane.

Fix direction: give `live_processes` the same expression-based unique index and
insert with OR IGNORE (or dedupe in `parsePaneList`). Worth a regression test
that seeds a duplicate pane and asserts the view still yields one row per
session, since this is invisible until a window happens to be linked.

User-visible impact meanwhile: `esu` cannot auto-resolve a sibling pane at all,
so entering a worktree by session is blocked.

# E-1899 — Remove the unused list tree

A removal checklist, not a design. The only risk in this task is deleting the
wrong `--tree`: there are four flags by that name and two identically-named
glyph maps, and the two flags you must NOT touch are the ones actually in use.

> **Amended during implementation.** Three things landed that this plan did not
> anticipate; each is marked ⊕ below.
>
> 1. A **third bare `tree` reference** in `show_plan` — the sort default —
>    which the site table missed. Mechanical.
> 2. A **doc line** in `docs/guide/tasks.md` advertising the removed flag.
> 3. The **second `status_indicators` map was deleted too**, reversing this
>    plan's "Do NOT touch" directive. It turned out to be dead code. See
>    *Reversal* below; filed and closed as E-1924.

## One renderer, two flags

`epic_cmd.list_epics` is a thin wrapper that forwards `tree=tree` into
`task_cmd.show_plan` with `type_filter="epic"`. So `task list --tree` and
`epic list --tree` share a single implementation — there is ONE branch and ONE
glyph map to delete, not two.

## Remove

| Site | What |
|---|---|
| `cli.py:1225` | the `--tree/as_tree` option on `task list` |
| `cli.py:2521` | the `--tree/as_tree` option on `epic list` |
| `cli.py` (both bodies) | the `tree=as_tree` argument passed onward |
| `epic_cmd.list_epics` | the `tree` parameter and its pass-through to `show_plan` |
| `task_cmd.show_plan` | the `tree` parameter |
| `task_cmd.show_plan` | the `else: # Tree output` branch — the `by_id` / `children_of` / `_render` block, ending at the `_render(None, 1)` call |
| `task_cmd.py` ~:1100 | the `status_indicators` map that opens that branch |
| ⊕ `task_cmd.show_plan` | the sort default `if not tree and not sort_by:` → `if not sort_by:` |
| ⊕ `docs/guide/tasks.md:34` | the `endless task list --tree # hierarchical` line |
| ⊕ `task_cmd.next_tasks` ~:1209 | the second `status_indicators` map — see *Reversal* |

After removal, `show_plan`'s `if not tree: _render_flat_table(rows)` collapses
to an unconditional `_render_flat_table(rows)`; the trailing `click.echo()` and
the `N item(s)` summary below the branch stay.

⊕ The site table above missed a third bare `tree` reference: `show_plan` picked
its ORDER BY with `if not tree and not sort_by: sort_by = "id"`, falling through
to `pi.sort_order` for the tree. Removing the parameter leaves `if not sort_by`.
Flat ordering is unchanged — the flat path always defaulted to id. A `NameError`
on the first `task list` after the branch deletion is what surfaced it.

## ⊕ Reversal — the second glyph map went too

This plan told the implementer to preserve the `status_indicators` map in
`next_tasks` as an unrelated bystander. That was wrong: the map is **dead
code**. It is assigned and never read — `next_tasks` renders through
`_render_flat_table`, which has no glyph column. `grep -n 'indicator'
task_cmd.py` returned only the assignment line.

So the resolution is deletion, not preservation. Adding a glyph column to
`task next` to make the map live would be an unrequested behavior change;
`task next` output is byte-for-byte what it was. Filed as E-1924
(`cleans_up` E-1899), then folded into this task's commit and closed obsolete.

Consequence for the framing at the top of this plan: there were two
identically-named glyph maps and **both** are gone. The "don't delete the wrong
one" hazard is now only about the four `--tree` flags.

## Do NOT touch

- **`session status --tree`** (`cli.py:815`) and **`session monitor --tree`**
  (`cli.py:839`). These are the trees actually in use. They are Go-backed
  (`internal/sessionstatuscmd`), reach the renderer through
  `session_status_resolve`, and share nothing with the list tree but the flag
  name.

## Verification — `tests/tasks/e-1899-verify.sh`

Author the script; it is the deliverable the user runs. Hand back exactly one
command:

```
esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1899-verify.sh
```

Copy the harness shape from `tests/tasks/e-1845-verify.sh` (the `report_pass` /
`report_fail` / `assert_*` / `summary` block and the isolated-fixture setup:
throwaway git repo, temp `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME`, worktree `bin` on
PATH). E-1623 will retrofit these onto a shared harness later; until then match
the current shape rather than inventing a new one.

**A — fail-fast gate.** `uv run pytest tests/ -q` passes. A removal must not
break an unrelated suite, and there is no point running the rest if it did.
Abort the run on failure.

**B — the flags are gone.** `endless task list --tree` and
`endless epic list --tree` both fail as unknown options, and their `--help`
output no longer lists `--tree`.

**C — the flat table is untouched.** `endless task list` and
`endless epic list` still render, and `--status`, `--phase`, `--sort`, `--llm`,
and `--json` all still behave. Seed a small task tree with parents and children
so a regression in the flat renderer would actually show.

**D — the trees that matter still work.** `endless session status --tree` and
`endless session monitor --tree` still render. This is the check that catches
the one dangerous failure mode of this task: deleting the wrong `--tree`. Assert
against real output, not just an exit code.

**E — ⊕ both glyph maps are gone and `task next` is unchanged.** As written this
check asserted that `endless task next` "still renders its status glyphs" —
a false premise: it never rendered them, which is exactly how the map was found
to be dead. Reframed to the guarantee that actually holds: no `status_indicators`
survives in `task_cmd.py`, nothing reads an `indicator`, and `task next` still
renders its header, column heads, rows, `--json` and `--llm` exactly as before.

**F — no dangling references.** Grep the tree for `tree=` and `as_tree` in
`src/endless`; the only survivors should be the two `session_status_resolve`
call sites. Nothing should still pass `tree` to `show_plan` or `list_epics`.

**⊕ G — project-wide regression.** `go test ./...` passes. The Python suite is
already the section-A gate; this is its Go counterpart, run at the end.

## Not in scope

An interactive TUI tree — what is actually wanted instead of this — is a much
larger piece of work and is deliberately unfiled.

## Note for E-1891

The deleted glyph map is the per-row lookup cited in E-1891's plan as the one
place worth measuring for subprocess cost. Landing this first dissolves that
concern rather than answering it. ⊕ Doubly so: both maps are now gone, so
whichever of the two E-1891 meant, there is nothing left to measure.

# Findings — dev-machine resource investigation, 2026-08-06

Triggered by `kernel_task` at 156% and `fseventsd` saturating CPU on the M4 mini
(24 GB RAM, 10 cores, 99-day uptime).

## Measured state

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Swap | **49.2 GB used of 50.2 GB (98%)** |
| Free pages | 3,412 x 16 KB = 55 MB |
| CPU split | 65% sys / 20% user / 15% idle |
| Load average | 44-57 on 10 cores |
| Processes | 841, of which 43 are `claude` |
| tmux panes | 408 across 6 sessions |
| fseventsd CPU | 29,098 min in 100 days (~20% of a core, continuously) |

`pmset -g therm` recorded no thermal warnings, so `kernel_task` is the VM
compressor thrashing, not throttling.

## Worktree / sandbox footprint

- 113 worktrees, 180,117 files, 5.4 GB under `.endless/worktrees`
- **84,303 files (47%) are pure derived output:**
  `.venv` 67,289 - `__pycache__` 15,596 - `bin/` 1,159 - caches 259
- By bytes `bin/` dominates: 70 MB of a 76 MB worktree
- 267 sandboxes, of which **184 are orphaned** (no matching worktree), 228 MB,
  oldest dating to 2026-06-17
- Time Machine backs up all of it (`tmutil isexcluded` reports `[Included]` for
  `~/Projects`, `.endless/worktrees`, `~/.cache`) to a **network SMB share**
  (Synology, 708 GB / 3,846,305 files). Spotlight indexes the same churn
  (`spotlightknowledged.updater` 11.8%, `mds` 5.5%).

## Why we cannot just exclude and reap

A worktree dir is the only home for uncommitted + untracked work. That is
precisely what must survive removal.

## Verified mechanism for making WIP durable

A worktree's `.git` is an 84-byte pointer file; its object database is the
**main checkout's** `.git/objects`. Snapshot without mutating the working tree:

```sh
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp -u)
git add -A                      # honors .gitignore -> skips bin/, .venv/, __pycache__
TREE=$(git write-tree)
COMMIT=$(git commit-tree "$TREE" -p HEAD -m "wip: <name>")
unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
git update-ref refs/wip/<name> "$COMMIT"
```

Three properties, all verified end-to-end in a scratch repo:

1. Objects land in the main checkout's shared store, not the worktree.
2. `refs/wip/*` is outside git's per-worktree ref namespace (only `HEAD`,
   `refs/bisect/*`, `refs/worktree/*` are per-worktree), so the ref is written
   to `<main>/.git/refs/wip/` and survives worktree removal.
3. A ref pins its objects against GC.

Destructive test — after `git worktree remove --force`, `git branch -D`,
`git reflog expire --expire=now --all`, `git gc --prune=now --aggressive`:

```
$ git show refs/wip/e-999:scratch-notes.md
PRECIOUS untracked
```

Both the modified tracked file and the untracked file were recovered.
`git add -A` honoring `.gitignore` was confirmed against this repo's
`.gitignore` (`/bin/` :13, `.venv/` :10, `__pycache__/` :8), so snapshots
capture only the precious source and are kilobytes.

## Time Machine exclusion mechanics (verified)

Two mechanisms with opposite lifetimes:

| Form | Storage | Survives dir deletion | Root |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tmutil addexclusion <path>` | xattr `com.apple.metadata:com_apple_backup_excludeItem` on the dir | **No — dies with the inode** | no |
| `tmutil addexclusion -p <path>` | `SkipPaths` in `com.apple.TimeMachine.plist` | **Yes — accumulates forever** | yes |

Confirmed the sticky (non-`-p`) form leaves `SkipPaths` nonexistent before and
after. `-p` requires root, so it cannot be triggered accidentally. `tmutil` has
**no glob/pattern support**; the only pattern list is `StdExclusions.plist`
inside the SIP-protected `backupd.bundle`. The per-worktree creation hook is
therefore the correct place to apply exclusions.

## Sandbox leak — two independent defects

1. `internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go` contains **zero** occurrences of
   "sandbox". `Sandbox.Destroy()` is called only from `sandboxcmd/run.go:50`
   (ephemeral teardown) and the manual `endless-sandbox destroy` CLI.
2. `internal/sandboxcmd/list.go:83` `classify()` returns `stateInUse` for any
   sandbox whose mode is `keep` or `persistent` — **unconditionally**, with no
   worktree-existence or PID check. All 267 sandboxes report `persistent` /
   `in-use`, and `prune` only removes `stateOrphaned`, so `sandbox prune` is
   structurally incapable of reclaiming any worktree sandbox. Its own message
   ("no orphaned ephemeral sandboxes") shows it was only ever built for
   ephemeral ones.

## Platform scope

The repo currently has **no** `runtime.GOOS` usage and no `_darwin.go` files —
no precedent for platform-conditional behavior. Anything built on `tmutil` or
`.metadata_never_index` would be the first, and needs an explicit no-op path on
other platforms rather than an assumed-macOS shell-out.
