fields.analysis:
# Worktree teardown leaves three kinds of dependent behind

Found 2026-08-06 while investigating fseventsd/kernel_task saturation.
Measured: 267 sandboxes against 113 worktrees — **184 orphaned**, 228 MB,
oldest dating to 2026-06-17.

## Defect 1 — `classify()` can never report a worktree sandbox as orphaned

`internal/sandboxcmd/list.go:83`:

```go
func classify(meta SandboxMeta) sandboxState {
    if meta.Mode == modeKeep || meta.Mode == modePersistent {
        return stateInUse    // unconditional: no worktree check, no PID check
    }
    if isAlive(meta.CreatorPID) {
        return stateLive
    }
    return stateOrphaned
}
```

Every worktree sandbox is `persistent`, so all 268 classified `in-use`.
`prune.go:33` only removes `stateOrphaned`. **`endless-sandbox prune` was
structurally incapable of reclaiming a single worktree sandbox** — its own
message ("no orphaned *ephemeral* sandboxes") shows it was built only for
ephemeral ones. A persistent sandbox whose worktree no longer exists should
classify as orphaned.

## Defect 2 — the reaper never destroys the sandbox

`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go` contains **zero** occurrences of
"sandbox". `Sandbox.Destroy()` is reachable only from
`internal/sandboxcmd/run.go:50` (ephemeral teardown) and the manual
`endless-sandbox destroy` CLI. Nothing in the drop/land/reap path calls it.
`CLAUDE.md` documents the gap ("Sandbox cleanup on worktree drop/land is not
yet automatic") but the reaper shipped without closing it.

## Defect 3 — `endless-go channel` processes outlive their worktree

Four processes aged **18–24 days** still hold open the sandbox DBs of
worktrees that are gone:

| PID | age | sandbox | worktree dir |
|---|---|---|---|
| 73345 | 18d18h | e-1533 | GONE |
| 93453 | 23d21h | e-1603 | GONE |
| 1973  | 23d21h | e-1774 | GONE |
| 79957 | 18d21h | e-1789 | GONE |

They were the only 4 of 183 orphans that `sandbox destroy` refused (correctly,
without `--force`) during the 2026-08-06 manual cleanup that removed the other
179. Each is a live process plus a pinned SQLite handle on a directory nobody
will read again. Teardown should terminate the channel process, or the channel
process should exit when its worktree disappears.

## Manual cleanup already performed

179 of 183 orphans destroyed by hand (288 MB → 68 MB, 268 → 89 sandboxes).
Backup at `orphaned-sandboxes-backup.tgz` in the session scratchpad. This task
is about making that automatic, not about re-doing it.

---

# Reap safety predicate (learned the hard way, 2026-08-06)

The manual cleanup used "worktree dir exists OR git tracks a worktree of that
name" as its protection rule. **That rule is insufficient.** It destroyed 10
sandboxes it should not have; all were restored from the pre-delete backup.

A sandbox may be reaped ONLY when every one of these is false:

| # | Condition | How to check | Missed by the manual run? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Worktree dir exists | `[ -d .endless/worktrees/<n> ]` | no |
| 2 | Git still tracks a worktree of that name | `git worktree list --porcelain` | no |
| 3 | **A live tmux window references the task ID** | window names carry `[E-NNNN]` | **YES — 8 destroyed** |
| 4 | **The task branch is unmerged to main** | `git branch --no-merged main` | **YES — 2 destroyed** |
| 5 | Worktree is unsettled (dirty working tree) | existing `worktree_unsettled.go` | n/a — implies (1) |
| 6 | A live process holds files in the sandbox | already enforced by `destroy` | no — correctly refused 4 |

## Why (3) matters

A tmux window is the user's own record that a task is still in play, and it
outlives the worktree. Of 57 task IDs with a live window in the `active`
session, 12 had no worktree directory at all — the window is the only surviving
handle on that work. Destroyed in error: `e-1202 e-1368 e-1552 e-1621 e-1664
e-1687 e-1702 e-1714` (the other 4 — `e-1533 e-1603 e-1774 e-1789` — survived
only because condition 6 blocked them).

Window names follow `endless_<slug>[E-NNNN]`; parse the bracketed ID. Note the
`active` session is grouped with `active-6`, so enumerate windows rather than
panes to avoid double-counting.

## Why (4) matters

A removed worktree whose branch never merged still holds the only copy of that
work. `git branch --no-merged main` currently lists **64** task branches.
Destroyed in error: `e-1036 e-1669`.

Condition (5) is subsumed by (1) for live worktrees, but must be checked
explicitly if reaping is ever extended to prune worktree dirs themselves.

## Implementation note

Conditions 3 and 4 are the two that survive worktree deletion, which is exactly
why a dir-existence check cannot stand alone. Both belong in the same predicate
the reaper consults, not as ad-hoc guards at the call site.

# Plan — E-1905: remove vestigial `transcript_path` + `session reimport`

Both are vestigial. `session_messages` is kept current by the LIVE Go parser
(`ParseTranscript`, `transcript.go:304`) on every event using Claude's payload
path; the stored `transcript_path` column feeds essentially nothing and goes
stale when a session changes cwd after start (recorded once at SessionStart,
never re-recorded). `session reimport` is a manual-only CLI escape hatch with a
duplicate Python parser; nothing automatic needs it. Decision (this session):
remove `session reimport` as well (option A), not keep a discovery-based form.

KEEP `transcript_offset` — it is the live parser's resume cursor
(`transcript.go:241/252`), unrelated to `transcript_path`.

## 1. Remove `session reimport` (command + Python parser)

- `src/endless/cli.py:1060-1065` — delete the `reimport` command + wiring.
- `src/endless/session_cmd.py` — delete `reimport_sessions` (~849), the duplicate
  `_parse_transcript_py` (~1202) and its helpers, and `_find_jsonl` (~857 — used
  ONLY by reimport). Remove any now-dead imports.
- Drop reimport-specific tests.

## 2. Drop the `transcript_path` column

- Schema: remove `transcript_path TEXT` from `internal/schema/schema.sql:137` and
  the mirrored DDL/backfill in `src/endless/db.py` (~361).
- Add a schema change under `internal/schema/changes/` that drops the column,
  following the `e-1568` sessions-rebuild pattern (SQLite `ALTER TABLE ... DROP
  COLUMN`, or table rebuild if the version in use needs it). The `sessions` table
  is machine-local (not journaled to the shared ledger), so this is a local
  schema change — no ledger upcast needed.

## 3. Remove writers/readers of the column

- `internal/hookcmd/claude.go:194-197` — delete the SessionStart
  `SetTranscriptPath(payload.SessionID, payload.TranscriptPath)` block (and the
  "Store transcript path for reimport" comment). `payload.TranscriptPath` is still
  used live by the `ParseTranscript` calls (232/252/262/265) — leave those.
- `internal/monitor/transcript.go` — delete `SetTranscriptPath` (~319) and
  `GetTranscriptPath` (~331, already caller-free) plus their round-trip tests
  (`transcript_test.go:397-419`).
- `internal/events/reopen_context.go` — in `inheritedSessionID`'s ORDER BY, drop
  the `OR transcript_path IS NOT NULL` evidence clause (leave `process IS NOT NULL`
  and the `>= 10`s span). Update the doc comment (~41) that names transcript_path
  as an evidence signal. Minor, intended behavior change: transcript_path is no
  longer a tiebreak signal.
- `src/endless/session_cmd.py:69/81/91` — remove `transcript_path` from the SELECT
  column lists; drop the `:854` read (goes with reimport).

## Verification — tests/tasks/e-1905-verify.sh (fully scripted)

- Build + `go test ./...` + `just test` green.
- `endless session reimport` is gone (command not found / not registered).
- `session list`, `session search`, and recaps still work — `session_messages` is
  unaffected (still populated by the live Go parser); assert a live-parsed session
  still yields messages/search hits against the sandbox.
- No remaining references to `transcript_path` in `internal/` or `src/` (grep guard).

## Boundary

- Does NOT touch `transcript_offset` or the live `ParseTranscript` path.
- Not a plan-file/plan-reimport change — that is a separate, already-abandoned
  concept; this is only session transcript tracking.

# Plan: stop the sandboxcmd destroy tests from cold-building the world

## Fix

Preferred: **build once per package, before any environment redirect.**

1. Promote `buildSandboxBinary` (already in `destroy_test.go`) to a
   package-level once-built helper — a `sync.Once` guarding a single build into
   a package-scoped temp dir, returning the same path to every caller. Building
   happens with the ambient environment, so it reuses the developer's warm
   `GOCACHE`.
2. Point `livewriters_test.go:117` and `:165` at that helper instead of their
   own `exec.Command("go", "build", ...)` calls.
3. Drop `t.Setenv("HOME", tmp)` from both tests. Keep
   `t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", tmp)` — `Provision(...)` runs in-process and
   needs it. If `Provision` also consults HOME, set HOME via the existing
   child-only `cmd.Env` lines rather than in-process; confirm which it reads
   before deciding.

Acceptable smaller alternative if the once-per-package refactor is unwanted:
give the build command an explicit `GOCACHE` captured before the redirect
(`build.Env = append(os.Environ(), "GOCACHE="+realGOCACHE)`). Keeps the change
to two lines but leaves two full builds in place.

## Verification

`tests/tasks/e-1908-verify.sh`:

- **The regression, as a wall-clock budget.** `go test ./internal/sandboxcmd/
  -timeout 180s` completes well inside its timeout. Assert on exit status, and
  print the elapsed time so a regression is visible rather than merely slow.
  Baseline for the report: the package currently cannot finish in 10 minutes.
- The four behavioral assertions these tests make must be unchanged — destroy
  refuses with a live writer and names the PID and `--force`; `--force`
  destroys and prints the confirmation. Do not weaken the tests to make them
  fast; the point is to stop paying for a cold compiler, not to stop testing.
- Assert no `_test.go` in the repo combines `t.Setenv("HOME"` with an in-test
  `go build` — a grep guard so the pattern cannot come back. Both current call
  sites are in `internal/sandboxcmd`.
- Fold-in regression: `go test ./internal/...` completes without a package
  timeout panic. This is the whole point of the task and is the one check that
  would have caught the defect originally.

## Out of scope

The other five in-test `go build` call sites. They do not redirect HOME and are
not affected; consolidating them onto one shared build helper is a separate
cleanup if anyone wants it.
fields.analysis:
# Root cause (measured, not inferred)

Both slow tests follow this order:

```go
tmp := t.TempDir()
t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", tmp)
t.Setenv("HOME", tmp)          // <-- the problem
...
build := exec.Command("go", "build", "-o", bin, "../../cmd/endless-go")
build.CombinedOutput()          // livewriters_test.go:117 and :165
```

`go env GOCACHE` is derived from HOME on macOS:

- real HOME  -> `~/Library/Caches/go-build` (warm; the same cache every other
  build in the repo uses)
- HOME=tmp   -> `<tmp>/Library/Caches/go-build` (empty, and thrown away with
  the test's TempDir)

Measured in this worktree:

| build | elapsed |
|---|---|
| `go build ./cmd/endless-go` with real HOME | **3s** |
| same build with HOME redirected to an empty temp dir | **still running at 60s** (capped) |

GOMODCACHE is unaffected (GOPATH-derived), so nothing is re-downloaded — this is
pure recompilation of every dependency, `modernc.org/sqlite` being the expensive
one.

The goroutine dump that made this look like a deadlock is just
`CombinedOutput`'s pipe copy waiting on a compiler that has not finished:
`livewriters_test.go:166` is the `go build` line, not the `destroy` invocation.

# Why the whole package blows its timeout

Two tests, each paying a full cold compile into a cache that is discarded
immediately afterward (each `t.TempDir()` is unique, so they cannot even reuse
each other's). That is what consumes the 10-minute package timeout and takes
`go test ./internal/...` down with it.

# The correct pattern already exists in this package

`internal/sandboxcmd/destroy_test.go` never redirects the test process's own
environment. It builds via the shared `buildSandboxBinary(t)` helper with the
ambient env intact, then scopes the redirect to the child only:

```go
cmd.Env = append(cmd.Environ(), "XDG_CACHE_HOME="+tmp, "HOME="+tmp)
```

`livewriters_test.go` already does exactly this for its own `destroy` command
(lines 123-125, 171-173). The `t.Setenv` pair at the top of each test exists
only because `Provision(...)` runs IN-PROCESS and reads `XDG_CACHE_HOME`. So the
in-process redirect is needed for `XDG_CACHE_HOME`; the `HOME` redirect is the
part that costs the build cache.

# Scope check

Only these two tests combine an in-test `go build` with a `t.Setenv("HOME")`.
Five other files shell out to `go build` in tests
(`internal/monitor/worktreecheck_scripts_test.go`, `internal/eventcmd`,
`internal/templatecmd`, `internal/sessionquerycmd`, and `destroy_test.go`
itself); none of them redirect HOME, so none are affected. This is a
two-test defect, not a systemic one.

`./tests/tasks/e-1906-verify.sh` reports 44 passed, 2 failed on main:

    ✗ no live `needs_recap` anywhere in the source tree
        got: tests/tasks/e-1905-verify.sh:375:    needs_recap INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    ✗ no live `summary_seq` anywhere in the source tree

Confirmed pre-existing and NOT caused by E-1901: reproduces identically from the
main checkout, same two checks, same counts.

Cause: E-1905 and E-1906 landed in close succession. E-1906's section 1 is a
grep-based "zero hits in the source tree" assertion for the identifiers it
removed. E-1905's verify script legitimately contains a historical `CREATE TABLE
sessions` fixture that still lists `needs_recap` and `summary_seq` — it is
asserting against a pre-drop schema on purpose. E-1906's grep cannot tell a live
reference from a deliberate historical fixture, so the sibling script trips it.

Fix direction: narrow E-1906's grep to exclude sibling task-verify fixtures (it
already excludes `internal/schema/changes/`, which has the same
period-accurate-schema property), rather than editing E-1905's fixture — the
fixture is correct and load-bearing for E-1905's own assertions.

Both symptoms are one defect and are filed together deliberately: they share a
single cause and a single fix, and splitting them would put two sessions in the
same grep block.

This is also a concrete instance of a coordination hazard worth noting: two
tasks whose changes overlap the same files landed in parallel and broke each
other's verification, with neither task's own suite green afterwards.

# Plan — E-1911: append a curated block, park the relay gate

One task, four parts, one land. It closes E-1785.

**Start from current main.** E-1901 landed (`19974ef`, `aa83a0c`), so
`internal/hookcmd/relay_gate.go` and the Stop-branch call site exist there but
NOT in the `task/1785-*` worktree, which predates them. Rebase before starting
or part 1 will look unimplementable.

## Part 1 — park the gate, in code

**Kill switch.** The gate has exactly one call site,
`internal/hookcmd/claude.go:268`:

```go
if handled, err := enforceRelayGate(payload); err != nil {
```

Add a package-level `const relayGateEnabled = false` in `relay_gate.go`, with a
comment stating it is parked pending the append contract, not abandoned, and
have `enforceRelayGate` return `(false, nil)` immediately when it is false.

Everything else stays: `relay_gate.go`, its unit tests, the checkpoint
recording, the `GateKindRelay` row, the `session_gates` columns. Reviving is a
one-line flip.

**Not in `settings.json`.** The `Stop` hook stays installed and stays
synchronous (E-1901 moved it into `SYNC_EVENTS` and added the async repair —
leave both). Disabling via config would drift per-machine and per-worktree, and
would silently un-fix itself on the next `setup` run.

**The compose-time nudge must go too.** `internal/hookcmd/claude.go:490`
(E-1803) injects "relay the report's output verbatim, add nothing" at
PostToolUse on `task report`. That is the same contract the gate enforced, and
it contradicts the append model directly — leaving it means the harness keeps
instructing the opposite of what the command now asks for. Rewrite it to state
the append contract: answer normally, then append the block after the
separator.

The literal at `claude.go:298` ("hand-write it — run `endless task report <id>`
and relay its output") needs the same treatment.

## Part 2 — the append contract

**Steer text** (`src/endless/report_cmd.py`, `report_prompts.py`). Today's
`STEER` says relay the block as the ENTIRE final message, byte for byte, and
names the Stop hook as enforcement. Replace with: your own answer comes first
and is not constrained; append the block below, unchanged, after the separator.
Drop the enforcement sentence — it will be false once part 1 lands, and a steer
that threatens a gate that no longer fires teaches the agent to discount steers.

**Separator.** One opening marker, not the current BEGIN/END pair — the block
runs to the end of the message, so a closing marker is redundant. It must be
machine-detectable so a future validator can find the block:

```
----- ENDLESS REPORT -----
```

Keep it a single fixed literal in one Go/Python-shared constant, not a tunable
prompt entry, since a validator has to match it exactly.

**Empty block still renders: separator + `Nothing to report.`** Not silence.
The null case must be *stated*, because an absent block is ambiguous in a way
that matters: the user cannot tell "there were no facts" from "the block failed
to render." A rendering bug that swallows the block would be invisible, and the
user would have to go check by hand — which is the cost this whole epic exists
to remove. One fixed line makes the null result an assertion rather than an
absence.

Keep the `nothing-to-report` prompt entry; it retains its purpose under the
append contract.

Note this does NOT reintroduce the failure E-1911 was filed for. That failure
was "nothing to report" *displacing* the agent's actual message. Under the
append contract the organic answer is always present above the separator, so
`Nothing to report.` now correctly means "the computed half found nothing to
add," not "there is nothing to say."

## Part 3 — stop duplicating `session status`

Three coordinated edits; the point is that the report and the handoff template
each demanded children because the other did.

- `src/endless/report_cmd.py:276–285` — delete the `Children:` branch. This is
  also the fix for the report listing E-1907 (parent E-1671) and E-1908 (root)
  as children of E-1785: the wrong list stops being computed at all.
- `internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/epic.md.tmpl:29` — drop
  "Final message — lead with the state of the children."
- `internal/templatecmd/template_test.go:134` — the epic case asserts that exact
  string; update it.
- `internal/monitor/task_report.go:21` — the children fact and its comment
  become dead once nothing renders them; remove rather than leave orphaned.

## Part 4 — confirmed children are not hidden

`src/endless/task_cmd.py` lines 4400, 4462, 4596 all carry:

```sql
FROM tasks WHERE parent_id = ? AND status != 'confirmed'
```

Remove the filter. It excludes `confirmed` only, so an epic renders its
`obsolete` and `assumed` children but drops the ones that were verified and
landed — which is how E-1906 vanished from `task show E-1785 --children` while
four obsolete children stayed. Confirmed children are precisely what an epic
nearing completion needs to show.

## Explicitly NOT in scope

- **The veracity rule and mechanical citation check** (E-1876 part 2). Under the
  append contract the curated block is *computed by Endless*, not composed by
  the agent, so its facts are true by construction; the organic half is
  deliberately unconstrained. What remains is agent-authored `--json` note text,
  which is not worth a task of its own.
- **`task annotate`** (E-1876 part 3). It existed to house observations that
  suppression displaced. Nothing is suppressed now, so it has no purpose.
- **The plan-write do-not-recap reminder** (E-1876 part 4) — pure suppression,
  dead under the new direction.
- **Monitor checkpoint surfacing** (E-1876 part 5). The gate is parked; surface
  it if and when the gate returns.
- **Re-enabling the gate under the append contract.** Deliberately deferred —
  the whole point of parking it is to decide its shape once the append block
  has settled.

## Verification — `tests/tasks/e-1911-verify.sh`

- **Go.** `enforceRelayGate` returns not-handled while `relayGateEnabled` is
  false, for an input that would otherwise bounce (guards against the switch
  being wired to the wrong branch). The epic handoff template no longer contains
  the children directive. `Stop` is still in `SYNC_EVENTS`.
- **Python.** `task report` on an epic omits `Children:`; a report with no facts
  emits the separator followed by exactly `Nothing to report.`; a report with
  facts emits the separator followed by the block. The separator is present in
  BOTH cases — that is the property that makes a swallowed block detectable.
  `task show --children` includes a `confirmed` child.
- **End-to-end.** Through the real CLI → worktree `endless-go` → sandbox DB:
  `task report` on an epic with a confirmed child and an unrelated task
  elsewhere in the tree produces neither a children line nor a stray id.
- **Regression.** `task show E-1785 --children` lists E-1906.

## Sequencing

Part 1 first and alone — until the gate is parked and the nudge rewritten, any
session working this task is itself being told to replace its message, which is
the contract being removed. Parts 2–4 after, in any order.

# Plan: make `--keep-status` hold the status across every auto-transition

## Decision

Implement option (a) from the analysis: when `--keep-status` is passed, the
Python layer sends the task's current status explicitly, so the executor's
existing "caller wins" precedence suppresses the plan-attach promotion. No
change to the event vocabulary, and nothing that collides with E-1671.

If review prefers option (b) — a `KeepStatus` field on
`TaskFieldsUpdatedPayload` — say so before implementing; the rest of this plan
holds either way.

## Scope of the contract change

`--keep-status` today is documented as the done-task auto-revisit escape hatch.
It becomes: **no auto-transition fires; the status you see is the status you
keep.** That covers all three:

1. E-1762 auto-revisit (done task, plan text edited) — already guarded
2. E-1845 auto-untriage (pre-work task, description edited) — already guarded
3. plan-attach promotion (`untriaged`/`unplanned` + non-empty `--text` ->
   `submitted`) — the gap this task closes

An explicit `--status` in the same call still wins over everything; passing both
`--status` and `--keep-status` should be rejected as contradictory rather than
silently resolved.

## Implementation

1. `src/endless/task_cmd.py` (`update_task`, near the `auto_revisit` /
   `auto_untriage` block around lines 3990-4045): when `keep_status` is set and
   `status is None`, add the row's current status to the fields map. Placing it
   with the other status resolution keeps the three transitions readable as one
   decision rather than two-here-one-in-Go.
2. Reject `--status` together with `--keep-status` in `src/endless/cli.py`
   (or in `update_task`, wherever the other argument conflicts are caught).
3. Correct the help text in `src/endless/cli.py:1718` — drop "on a done task",
   state that no auto-transition fires.
4. Update `endless guide tasks`, which frames the flag as the escape hatch for a
   "typo- or formatting-only edit". Same wording appears in `CLAUDE.md` and the
   status-lifecycle prose; re-sync whichever copies the guide test asserts.

## Verification

`tests/tasks/e-NNNN-verify.sh`, self-contained against a throwaway
XDG_CONFIG_HOME and a temp project (shape per `tests/tasks/e-1880-verify.sh`):

- **The regression itself.** Create a task, leave it `unplanned`, update it with
  `--text-file` + `--keep-status`, assert status is still `unplanned` and the
  text did change. Without `--keep-status` the same update must still promote to
  `submitted` — the promotion is correct default behavior and must not be lost.
- Same pair from `untriaged`.
- E-1762 still guarded: a done task (`assumed`) + text edit + `--keep-status`
  stays `assumed`; without the flag it goes `revisit`.
- E-1845 still guarded: a `ready` task + description edit + `--keep-status`
  stays `ready`; without the flag it resets.
- `--status` and `--keep-status` together exits non-zero.
- Fold-in regression: `uv run pytest tests/` for the task-update tests, and
  `go test ./internal/events/...` (the promotion's white-box test lives in
  `internal/events/pre_judgment_test.go` and must stay green — the executor
  behavior is unchanged under option (a), which is itself worth asserting).

## Out of scope

Any change to `internal/events` payloads or the executor. Under option (a) the
Go side is untouched, which is the point.
fields.analysis:
# Root cause

Three auto-transitions can change status during `task update`. `--keep-status`
guards two of them and cannot reach the third.

**Guarded (Python, `src/endless/task_cmd.py`):**

- `auto_revisit` (E-1762, ~line 3993) — a real text edit on a done task flips it
  to `revisit`. Condition opens with `not keep_status`.
- `auto_untriage` (E-1845, ~line 4018) — a material description edit on a
  pre-work task resets it to `untriaged`/`submitted`. Also opens with
  `not keep_status`.

**Unguarded (Go, `internal/events/executor.go:579-594`, `execTaskFieldsUpdated`):**

```go
if textVal, hasText := p.Fields["text"]; hasText {
    if _, statusSet := p.Fields["status"]; !statusSet {
        ...
        if isPreJudgmentStatus(currentStatus) {
            setClauses = append(setClauses, "status = ?")
            args = append(args, "submitted")
        }
    }
}
```

Its only suppression is `!statusSet` — "caller wins" when status is explicit.
`--keep-status` is never serialized into the event, and
`TaskFieldsUpdatedPayload` is just `Fields map[string]any`, so there is no field
in which the intent could travel. The Python comment at task_cmd.py:4031 even
names this split ("left to the executor's plan-attach auto-move: that move only
fires when the update does not set status explicitly") without noticing that
`--keep-status` therefore cannot influence it.

# The documented contract is also too narrow

`cli.py`'s help reads "Keep the current status when editing plan text on a done
task (suppresses the auto-revisit for a typo/formatting-only edit)." That
describes E-1762 only. `endless guide tasks` frames it as the escape hatch for a
"typo- or formatting-only edit". Neither promises the plan-attach case, so part
of this task is a deliberate decision to widen the flag to mean what its name
says: no auto-transition fires.

# Fix options

**(a) Python sends `status = <current>` when `--keep-status` is passed.**
The executor's existing "caller wins" branch then suppresses the promotion, and
the two Python guards already work. No event-vocabulary change, no new payload
field, nothing in `internal/events` to coordinate. Cost: the emitted event
carries a status field whose value equals the old one — a no-op status write in
the ledger. Replays cleanly.

**(b) Add `KeepStatus bool` to `TaskFieldsUpdatedPayload` and honor it in the
executor.** Semantically cleaner — the intent is named rather than encoded as a
degenerate status write. Cost: a new field in the event vocabulary, which is
exactly the surface E-1671's upcasting epic is about to rework, and whose
"Coordination" note asks work to be sequenced so it does not collide on
`internal/events` / `internal/eventcmd`.

**Recommended: (a).** It is the smaller change, it needs no ledger-shape
decision, and it keeps this fix off E-1671's path. If (b) is later wanted, the
upcasting pipeline is the natural place to introduce it.

# Provenance

Found during E-1906 while folding the E-1907 finding into E-1671's text. The
append promoted E-1671 `unplanned` -> `submitted` despite `--keep-status`, and
the status was restored manually.

# E-1917 post-land defects

Two defects in the landed implementation. The first was found by another session
working on E-1898; the second surfaced while verifying the first.

## Defect 1 — suppression silences exactly the session that needs the notice

**Symptom.** The user changes a task's status from a shell pane. Every session
holding that task is notified EXCEPT the one actually working on it.

**Evidence** (`session_notices`, task 1898): every row is stamped
`changed_by_session = 1034`, and 1034 — the session holding E-1898 — is a
recipient of none of them except id 625, which session 1046 authored.

```
620  →1026  actor=1034  {"status":{"before":"unverified","after":"assumed"}}
621  →1054  actor=1034  {"status":{"before":"unverified","after":"assumed"}}
                        (no row for 1034)
```

**Root cause.** `evt.Actor.SessionID` answers *"which session should this command
be credited to"*, not *"which session physically made this change."* E-1917's
suppression consumed it as if it answered the second.

`_current_endless_session_id` (`src/endless/task_cmd.py:3425`) resolves in four
layers, and two of them attribute a HUMAN's command to an agent session:

- **Layer 4** (E-1294): a shell pane with exactly one sibling Claude pane in the
  same tmux window is attributed to that sibling. This is deliberate and
  documented — "lets a shell pane in a Claude-using window transparently
  attribute commands to its sibling Claude session."
- **Layer 1**: `ENDLESS_SESSION_ID`, which `esu` / `endless shell-init` exports
  into the user's own shell.

Only **layer 2** (`CLAUDECODE=1` + `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`) means the mutating
process IS the agent.

So in the tmux layout the user actually works in, "the user edits from a bare
terminal" does not produce a NULL actor. It produces the adjacent agent's
session id. The suppression rule then works exactly as designed on wrong input.

**Where the plan went wrong.** E-1917's own plan asserted: *"A NULL actor (the
user editing from a bare terminal) suppresses nobody, which is correct — that is
the case this feature exists for."* That assumption was never validated against
the resolver. It is false in the primary scenario, so the feature is defeated
precisely where it was meant to help.

**Fix options.**

- **(a) Remove suppression.** Every holder is notified, including the session
  that made the change. Cost: one redundant confirmatory line on the turn after
  a session changes something itself. Cannot silence the wrong session. Smallest
  change; safe immediate revert.
- **(b) Suppress only on in-process agent identity.** Suppress when the mutating
  process is the agent (layer 2); notify for layers 1, 3 and 4, which are all
  humans at a keyboard. Keeps the original intent without the failure mode.
  Requires the event to carry HOW the actor was resolved, not just the id —
  `Actor` gains an in-process flag that the Python resolver sets only on layer 2.

Recommend (b), with (a) available as an immediate stop-gap if the fix needs to
wait. Note (b) touches the event Actor contract, so it wants review.

## Defect 2 — undelivered notices accumulate forever for dead sessions

**Symptom.** 553 of 679 notice rows (82%) are undelivered, and the largest
holders are sessions that have ended.

```
session  state        undelivered
994      needs_input  34
996      ended        32
614      ended        27
794      needs_input  26
738      idle         25
1029     ended        22
534      ended        20
```

**Root cause.** The trigger fans out to every `session_tasks` row for the task.
That table deliberately has no FK to `sessions` and outlives them, so notices are
written for sessions that ended long ago. Nothing filters on session state at
write time, and nothing reaps. An ended session never takes another turn, so its
rows are permanently undeliverable.

**Consequence.** Unbounded growth, and the table's contents stop being a useful
signal — you cannot tell a genuine backlog from dead weight.

**Fix.** Filter the trigger's fan-out on session state so ended sessions are
never written to, and reap existing rows for ended sessions. Excluding only
`ended` is the conservative choice: `idle` and `needs_input` sessions may still
take another turn, and their notices are legitimately pending.

Open question for the fix: `sessions.state` at WRITE time is not the same as at
delivery time. A session that ends between write and delivery still leaves a
dead row, so a reaper is needed regardless of the write-time filter.

## Not a defect — notice 625

The E-1898 session observed that notice 625 was `notified = 1` yet "never
surfaced in my transcript." That is expected: `additionalContext` is injected as
a system-reminder into the model's context, not as visible transcript text, so
its absence from the transcript is not evidence it was never injected.
`.endless/logs/session-notices.jsonl` records every delivery and is the place to
confirm or refute injection.



---

# Third post-land defect: `esu` makes the user's own edits self-suppress

Found 2026-08-20 while working E-1997. The user confirmed that task from the
CLI while a session held it, and the session was never told — it went on to
report the task as `unverified` two turns later.

## The chain, each link verified

1. `tasks.changed_by_session` for E-1997 named the session that was *holding*
   the task, not the actor. The user made the change.
2. It was stamped that way because the user's shell had `ENDLESS_SESSION_ID`
   exported by `esu`. The same land run printed "Derived task ID from session: E-1997",
   so the routing was demonstrably active.
3. `tasks_notify_sessions` ends with
   `AND st.session_id IS NOT NEW.changed_by_session`, so the holding session was
   excluded from the fan-out.
4. `SELECT ... FROM session_notices WHERE task_id = 1997` returns **zero rows**.
   The notice was never created — nothing was lost in delivery.
5. Reproduced against the trigger directly (sandbox DB, synthetic task + one
   holding session):
   - `changed_by_session = NULL` (bare terminal) → **1** notice
   - `changed_by_session = <the holding session>` → **0** notices

## Why the premise is wrong

`stampTaskActor`'s comment states the assumption outright:

> An empty Actor.SessionID stamps NULL, which suppresses nobody. That is
> correct, not a fallback: a NULL actor is the user editing from a bare
> terminal, which is the case this whole feature exists for.

The bare terminal is not the common case, because Endless tells the user not to
have one. `endless guide` instructs `eval "$(endless shell-init)"` then `esu`,
whose entire purpose is to export `ENDLESS_SESSION_ID` so subsequent commands
route through the session's worktree. Following the documented workflow converts
every user-side task edit into a change attributed to the agent.

The result is inverted: the notices that DO get through are the low-value ones
(background triage, actor NULL), and the one that matters most — the human just
changed the task you are holding — is the one guaranteed to be suppressed.

## The distinction the schema is missing

`ENDLESS_SESSION_ID` answers "which session's worktree should this command route
through". Self-suppression needs "which agent made this change". Today one value
serves both. A human at a shell prompt with `esu` active is a different actor
from the agent running in that session, and only the second should suppress.

Worth considering (not a decision): stamp the actor from the hook-observed agent
session (the session whose harness ran the command) rather than from the routing
env var; or have the CLI distinguish an interactive TTY invocation from one made
by an agent's tool call, and stamp NULL for the former.

## Related but separate

Two notices for E-1998/E-1999 (background triage, actor NULL) were rendered,
logged to `.endless/logs/session-notices.jsonl` at 08:48:14Z, and marked
`notified = 1`. The session did not act on them. Whether they reached the
session's context is unresolved: the transcript's user message at 08:48:13.986Z
carries no injected text, but it is not established that Claude Code records
injected `additionalContext` in the transcript at all, so that is not proof of
non-delivery. Worth settling before treating it as a delivery bug — the code's
own comment says marking a notice delivered that was not injected is the one
thing that must never happen.

The hook side is confirmed working. Driving the real global binary with a
UserPromptSubmit payload for this session returns exit 0 and exactly:

```json
{"additionalContext":"Active task: E-1997 (confirmed · now) — Fix unsupported-harness banner leaking into unrelated Bash tool output on Claude Code Desktop."}
```

Correct shape per the Claude Code hooks contract (top-level `additionalContext`
for UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart; nested under `hookSpecificOutput` only for
PostToolUse), and it carries the current status. So the injection payload was
right; only the notice was missing.

fields.text:
# Implementation spec — `ES-` refs everywhere + resuming a task-less session

Surfaced while verifying E-1914's reworked `session list`, which made task-less
sessions visible for the first time. ES-963 is the live example: 133 messages,
six `session_tasks` rows (revisited E-1776/E-1797, surfaced E-1801/E-1802/
E-1804/E-1805 — it is the session that designed `session resume` itself), and no
claimed goal. Both attempts to get back into it failed:

```
$ endless session resume ES-963
Error: no session matches "ES-963"

$ endless session goto ES-963 --resume
Error: session 963 has no task worktree to resume into (a background agent that never started?).
```

Two independent defects, plus a third found while inventorying. None is caused by
E-1914 — E-1914 only made the session visible enough to try.

---

## Thread 1 — accept `ES-` at every session-ref entry point

`ES-NNN` is the form `task show` prints under `Created:`/`Touched by:` and the
form `endless guide` tells sessions to prefer, precisely because a bare integer
matching both a session and a task is ambiguous. Today only half the entry points
honor it.

| Entry point | Backing | Reached by | `ES-`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_resolve_session` — `src/endless/session_cmd.py:62` | DB | `session history`, `session hide`/`unhide` (incl. `--task`) | yes (E-1914) |
| `_resolve_goto_target` — `session_cmd.py:~2010` | live panes | `session goto` | yes |
| `_match_companions` — `session_cmd.py:1778` | live panes | `session show`, `session cd`, `session use` (via `_resolve_companion`) | **no** |
| `ResolveResumeTarget` — `internal/monitor/resume.go:62` | DB | `session resume`, `session goto --resume` | **no** |

`session goto ES-963` works only because `_resolve_goto_target` strips the prefix
itself and passes bare digits downstream; every resolver it delegates to is still
prefix-blind.

### Fixes

1. **`_match_companions`** — strip a leading `ES-`/`es-` before the `isdigit()`
   branch. Without it the ref falls through to the UUID-prefix branch and matches
   nothing, so `session show ES-963` reports "No Claude session matches".

2. **`ResolveResumeTarget`** — add an `ES-`/`es-` branch routing straight to
   `resumeBySessionID`. It must be session-**explicit**: never fall back to the
   task lookup, mirroring how `E-` is already task-explicit. Stating the id space
   is the entire purpose of the prefix, so `ES-500` must never silently resolve to
   task E-500's session. The bare-integer path keeps its current
   task-first-then-session behavior unchanged.

### Deliberately NOT a shared parser

Go and Python cannot share code, so a "shared session-ref parser" means two
implementations plus a cross-language contract to keep in sync — the exact shape
that let `ES-` go missing on the Go side to begin with. The three resolvers also
have genuinely different policies (session-only vs session-or-task, DB-backed vs
live-pane-backed), so only the lexing is common and it is a few lines each.

The guarantee comes from a **drift test** instead (below): every entry point must
accept `ES-<id>`, enforced by a table a new entry point has to be added to.

---

## Thread 2 — auto-create a task + worktree for a resumed task-less session

`_resolve_resume` (`session_cmd.py:~221`) raises when `active_task_id` is NULL,
because `ResumeTarget.WorktreePath` is only populated for a task. A no-goal
session therefore has nowhere to be resumed into, even though its transcript is
intact and it did real work.

**Resuming into the project root was considered and REJECTED.** The project root
is the main checkout, which this project's own rules forbid editing — it would
drop a live Claude session somewhere it must not work, with no branch and nowhere
to commit. In Endless one session maps to one task, and the fix must honor that
rather than route around it.

**Prompting the user for a title was also considered and REJECTED.** Someone
resuming a task-less session is doing so *because* they do not know what it was
about; asking them to name it asks the one question they cannot answer. Figuring
that out is `session recap`'s job — a separate, additional command (see the
companion task), not a blocker for this one.

So: create the task, claim it, resume into its worktree.

1. **`internal/monitor/resume.go`** — `ResumeTarget` needs the session's
   `project_id` (or resolved project path) available to the Python caller so the
   task can be created in the right project. Fill it unconditionally, not only on
   the task branch; the task branch's `WorktreePath` stays exactly as it is.

2. **`_resolve_resume`** — when `task is None`, create and claim a task rather
   than raising:
   - **Title:** `Auto-resumed task for session ES-NNN`. A deliberate placeholder,
     not a description — it says exactly what it is and claims nothing about
     content it cannot know.
   - **Description:** name what the session already touched (one query against
     `session_tasks`), so the container is not contentless — e.g. "Container task
     auto-created so session ES-963 could be resumed into a worktree. The session
     had already touched: E-1776, E-1797, E-1801, E-1802, E-1804, E-1805."
   - **Status:** created already-claimed, straight to `underway`. It skips triage
     and the approve gate deliberately: a human ran `session resume`, so the
     approval that gate exists to capture already happened interactively. Triage
     could not judge a placeholder description anyway.
   - **Worktree:** reuse `task claim`'s existing worktree-creation path. Do not
     reimplement worktree setup here.
   - Print what happened before exec'ing — the user must see the task id and
     worktree they just acquired.

3. **Idempotency falls out for free, but assert it.** Once the first resume sets
   `sessions.active_task_id`, a second resume of the same session takes the
   ordinary task path and creates nothing. Cover it in the verify script so a
   future refactor cannot start minting a task per resume.

4. **Rewrite the diagnostics.** "(a background agent that never started?)" is
   plainly wrong for a 133-message session; that parenthetical belongs only on the
   no-UUID branch it was written for.

5. **Residual error cases** (keep them errors, and name the UUID so
   `claude --resume <uuid>` by hand is one copy-paste away): the session has no
   `project_id`, or worktree creation fails.

### `--dry-run` — widen the seam and rename it, decided

`session resume` ends in `os.execvp` (`session_cmd.py:432`): the process becomes
Claude, so nothing after it runs and a test cannot inspect the outcome.
`--print-decision` is the existing seam — it stops one line short of the exec and
prints the resolved target as JSON — but `session_cmd.py:405` refuses it unless
`--review`/`--reopen` was passed.

Remove that guard. `decision_out` is **already populated on the plain path**
(`session_cmd.py:213-218` sets `recovered`/`worktree`/`label`), so the guard is the
only thing preventing it from working, and widening it costs nothing. Extend the
emitted dict to carry the resolved uuid, session id, and — for Thread 2 — whether
a task was auto-created and which.

**Name it `--dry-run`, with `--print-decision` kept as a deprecated alias.** Once
the flag works on every path it is no longer printing a *recovery decision*, it is
declining to act — and `endless triage run --dry-run` already establishes that
spelling in this CLI for exactly this meaning ("print what I would do, write
nothing"). Keep the old spelling working so E-1801's verify script and any muscle
memory do not break; it need not be advertised in `--help`.

Verification must never launch Claude.

### Non-goals

- **`--review`/`--reopen` stay task-only.** They rebuild a *task's* dropped
  worktree from its landing sha or branch tip; with no task there is nothing to
  rebuild, which is why that path was never reachable for ES-963.
- **No cwd column on `sessions`.**
- **No transcript-derived title.** That is `session recap`'s job, in its own task.

---

## Verification

Write `tests/tasks/e-1918-verify.sh`, isolated exactly as `e-1914-verify.sh` is
(throwaway git repo as project root under a temp dir, own `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and
`XDG_CACHE_HOME`, worktree binary on PATH, no real DB/ledger/cache touched).

Checks:

- **The drift test.** For every entry point in the Thread 1 table, `ES-<id>`
  resolves to the same session as the bare `<id>`. Table-driven over the command
  surface (`session show`, `session cd`, `session use`, `session history`,
  `session hide --task`, `session goto`, `session resume`), so adding a new
  session-ref command means adding one row — and forgetting `ES-` fails the suite.
- `ES-<n>` never resolves to task `<n>`'s session, even when a task with that id
  exists and has a session. This is the whole point of the prefix.
- `E-<task>` still resolves task-first; a bare integer still prefers the task and
  falls back to the session. Both unchanged.
- Resuming a task-less session creates exactly one task, titled
  `Auto-resumed task for session ES-NNN`, at `underway`, with a worktree on disk,
  and sets `sessions.active_task_id` to it.
- The auto-created task's description names the tasks the session had touched.
- **Resuming the same session twice creates exactly one task** (idempotency).
- A task-bearing session still resumes into its own worktree and creates nothing.
- The no-`project_id` case still errors, and the error names the UUID.
- `--dry-run` works on the plain resume path (it is the seam every check above
  runs through — no check may exec `claude`), and `--print-decision` still works
  as its alias.

Alongside the script: Go units for `ResolveResumeTarget` (the `ES-`/`E-`/bare
matrix and the project field) and pytest for the two Python resolvers.

fields.description: task update --status=submitted fails with "Invalid status 'submitted'" even though submitted is a real lifecycle status that task add and task submit both accept. Cause: src/endless/task_cmd.py:4001 re-declares its own hardcoded status tuple that omits submitted, instead of using the canonical TASK_STATUSES at src/endless/cli.py:122 (which includes it and backs every Click choice). Effect: a task cannot be moved back to submitted at all, so an accidental status change is unrecoverable via the CLI. Fix the drift at its source by having the update validator use the canonical list, and set E-1817 back to submitted (it was knocked from submitted to assumed by an accidental task assume).

fields.text:
# Implementation spec — `endless session recap`

Answer "what was this session about?" on demand. The need is concrete: E-1914's
reworked `session list` renders the active task's id and title, so a session that
never claimed a task shows two blank cells, and E-1918 auto-creates a task titled
`Auto-resumed task for session ES-NNN` on resume *because the user cannot name
it*. This is the command that lets them find out.

Explicitly user-invoked and expected to be rare — reached when triaging a
task-less session, not on a schedule.

---

## Command surface

```
endless session recap <session-id|task-id> [--refresh] [--json]
```

- `<ref>` accepts a session (`ES-NNN`, bare integer, UUID prefix) or a task
  (`E-NNN` → that task's most-recent session that has messages).
- Resolve via `_resolve_session` (`src/endless/session_cmd.py:62`), which is
  ES-aware as of E-1914. Do not add a fourth session-ref resolver; E-1918 is
  actively reducing the count.
- `--refresh` — ignore the cache and regenerate.
- `--json` — `{session_id, recap, generated_at, cached, stale}`.

---

## Input: `session_messages`, not the transcript file

E-1905 dropped `sessions.transcript_path`, and the path is known only at hook
time — so there is no stored path to re-read. There does not need to be:
`monitor.ParseTranscript` already writes every message into `session_messages`,
which is what `session history` and `session search` read. Recap summarizes that.

Consequence worth stating: recap works for an ended session whose transcript file
has been deleted, because the content was projected into the DB when it was live.

Selection:

- Roles `user` and `assistant` only. `tool_use` is excluded — it is 61% of the
  whole table (56,236 of 92,545 rows), and tool input (file paths, command text)
  compresses poorly and would crowd out the conversation.
- **Known boilerplate excluded**, from BOTH the input and the staleness count.
  Skill prompts recur verbatim across sessions — one appears 149 times across 133
  real sessions — and a boilerplate `user` row is not a turn in any meaningful
  sense. Left in, running such a skill four times would stale a recap without the
  conversation having moved, and would spend budget on text that says nothing
  about this session. Match the same way `session list` already filters recap
  probes (`content LIKE` prefixes), and keep the patterns in one named constant.
  Excluded from recording? **No** — these are real user turns, and dropping them
  at record time would make `session history` misrepresent what was typed. They
  are excluded from recap only.
- Ordered by `created_at, id`.
- Bounded by `RECAP_INPUT_BUDGET = 60_000` characters, **enforced in SQL, not in
  Python**. Reading 696 KB into memory to then discard 90% of it is backwards;
  the query must return only what will be sent.

### Budgeting in the query

Two levels, both in SQL:

1. **Per-message cap** so one pathological message cannot consume the budget:

   ```sql
   CASE WHEN length(content) <= :msg_cap THEN content
        ELSE substr(content, 1, :msg_cap/2) || ' … ' ||
             substr(content, -(:msg_cap/2))
   END
   ```

2. **Set-level budget** via a running total, so the row count is decided by the
   database:

   ```sql
   SUM(length(content)) OVER (ORDER BY created_at, id)              -- from the head
   SUM(length(content)) OVER (ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC)    -- from the tail
   ```

   Take head rows while the ascending running total is under the head share, tail
   rows while the descending running total is under the tail share, `UNION` them,
   and emit `… N messages elided …` between when anything was dropped. SQLite has
   supported window functions since 3.25, and the bundled `modernc.org/sqlite`
   is well past that.

### Head/tail split — sliding, tail-weighted

The longer a session ran, the less its opening predicts its outcome: sessions
drift, and the ending is where the conclusion lives. So the head share shrinks as
the session grows past budget:

```
head_share = clamp(0.5 * RECAP_INPUT_BUDGET / total_chars, 0.15, 0.5)
tail_share = 1 - head_share
```

| total | head / tail |
|---|---|
| 1× budget | 50% / 50% |
| 2× budget | 25% / 75% |
| 10× budget | 15% / 85% (floor) |

The 0.15 floor keeps some opening context at any length — a recap that never says
what the session set out to do is not a recap. `total_chars` comes from a
`SELECT sum(length(content))` over the same filtered set, so the split is computed
before any content is fetched.

---

## The model call

Route through `internal_claude.run_internal_claude` (`src/endless/internal_claude.py`).
**Never hand-roll a `subprocess.run(["claude", ...])`.** That helper sets
`ENDLESS_NO_HOOKS=true`, which is the entire defense against E-1470 — a headless
`claude -p` inheriting the caller's `TMUX_PANE`, registering a fresh session UUID,
and the pane-collision rule then marking the CALLING live session `ended`, which
broke `endless session id` and `task add` until the next Stop hook. Recap was one
of the two original callers that hit it.

```python
internal_claude.run_internal_claude(
    prompt,
    timeout=RECAP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,      # 120 — input is far larger than triage's
    model=config.internal_model("recap"),
    effort="low",
)
```

Add to `config.INTERNAL_MODEL_DEFAULTS`:

```python
"recap": "haiku",
```

A recap is compression, not judgment, so it sits with `verb_check` (haiku) rather
than `triage` (sonnet). Per-project and per-user override come free from
`internal_model`.

**Failure is loud, not fail-open.** Triage fails open because it is a background
sweep whose worst case is the status quo. This is an explicit command the user is
waiting on, so a missing `claude`, a timeout, or a non-zero exit raises a
`ClickException` naming the cause. Nothing is cached on failure.

### Prompt

Ask for 1–3 sentences of plain prose answering *what was this session working on,
and where did it end up*. No preamble, no markdown headings, no bullet list — the
result has to survive being truncated into a `session list` Title cell.

---

## Storage — ONE field, named `recap`

`sessions.summary` is renamed to `sessions.recap`. It is not joined by a second
column; there is exactly one "what is this session about" field.

E-1906 was supposed to make this rename and did not — it dropped `needs_recap`
and `summary_seq` but left `summary` in place, contrary to the requirement. This
task finishes that. Adding a *new* `recap` column beside `summary` (as the first
draft of this plan proposed) would have entrenched the duplication rather than
removing it: both fields answer the same question about the same session.

The two writers are then two qualities of the same value:

| Written by | When | `recap_at` |
|---|---|---|
| `seedRecapIfEmpty` (transcript parse) | first assistant response, if empty | NULL |
| `session recap` | on demand, from the whole conversation | set |

`recap_at IS NULL` therefore means "cheap seeded placeholder, never generated" and
is the discriminator wherever the distinction matters. A generated recap
overwrites a seeded one; a seeded one never overwrites anything (the writer is
`IfEmpty` and stays that way).

Columns after this task:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `recap TEXT` | the text (seeded placeholder or generated) |
| `recap_at TEXT` | when GENERATED; NULL for a seeded placeholder |
| `recap_watermark_id INTEGER` | `MAX(session_messages.id)` at generation time |

Staleness is **derived at read time**, never stored-and-cleared, so there is no
write-path touchpoint in the Go hook at all:

```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM session_messages
 WHERE session_id = ? AND role = 'user' AND id > recap_watermark_id
```

…excluding known boilerplate (below). Stale when that count `>= RECAP_STALE_TURNS`, which is **4** (Mike specified
"3 to 5"; 4 is the midpoint, held in one named constant so it is tunable without
a hunt). A *turn* is a **user** message — the unit a human perceives as a turn,
and the one that does not inflate with tool_use noise.

This is knowingly the mechanism E-1906 removed. Its change file describes
`summary_seq` as *"the recap watermark (the count of user messages at the last
recap, used to decide whether enough new ones had accrued)"*. The watermark was
sound; what E-1906 removed was the **automatic background generator** wrapped
around it, on the premise that one session maps to one task — the premise a
task-less session violates. So: reinstate the watermark, never the generator.

Two deliberate differences from the dropped column: the name is
`recap_watermark_id`, not `summary_seq`, so it cannot be mistaken for the old one;
and it stores a message **id** rather than a count, which stays correct if rows
are ever backfilled or deleted.

### Schema mechanics

Declare the final shape in `internal/schema/schema.sql` **and** ship a change file
(`internal/schema/changes/e-1925-rename-summary-to-recap.sql`):

```sql
ALTER TABLE sessions RENAME COLUMN summary TO recap;
ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN recap_at TEXT;
ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN recap_watermark_id INTEGER;
```

schema.sql alone is not sufficient, and this is the trap: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT
EXISTS sessions` no-ops on a populated DB, so an existing ledger would keep
`summary` and never gain the new columns. Same two-part pattern as E-1683's
`do_order` and E-1914's `session_hidden_tasks`.

The rename preserves existing data — every current `summary` value becomes a
seeded placeholder recap with `recap_at` NULL, which is exactly what it is.

`src/endless/db.py`'s legacy `_migrate` adds a `summary` column to very old DBs
(`db.py:382`). Leave that alone: it reproduces a historical shape, and this change
file then renames it. Same rule E-1906 applied to the e-1568 change file.

### Rename every reader

The column is read in more places than its name suggests. All of these move:

| Site | What it does with it |
|---|---|
| `internal/monitor/transcript.go:257` | the writer (`setSummaryIfEmpty` → `seedRecapIfEmpty`) |
| `internal/monitor/live_sessions.go:65` | carried on every live-session record |
| `internal/monitor/session_nav.go:140-141` | labels BOTH endpoints of every `session trail` edge |
| `src/endless/session_cmd.py:761` | the `Not logged in%` exclusion in `session list` |
| `src/endless/session_cmd.py:778, 812` | `session list` query + its `--json` field |
| `src/endless/session_cmd.py:1239` | live-session record passthrough |
| `src/endless/session_cmd.py:1576, 1598, 1617` | `session show` display + `--json` |

`session list --json` and `session show --json` rename their `summary` key to
`recap`. That is an intentional shape change: the field's meaning is being
unified, and leaving a `summary` key over a `recap` column would reintroduce the
confusion this task exists to end.

---

## Fix the byte-slicing truncation while renaming the writer

`setSummaryIfEmpty` (`internal/monitor/transcript.go:257`) currently corrupts
UTF-8, and it is live on every new session — not historical damage:

```go
cutoff := 200
for i := cutoff; i > 100; i-- {
    if summary[i] == '.' || summary[i] == '!' || summary[i] == '?' { cutoff = i + 1; break }
}
summary = summary[:cutoff]           // byte index into a UTF-8 string
```

Indexing a Go string yields a **byte**, so both the scan and the cut operate on
bytes. When no `.`/`!`/`?` falls between bytes 101–200, `cutoff` stays 200 and the
slice lands wherever byte 200 lands — splitting a multi-byte codepoint and writing
invalid UTF-8. (The punctuation hits are safe by accident: a single byte can only
equal `.` on an ASCII char.) One row in the real ledger is already damaged this
way, and every new session whose first assistant response exceeds 200 bytes
without punctuation in that window can produce another.

**The fix itself belongs to E-1985**, not here. That task owns truncation
correctness across all three byte-slicing sites (this one, the 500-char tool_use
cap 55 lines away, and `jobs/run.go`), adds the shared rune-safe helper they all
call, and repairs the rows already damaged. Two tasks carrying the same fix would
conflict on the same function.

What this task owes E-1985 is only the rename: `seedRecapIfEmpty` must call the
shared helper rather than re-deriving a cut. Whichever lands second rebases over
the other — they touch the same function, so expect that and do not try to avoid
it by duplicating the fix.

**Also correct the comment E-1914 landed in `src/endless/db.py`.** It attributes
this to "the recap generator removed in E-1906" and calls it "inert historical
damage no current code can add to". Both halves are wrong: the writer is
`setSummaryIfEmpty`/`seedRecapIfEmpty` in the transcript parser, it is live, and
the damage is 56× wider than the one row that comment implies (E-1985 measured it
across `session_messages`). The lenient `text_factory` stays — it is the right
defense for damage no fix can retroactively repair — but its rationale must name
the real writer. Correcting it here is fine since this task already edits that
function's name; correcting it in E-1985 is equally fine. Do not do both.

---

## Interaction with `session list`

- A **fresh, GENERATED** recap (`recap_at IS NOT NULL`) may fill the Title cell of
  a **task-less** row. A seeded placeholder does NOT qualify: the rule is that the
  listing shows a recap only when `session recap` has actually produced one, and a
  200-character slice of the first assistant response is not that.
- Only under `--all`. E-1914 omits task-less rows by default and that rule is
  unchanged: row inclusion must stay a function of the data, not of cache state.
- **Never generate on read.** `session list` renders up to `--limit` rows; a
  generate-on-read fallback would fan out one `claude -p` per blank row — exactly
  the automatic background behavior E-1906 removed.
- A **stale** cached recap renders as blank, not as text. A listing is a glance
  surface, and a recap that no longer describes the session is worse than an empty
  cell; the user refreshes with `session recap`. This also avoids inventing a
  per-cell staleness marker in a table that has no per-cell styling.
- A task-BEARING row is untouched — the task title wins, always.

---

## Non-goals

- **No automatic generation, ever.** Not on `task add`, not from a job, not on
  read, not from the prompt hook. Every path is user-invoked.
- **Does not remove the seeded placeholder.** `seedRecapIfEmpty` keeps running on
  transcript parse. Its unique load-bearing job is the error/login **auto-hide** —
  it is the only code that spots a first response starting `Not logged in` or
  `Error:` and sets `hidden = 1`, keeping dead login-failure sessions out of
  `session list`. Deleting it would silently retire that.
- No recap surface beyond `session recap`, the `session list --all` fallback, and
  the existing label sites the rename carries over.

---

## Verification

Write `tests/tasks/e-1925-verify.sh`, isolated exactly as `e-1914-verify.sh` is
(throwaway git repo as project root under a temp dir, own `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and
`XDG_CACHE_HOME`, worktree binary on PATH, no real DB/ledger/cache touched).

**No check may invoke a model.** Seed `recap`/`recap_at`/`recap_watermark_id`
directly via SQL and assert cache-hit behavior; in pytest, stub
`internal_claude.run_internal_claude`. A verify script that calls Claude is
non-hermetic, slow, and bills the user to run its own tests.

Checks:

- The change file renames `summary` → `recap` and adds `recap_at` /
  `recap_watermark_id` on an existing `sessions` table; a re-apply is a recorded
  no-op (`"status":"skipped"`).
- **The rename preserves data**: a pre-existing `summary` value survives as
  `recap` with `recap_at` NULL (a seeded placeholder), and the row's `hidden` flag
  is untouched.
- **No `summary` reference survives** anywhere in `internal/` or `src/endless/`
  outside the change files and the legacy `db.py` migrator — asserted by grep, so
  a missed reader cannot pass silently.
- **The UTF-8 truncation is fixed**: a first assistant response with a multi-byte
  character straddling byte 200 and no `.`/`!`/`?` in bytes 101–200 yields valid
  UTF-8. Go unit test, driven directly against `seedRecapIfEmpty`.
- The error/login **auto-hide still fires**: a first response starting
  `Not logged in` sets `hidden = 1`.
- A seeded placeholder (`recap_at IS NULL`) is NOT rendered by
  `session list --all`; a generated one is.
- `recap` resolves `ES-NNN`, a bare integer, a UUID prefix, and `E-NNN` (task →
  most-recent session with messages).
- A second call inside the watermark is served from cache and makes no model call.
- After `RECAP_STALE_TURNS` new **user** messages the cache reads stale.
- After exactly `RECAP_STALE_TURNS - 1` it does **not** — the boundary, asserted
  explicitly.
- New `tool_use` and `assistant` messages do **not** advance staleness; only
  `user` messages do.
- Input selection excludes `tool_use` and the boilerplate patterns, and over
  `RECAP_INPUT_BUDGET` applies the head+tail elision (assert on the assembled
  prompt, not on model output).
- **The budget is enforced by the query**: seed a session far over budget and
  assert the number of rows the query RETURNS is bounded — not merely that the
  assembled prompt is. A regression that filters in Python would pass a
  prompt-only assertion.
- The sliding split behaves: at ~1× budget the head/tail shares are even; at 10×
  the head is at its 0.15 floor.
- A boilerplate `user` message does NOT advance the staleness count, while a real
  one does.
- `--refresh` regenerates regardless of freshness.
- A missing `claude` produces a clear error and caches nothing.
- A session with no messages errors rather than calling the model.
- `session list --all` renders a fresh cached recap in a task-less row's Title
  cell, renders blank when stale or absent, and never invokes the model.
- The implementation routes through `internal_claude` — assert the source contains
  no direct `subprocess` invocation of `claude`, so a hand-rolled call (and E-1470
  with it) cannot creep back in.

Alongside the script: pytest for ref resolution, input assembly/elision, the
watermark boundary, and the failure paths.

## Docs

Add `session recap` to `docs/guide/appendix-a.md` (it is a human-run interactive
command) and reference it from the **Quieting a noisy status view** neighborhood
in `docs/guide/sessions.md`, where task-less sessions are already discussed.

# Analysis

## Why this is being asked now

E-1898 rebuilt session→pane binding onto a `processes` table keyed on
`(kind, server_uuid, address)`, because the old `sessions.process` string (a
bare tmux pane id) is not unique across tmux server lifetimes — the root cause
of the 2026-08-05 incident that nulled live pane bindings project-wide.

`channels` keys on that SAME string (`INSERT INTO channels (process, port, pid,
created_at)`, `DELETE FROM channels WHERE process=?`, `SELECT port, pid FROM
channels WHERE process=?` — internal/monitor/session.go:274-308). E-1898
deliberately left it alone rather than migrate a surface believed dead, so
after E-1898 lands `channels` is the last consumer of the old non-unique key.

## The assumption that needs confirming first

"channels is vestigial" is Mike's read, and it may be wrong. The
`endless-channel` MCP server is still wired into live Claude sessions — its
instructions ship in the session system prompt:

    Events from Endless arrive as <channel source="endless-channel" ...>.
    When you see event_type="message", run: endless channel inbox

So the surface is at minimum still *installed*. Whether it is ever *exercised*
is the empirical question.

## What to brainstorm

1. **Confirm the premise.** Does anything read/write `channels`? Is the MCP
   server ever actually invoked? Check the ledger, the errors log, and whether
   any session has ever run `endless channel inbox` unprompted.

2. **Re-read the MCP standard.** It has changed recently; capabilities that
   were impossible when endless-channel was built may now be available.
   Reference Mike watched: https://youtube.com/watch?v=oqp6D-ugtX4

3. **Evaluate `SendMessage`.** Claude Code exposes a SendMessage tool that
   continues a previously spawned agent by ID/name with its context intact.
   That may be a better transport for inter-session communication than a
   bespoke MCP server plus a port/pid table — it needs no listener, no port
   allocation, and no process-keyed row that can go stale.

4. **Decide.** Three live options:
   - retire `channels` + the MCP server outright;
   - migrate `channels.process` onto `processes.process_id` (only worth it if
     the surface is genuinely used);
   - rebuild inter-session comms on SendMessage and retire the rest.

## Out of scope

Implementation. The outcome is a decision plus a follow-on retirement or
design task.

# Scope extension — the false-UNLANDED case (added 2026-08-10)

E-1940 covers two defects in `UnsettledDetail.Unsettled()`. There is a third,
opposite one, in the same function, and it has a second consumer.

## The defect

`internal/monitor/worktree_unsettled.go:172` runs
`git rev-list main..HEAD --count` and treats any non-zero result as unlanded.
Because `worktree land` REBASES onto main, a landed branch's commits are
rewritten — the originals stay on the branch and are unreachable from main by
construction. So every correctly-landed worktree reads "unlanded" forever, and
the count grows without bound as main advances.

Observed on E-1845: `task unsettled` reported "unlanded (161 commits)" for a
task that landed on 2026-08-05. Its commit IS on main as 2776f5a5 (same subject,
different SHA from the branch's ed41f1d2); the branch's merge-base with main is
1005 commits back. Most of the 161 were never E-1845's work at all — they were
main's commits at worktree-creation time, since rewritten.

This is worse than a wrong label: the printed fix is
`endless worktree land E-NNNN`, which would replay 161 stale commits onto a main
that already has the content.

## Second consumer — likely the worktree-backlog cause

`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go:220` runs the identical probe as reap
criterion 4. Criterion 1 already requires a `task_landings` row. So a landed
worktree passes 1 and is rejected by 4 — it can never be reaped, and landed
worktrees accumulate indefinitely.

## The fix

`task_landings` already records the landing (task_id, merge_commit_sha,
landed_at) and is already read by the reaper. Credit it: the commits a recorded
landing accounts for are not unlanded, whatever the branch's SHA divergence
says.

Note that `git branch --merged <base>` does NOT work here — a rebase-landed
branch is not an ancestor of the base. E-1308 proposes that probe for a related
case and would hit the same wall; the recorded landing is the reliable signal
for both.

### Anchor the credit on the BRANCH, not on the base (revised 2026-08-25)

This section originally said: a task whose recorded sha is reachable from main
is landed. Measurement against this repo falsified that before implementation.

- Most recorded landing shas ARE reachable from main, but a substantial
  minority are not — main's own history has been rewritten more than once, and
  a rewrite detaches every landing recorded before it.
- E-1889, the case this analysis was written from, is one of them. NONE of its
  recorded shas is reachable from main, so the reachable-from-main rule would
  have left the motivating symptom exactly as broken as it found it.
- Every affected branch, without exception, still reaches its own recorded
  landing sha. The branch is the durable anchor; the base is not.

So the primitive is: **unlanded = the commits reachable from HEAD that are
reachable neither from the base branch nor from any recorded landing.**

    git rev-list --count --ignore-missing HEAD ^<base> ^<landing>...

Excluding the base as well as the landings is what keeps the count honest when
the base has moved on: it counts only commits that are genuinely this branch's
and genuinely not in. `--ignore-missing` covers a landing sha that is no longer
an object in this clone; it cannot mask a bad base, because the resolver only
ever returns a branch it verified exists.

Applied to the affected worktrees, every false count collapsed to zero while
the branches carrying real post-landing commits kept theirs.

Verify with a rebase-landed worktree: `unsettled` must report settled, the ◆
marker must clear, and the reaper must consider it reapable. Verify the
distinction that motivated the revision by rewriting the base's history
afterwards — the verdict must not move.


# Consolidated from E-1308 (declined 2026-08-10)

E-1308 was a third symptom of this same cause. Its case: `worktree land E-NNNN`
when the worktree is GONE reports "No endless-managed worktree for E-NNN",
implying the work is lost. It isn't — the branch landed and the reaper later
removed the directory and branch once the `task_landings` row aged past
worktree_ttl.

Required behavior, carried over verbatim: report
"E-NNN already landed (commit <sha>); nothing to do" instead of the error, and
fall back to today's message only when the work is genuinely unaccounted for.

E-1308 proposed detecting this with `git branch --merged main`. That does not
work: `land` rebases, so a landed branch is not an ancestor of main and the
probe fails for exactly the case it targets. The recorded landing is the only
reliable signal — the same fix the unsettled probe and the reaper need.

## The three consumers, one primitive

| Consumer | Current probe | Symptom |
|---|---|---|
| `worktree_unsettled.go:172` | `rev-list main..HEAD --count` | false "unlanded (N commits)" forever after landing |
| `reap_worktrees.go:220` | same | landed worktrees never reaped; they accumulate |
| `worktree land` (gone worktree) | none / proposed `branch --merged` | "No endless-managed worktree", implying work lost |

Build the landed-state determination once — the commits a recorded landing
accounts for are not unlanded, regardless of branch SHA divergence — and route
all three through it. See the revision above for the exact primitive.
