invalidation was safe there — a reissued %422 really does get its own processes
row. The second is a claim about READERS, and no reader implements it.

## Where it breaks

src/endless/session_cmd.py, _resolve_companion:

    siblings = [
        c for c in live
        if c.get("pane_id") in window_panes and c.get("pane_id") != my_pane
    ]

`pane_id` here is the ADDRESS STRING, matched against the address strings tmux
reports for the current window. Two sessions bound to different processes rows
that happen to share "%422" both land in `siblings`. The function then refuses
an ambiguous set rather than ordering it:

    click.echo("Multiple sibling Claude panes in this window:")
    ... raise SystemExit(1)

So the write side stopped cleaning up on the promise that the read side would
disambiguate, and the read side neither disambiguates nor orders.

## Evidence

  id    session_id     state    process_id  address  last_activity
  976   42f7dd92-...   working  91          %422     2026-08-06T05:45:41
  1152  a86f2bc3-...   idle     185         %422     2026-08-26T03:38:48

Both non-ended, both reading as %422, different processes rows. `esu` in that
window refuses. Neither row is corrupt: 976 accurately records a session that
ran on an August %422 whose tmux server is long gone.

## What NOT to do

Do not "end" the older row. It is not a live session that can be ended — it is a
record of one that already finished, and ending it via the SessionEnd hook is
simulating a lifecycle event on something that has no lifecycle left. That
treats a read bug as a data problem and destroys accurate history to do it.
(This mistake was made once already while diagnosing; it is recorded here so the
implementor does not repeat it.)

## Two shapes, either of which closes it

- Compare identity the way the writer records it: carry the processes row (or
  server_uuid) through `session-query list-live` into the companion dicts, and
  match on (server_uuid, address) instead of the bare string. This is the
  faithful reading of E-1898 — pane identity is a pair, so every comparison of
  it should be a pair.
- Or implement the half E-1898 promised: when a sibling set is ambiguous, order
  by last_activity and take the newest. Cheaper, and it also covers a genuine
  same-server collision, which the identity fix does not.

The two are not exclusive and the second is a reasonable backstop for the first.

## Blast radius

Every companion-resolving surface, not just `esu`: `session use`, `session cd`,
`session show`, `session history` with no argument — anything that calls
`_resolve_companion` with no session_ref. The failure is a hard refusal, so a
long-lived tmux server that reissues pane addresses gradually makes those
commands unusable in exactly the windows that have been open longest.

## PRODUCT

Nothing here is Endless-specific. Any project whose sessions are pinned to tmux
panes accumulates rows for panes that no longer exist, and tmux reissues
addresses on server restart. A downstream user hits this the first time they
restart their tmux server with sessions recorded — with no verify scripts and no
self-dev worktrees involved.

fields.text:
Implements ED-1571, the one part of E-1944's outcome that was decided and never
filed.

Under ED-1567 a CANDIDATE binary may never migrate the real ledger. But
`_resolve_land_endless_go` (src/endless/worktree_cmd.py:1950) hands a self_dev
land the WORKTREE's own binary, and E-1664 made that an invariant rather than a
choice: "the only binary whose embedded schema/enums match the just-written rows
is the worktree's own build — never the not-yet-refreshed global." That binary is
a candidate by `candidateBuild()`'s definition — its path carries the worktree
marker.

So the moment E-2020 lands, a self_dev land has no binary permitted to apply its
own migration: the installed one does not carry it, the worktree one is not
allowed to run it. That is why this exists, and it is why it blocks E-2020 rather
than following it.

Build a migration-only executable from the landing branch, carrying the
migration set and nothing else. It performs migration steps in FULL — DDL plus
the DML those migrations define: enum seed rows, backfills, the INSERT ... SELECT
of a table rebuild. What it excludes is application runtime: it never serves a
hook, never runs a task command, never touches business data outside a
migration. That exclusion is what makes it immune to the
binary-expects-a-schema failure, because it has no expectations beyond the
migrations it carries.

`worktree land` builds and invokes it at the existing apply step (E-1941's
ordering: after the ff-merge, before `_record_landing`) instead of calling
`endless db apply-change` with the worktree binary.

Scope is self_dev ONLY. Every other project has one installed binary and no land
at all, so it carries and applies its own migrations under ED-1570; no separate
executable exists there, and nothing in this task may assume one does.

Two things to settle while planning, not now:
- `_record_landing` still runs on the worktree binary for the same E-1664
  reason, against a ledger this executable just migrated. Whether that remains
  correct under ED-1570's exact-agreement rule needs an answer.
- E-1709 rebuilds the worktree binary before land uses it. If the migration
  executable replaces that usage, E-1709's rebuild may be serving only
  `_record_landing` afterward.

# Verification

`.endless/tasks/e-2088/`, run only through the runner — `just verify E-2088` or
`endless task verify E-2088`. Never executed directly: `_guard.sh` refuses that,
and a suite exercising land-time migration against your real `HOME` is precisely
the run that must not happen.

Shape: a `verify.toml` whose first `[[check]]` is a `gotest` runner over the
executable's unit tests — the fail-fast half — plus a `verify.sh` driving a land
end-to-end. The script sources `_harness.sh`, opens with the DO-NOT-EDIT header
naming E-2088, uses `section` / `assert_eq` / `assert_contains`, and calls
`summary` last; shipped fixtures are read from `$ENDLESS_VERIFY_DIR`.

The runner's temp `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` are what make it safe to run a
real migration, so nothing here passes `--config-dir`.

1. The executable applies a migration end to end against a throwaway database:
   version before, version after, and the DML the migration defines actually ran
   (seed rows present, backfill applied), not just the DDL.
2. It refuses to do anything that is not a migration — assert the binary exposes
   no hook, task, or query surface, since "it never serves a hook" is the
   property that makes it immune to the binary-expects-a-schema failure and is
   otherwise untested.
3. `worktree land` invokes it at E-1941's apply step, between the ff-merge and
   `_record_landing`, and a failure there produces the existing post-merge
   message telling the operator to re-run rather than restore.
4. Landing a branch with no migration does not build or invoke it.
5. In a non-self_dev project no such executable exists and the installed binary
   applies its own migrations under ED-1570 — assert the self_dev-only scope
   rather than assuming it.
6. The worktree binary is still what `_record_landing` runs, against the ledger
   this executable just migrated. Assert that pairing works, because it is the
   half of E-1664 that survives E-2088 and nothing else covers it.

Coverage that must outlive the land is mirrored into the durable Go suite —
assertion 2's "no application surface" check in particular, since it is a
property of the build that would otherwise erode silently.

# Plan — Bracket an agent's CLI refusal with a repeated one-line verdict

## The failure this fixes, measured

`endless task update E-2093 --title <104 chars>` refuses with 17 lines on
stderr. The verdict is line 2:

    1
    2   Error: Title is 104 characters; max is 100.
    3
    4-16  (fourteen lines of guidance on how to shape a title)
    17

An agent piping `2>&1 | tail -3` keeps lines 15-17 — the tail of the guidance
block. The one line that names the constraint is the one line a small window
cannot see.

What that cost, in one session, across `task add` and `task update` (both call
`validate_title`, task_cmd.py:312, from :2252 and :4624):

1. `task add`, title 107 chars — refused. Read the fragment as a SHAPE
   complaint, reworded, and passed at 94 by accident while believing the shape
   was the problem.
2. `task add`, description 1032 > 1024 — refused.
3. `task update --title`, 141 chars — refused.
4. `task update --title`, 107 chars — refused. Thirty-four characters shaved
   between attempts 3 and 4 without ever reading the number the error stated
   both times. That is editing toward a constraint rather than reading it.
5. `--title "test"` written to a LIVE task to probe the validator — a mutation
   of real state to learn what the error had already said twice.
6. `--description-file` with newlines — refused.

Five refusals and one junk write, all against a message that was correct,
complete, and on stderr the whole time.

## The change

The bracket renders when EITHER an agent is running the command or a human
asked to see what one sees:

    agent_env.present() or agent_help.agent_view_requested()

Both, not one. An earlier draft of this plan said "NOT the `--agent-view` flag,
because an agent will never pass a flag it does not know it needs." The premise
is true and the conclusion is wrong: `--agent-view` is not a detection
mechanism, it is a HUMAN's override for previewing agent-facing output while
debugging. Excluding it would take that away, and the whole point of the flag is
to make output like this inspectable.

`agent_help._should_augment()` already composes exactly this predicate, for
exactly this reason — its docstring reads "An agent is reading this help, or a
human asked to see what one sees." Reuse or extract it; do NOT write a fourth
spelling of the question. That module's history is two consolidations of this
same duplication (E-1966 folded in a private `is_claude_code_agent()`, E-2006
folded in the last `!= UNKNOWN` comparison), and adding another would undo
them.

So refusals are emitted as:

    <verdict line>
    <blank>
    … today's guidance block, unchanged …
    <blank>
    <verdict line>          ← byte-identical to the first

The two lines are IDENTICAL, deliberately. Split them — verdict first, remedy
last — and `head -N` yields the problem without the fix while `tail -N` yields
the fix without the problem. Identical means whichever end survives is
sufficient alone, and seeing both reads as one repeat rather than two findings.

Length is unconstrained: `head`/`tail` are line-based, so a 200-character line
survives whole. Keep it to one dense line rather than a paragraph — a paragraph
invites the same skimming that caused this.

## What the verdict line must carry

Ordered by what would have stopped the failure above at attempt 3:

1. **Measured numbers, never an adjective.** `title 107>100 chars`, not "too
   long". The number is what makes the correction computable.
2. **A fixed sentinel plus the command and field**: `ENDLESS-ERROR task add:`.
   A bare error line read out of context does not say what produced it.
3. **Where the overflow goes**, not merely "shorten": `long-form goes in
   --analysis (rationale) or --text (plan); the title names WHAT`. Without
   this an agent mangles the field to fit instead of relocating the content —
   which is what happened.
4. **Whether anything changed**: `Nothing was created.` A refusal leaves an
   agent wondering whether it partially applied; that uncertainty is part of
   what produced the junk write in step 5.
5. **Every problem at once**, not the first. See below.

Deliberately NOT in it: the template, the HOW-vs-WHAT rationale, the examples.
Those are worth having and worth losing.

Not JSON, not key=value. A stable prefix and a plain sentence parses fine and
stays readable when a human hits it.

Worked example, ~170 characters:

    ENDLESS-ERROR task add: title 107>100 chars; description 1032>1024 chars. Long-form goes in --analysis (rationale) or --text (plan); the title names WHAT. Nothing was created.

## Collect every problem before refusing

Today `validate_title` raises on the first failure, so the sequence is: fix the
title, resubmit, discover the description. Steps 1-2 and 3-6 above are both
that shape. The validators for title, description and analysis on `task add`
and `task update` should accumulate their findings and refuse once, with all of
them in the verdict line.

Scope this to those validators on those two verbs. It is not a project-wide
refactor of every ClickException.

## Shape it as a shared helper

A rule that reaches two messages is not a convention. Add one helper — e.g.
`agent_error(summary: str, guidance: str)` beside the existing agent-facing
machinery — that renders the bracketed form when `agent_env.present()` and
today's plain form otherwise. Adopt it first in the title/description
validators, and document it so a new refusal reaches for it.

## Humans see no change

The duplication is agent-only. A person reading the full message in a terminal
gets today's output byte for byte. This is a requirement, not a nicety: a
repeated long line is noise to a reader who was never going to truncate it.

## Boundaries

- Does NOT touch which stream errors go to. They are already on stderr, already
  complete; the agent truncated them. Nothing about stdout/stderr changes.
- Does NOT add a PreToolUse matcher against `2>&1 | tail`. That was considered
  and rejected: it targets a correlate, would not catch `| tail -N` over a long
  stdout report, and would fire on `go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -30`, which is
  correct usage (a failing `go test` writes to stdout; a failing `endless`
  leaves stdout empty — measured).
- Does NOT reorder the existing guidance. The bracket makes order irrelevant.

## PRODUCT

Nothing here is Endless-specific. Every project using Endless is driven by
agents that pipe and truncate CLI output, and every CLI puts its verdict first
and its teaching after. The agent-gated bracket belongs in the shipped CLI, and
the detection signal (`agent_env.present()`) already ships.

## Verify — .endless/tasks/e-<id>/verify.sh

1. Fail-fast unit gate: the Python tests this task adds.
2. Under a simulated agent env, a refusal's first and last lines are
   byte-identical.
3. That line carries the measured numbers, the command, the field, the
   destination for long-form content, and the no-change statement.
4. `… 2>&1 | tail -3` and `… 2>&1 | head -3` of the same refusal EACH contain
   the verdict — the two ends of the property.
5. With no agent env AND no --agent-view, the message is byte-identical to
   today's: no duplication, no sentinel.
6. With no agent env but --agent-view passed, the bracket IS rendered — the
   flag's purpose is to let a human see what an agent sees, so a version that
   only fires on detection would make agent-facing output the one thing
   --agent-view cannot show.
7. A call that violates title AND description limits at once names both in one
   verdict line and refuses once.
8. A refused call mutated nothing.

fields.description: endless session resume execs 'claude --resume' in the current pane but never sets the tmux window options that task spawn sets (@endless_task_id, @endless_project_id, @endless_spawned_by), and relies on the hook's per-event self-heal for @endless_session_uuid. So a resumed pane lacks the window identity that _current_pane_task() (the E-1968 clobber guard, session_cmd.py:605) and session-status focal resolution read from @endless_task_id. Fix: on resume, set the window options on the current pane to match spawn. Long-standing gap since resume was introduced (eb2206ad), not a regression.
fields.text:
# Make `session resume` re-bind the tmux window options on the current pane

## Problem
`resume_session` (src/endless/session_cmd.py:558) resolves the target, then
`os.chdir(worktree)` + `os.execvp("claude", ["claude","--resume",uuid])`
(session_cmd.py:634-637). It sets NO tmux window options. So a pane resumed into
lacks the `@endless_*` window identity that a spawned window carries.

The four options and who sets them today:
- `@endless_task_id`, `@endless_project_id`, `@endless_spawned_by` — written ONLY
  by the spawn launcher (internal/spawnlaunchcmd/spawn_launch.go:39 ->
  tmux_driver.go:92-97). Never on the resume path.
- `@endless_session_uuid` — written by the hook every event
  (internal/hookcmd/claude.go:287, setTmuxSessionUUID), meant to self-heal.

## Why it matters
A resumed pane with no `@endless_task_id` silently loses:
- `_current_pane_task()` — the E-1968 clobber guard in resume itself
  (session_cmd.py:605) can't see the pane's held task.
- `session status` focal-task resolution, which reads the window's
  `@endless_task_id`.

## Fix
On the resume path, before `os.execvp`, set the window options on the current
pane to match a spawned window:
- `@endless_task_id` = resolved task id
- `@endless_project_id` = resolved project id
- `@endless_session_uuid` = resolved session uuid (set it here rather than
  depend on the hook's per-event self-heal, which is more fragile — see below)

Open design question for the implementer: `@endless_spawned_by` means "which
session spawned this window." A resumed pane was NOT spawned by `task spawn`, so
setting it is debatable — likely omit it (or record a resume-origin marker).
Decide during implementation; task_id/project_id/session_uuid are the clear wins.

## Not a regression
Verified via git pickaxe: `git log -S 'set -w' -- src/endless/session_cmd.py`
and `-S '@endless_task_id' -- …` both return zero commits. resume has been
option-less since it was introduced (eb2206ad). None of E-2074/E-2102/E-1918/
E-1851/E-1898/E-1976 touched the resume/hook option writes. This is a
long-standing design gap, not a recent breakage.

## Related but SEPARATE (do not fold in)
A distinct symptom was observed alongside this: `@endless_session_uuid` absent
even though the hook should self-heal it every event. That points at the hook
not reaching claude.go:287 for the affected session (candidates: the
`shouldSkipForWorktree` early return at claude.go:232, or a stale/missing
worktree-local hook wiring in that worktree's .claude/settings.json). That is a
hook-firing/wiring diagnostic, not confirmed as a code defect, and is NOT part
of this task. Setting session_uuid on the resume path (above) makes resume
robust to it regardless.

## Origin
Found while debugging a `session resume` in an unrelated session's worktree; the
task that session happened to be under (E-1834) is NOT related to this bug.

fields.analysis:
## Scope

Implements ED-1587. Three pieces, in order:

1. **Construction.** `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py:1546` and `:1653` build
   `f"task/{task_id}-{slug}"`. Both become `f"task/{task_id}"`. Whatever
   computes the slug for this purpose goes with them if nothing else uses it.

2. **Migration of the ~139 existing branches.** They are local-only — no
   remote, no PRs, no CI — so `git branch -m task/<id>-<slug> task/<id>` is
   cheap and safe. Each has a live worktree checked out on it, so the rename
   must go through git (which updates the worktree's HEAD), never by editing
   refs. Decide and state whether this is a one-shot `db apply-change`-style
   step or a resolver that accepts both forms during a transition; a one-shot
   rename is simpler and this project has no other clones to coordinate with.
   Sessions are live in some of these worktrees, so the rename must not run
   under them unannounced — gate it the way the reaper gates on
   `WorktreeInUse`, or require it to be run deliberately.

3. **Retire `task_landings.branch`.** Once the name is derivable the column is
   redundant. Two consequences worth doing in the same pass, because they are
   the reason the decision was made:
   - E-1719's record-only landing recorded no branch, which is why
     `maybeReapWorktree` scans it as `sql.NullString`. That case disappears.
   - E-2087 added a git fallback (`git symbolic-ref --short HEAD`) so a
     worktree with no landing row could still have its branch deleted at reap
     time, plus a carve-out that deliberately does NOT apply the fallback to a
     NULL-branch landing row. Both go away: the reaper derives `task/<id>`
     from the task id it already has.

   The column also feeds `internal/monitor/session_notices.go` and the
   `task landed` surface; check every reader before dropping it, and prefer
   deriving over reading rather than leaving a second source of truth.

## Also update

- `ED-1167` — supersede it via `endless decision supersede`, not by editing it.
- The guide's worktree/branch prose, wherever it shows a slug branch name.
- Any test fixture that hardcodes a `task/<id>-<slug>` branch.

## Out of scope

A configurable branch pattern. ED-1587 rejects it explicitly and says why.

## What the column says today

`session status` renders one column between the task-type letter and the task
id (`unsettledMark`, internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go:1010, rendered
at :679). Two states: ◆ when the row's worktree is unsettled, blank otherwise.

## What it says after this change

Three states. The column answers "is there work product here, and where is
it?":

| Glyph | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| ◆ | work product, still outstanding | anything unsettled |
| ⊙ | **no work product yet** | never spawned (no worktree), **or** `underway` with a settled worktree |
| blank | work product, all of it landed | `unverified` + settled |

The two cases sharing ⊙ are deliberate and are the point of the task: a task
nobody has picked up and a task a session is sitting on that has produced
nothing are the same fact about the work. The reader does not need this column
to tell those apart — the action icon and the status already do — so it must
not try to.

## The rule, decided

**⊙ when the row's task status is `underway` or earlier and the worktree is not
unsettled.** Blank when the status is past `underway` (`unverified`,
`unreviewed`, `confirmed`, `assumed`, `completed`) and the worktree is not
unsettled. ◆ whenever the worktree is unsettled, unchanged and taking
precedence over both.

Status is the discriminator, not landing history. `task_landings` is not a
reliable record of what reached main — E-2087 measured branches whose content
is demonstrably on main with no landing row at all — and a git-side answer
(`git log <base> --grep "E-<id>:"`) would put a new probe on a per-row hot
path. Status is already on `SessionStatusRow`, costs nothing, and reproduces
every case above.

Its one known mis-signal, accepted: a task that lands mid-flight and keeps
working is `underway` with real landed work and wears ⊙. It is still true that
nothing is outstanding. Label the glyph in the legend by what it MEANS, not by
what it is derived from, so the derivation can be sharpened later without the
vocabulary changing.

## The glyph, decided

**⊙ (U+2299 CIRCLED DOT OPERATOR).**

- It shares the unsettledMark column with only ◆ and blank, so the sole
  within-column distinction is circle vs diamond — different silhouettes, which
  ◇ (U+25C7) would not have given.
- The other circled-operator glyphs — ⊗ blocked, ⏸ blocks, ⊘ hidden, ⊕ queued —
  live in `blockField`/`hiddenField`/`relationField`, rendered after the id and
  phase char (:679-682). Position disambiguates them from this column.
- Width: U+2299 is East Asian Ambiguous, the same class as the already-shipped
  ⊘. Add a width assertion beside `TestHiddenGlyphWidth` rather than assuming.
- Known co-occurrence, accepted: an untriaged row carries ◌ (`actTriage`) in
  column 1 and will usually also carry ⊙ here, so `◌ T⊙E-2107` puts two round
  glyphs on one line. They mean compatible things and sit in different columns.

## Constraints the column imposes

- Display width 1. The prefix is a fixed 13 columns and the alignment
  guarantee ⏚/⁇/◆ carry (E-1765) holds only if every state in the slot matches.
- `buildLegend` shows a decoration only when a row bears it; ⊙ follows that
  rule and is labelled there — suggested label: "not started".
- ◆ vetoes dimming (E-1707) because it means "still something to do". ⊙ means
  the opposite and must NOT veto dimming — a never-started `later` row should
  still read dim.
- The "no worktree" half of the signal is already computed:
  `monitor.UnsettledDetail.HasWorktree`. `SessionStatusRow` carries `Unsettled`
  today and needs the second flag filled by the same
  `AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` pass.

fields.description: replace_task at task_cmd.py:2146-2179 currently does raw SQL — both the task_deps INSERT and the UPDATE tasks SET status='obsolete'. This violates the events-authoritative invariant reaffirmed in declined E-993. Fixing the status-write half is unavoidable when adding --outcome and --status to task replace, since those flags must flow through events. Scope decision: fix the status-write half via update_plan; leave the task_deps INSERT for E-957's typed-link work, where it belongs. Documenting this scope call so future readers don't see it as scope creep.

Verb-check (task_cmd.py:257) and recap shell out to headless claude -p. Unsuppressed, each inherits the caller TMUX_PANE, gets a fresh session UUID, and its hook trips the collision UPDATE (session.go:271-283) that false-ends the live caller. Fix: ENDLESS_NO_HOOKS=true so endless-hook self-suppresses (plus --tools '' --no-session-persistence --mcp-config '' --strict-mcp-config --effort low). Rejected --bare: forces ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/apiKeyHelper auth and never reads OAuth/keychain, which this env lacks, so it would fail auth and silently break verb auto-registration. Rejected --session-id: if hooks fire, SessionEnd on the caller UUID still ends the caller; a fresh UUID just re-collides. Only ENDLESS_NO_HOOKS closes both paths.

payload.title: Run database backups on a schedule with tiered retention, not only before migrations
payload.description: Backups only run before a schema migration: _backup_db has exactly one caller, and the Go path fires only from the pre-apply step during land and from an explicit endless db backup. So the newest backup can be weeks old — it was nine days stale when it was needed. The docstring's 'if last backup is > 60 seconds old' reads like a frequency but is only a throttle on a rare event. Register a backup job in the internal/jobs registry the way triagejob and minimizerjob do, so session monitor fires it on a schedule, and replace the keep-last-60-by-count rotation with tiered retention: hourly for 24 hours, then daily for 30 days, then weekly for a year.
payload.analysis:
## Why this surfaced

A bulk edit needed undoing and the newest backup was nine days old. It was still
usable, but only by luck: nothing about the current design makes recency likely.

Evidence for the diagnosis, not just the symptom:

- `_backup_db` has one caller, commented "backup before any migration".
- The Go equivalent runs from the pre-apply step during land, and from an
  explicit `endless db backup`. Neither is a schedule.
- Sixty files on disk — the rotation cap — spanning three months. That is about
  one every day and a half, clustered around migrations rather than evenly.
- The newest is dated to the last schema change, which is exactly what
  backup-on-migration predicts.

The 60-second window in the docstring is a throttle so two migrations back to
back do not write two copies. It is not a cadence, and it reads like one.

## Time Machine is not the fallback

Worth recording, because it was tried first. A Time Machine snapshot of the live
database was torn — SQLite was mid-write, `PRAGMA integrity_check` failed, and
`.recover` reassembled rows wrongly: fields from one table appeared in another's
columns, and whole rows were missing. A filesystem-level copy of an open SQLite
database has no consistency guarantee.

The project's own backups are safe because they go through the SQLite backup API
and `VACUUM INTO`. That difference is the reason this job belongs in Endless
rather than being delegated to the machine's backup software.

## Shape

Follow the two jobs that already exist. A stable `JobName` (changing it orphans
the scheduling row and restarts history), a `Schedule` with an interval and a
`MaxBackoff`, registered so `session monitor` picks it up via the same RunDue
path. Unlike the model-calling jobs, this one costs no spend, so the interval is
governed by acceptable data loss, not by budget.

## Retention

Replaces keep-last-60-by-count, which is a count where it should be an age:

- hourly for 24 hours
- daily for 30 days
- weekly for a year

That is roughly 106 files at steady state. Retention must be evaluated by
timestamp tier, not list position, so a burst of migrations can no longer evict
the older tiers — the failure mode the current rotation has today.

triage.rationale: the schedule interval/trigger conditions for the new backup job and the exact tiered-retention pruning algorithm (e.g., how boundaries between hourly/daily/weekly buckets are chosen and enforced) are not specified.

fields.analysis:
# The primary defect: test 1 reads as a purity test

Bullet 1 — "Could it reasonably be done now, inside the work already underway?
Do it" — **was** in the handoff. It is not missing. It was read and rejected,
and the rejection was reasonable on the wording: "inside the work already
underway" is a **topical membership** question. Asked of a stray id in a guide
paragraph while the task was `verb update`, the honest answer is "no, that is
not part of this task's subject" — so the session falls to the next branch.

`docs/guide/tasks.md` then hardens the topical read rather than softening it:

> "Reasonably, inside the work already underway" is a real bound, not a
> license. A drive-by that is *unrelated* to what you are changing stays a
> separate task…

So the guide makes bullet 1 about **kinship** while ED-1550 makes filing about
**arithmetic** — the file-to-close ratio. For a cheap, unrelated fix those pull
opposite ways, and kinship wins because it is the test actually printed at the
decision point.

This is a repeat, not a one-off. The same reasoning — "it wasn't a *pure*
example of the other task" — has been given before as the justification for
filing rather than folding. Purity is the wrong axis. What matters is what the
fix costs to make and to review, and whether carrying it in this diff would
mislead a reviewer; not whether it is a clean instance of this task's category.

**Proposed:** bullet 1 states the axis and names the failure mode, e.g.

    - Could it reasonably be done now? Do it — note it in the commit message
      and say so in your reply. The test is COST, not kinship: how big is the
      fix, and would carrying it here mislead whoever reviews the diff. Do not
      let purity get in the way of proficiency — "not a pure example of this
      task" is not a reason to file. A one-line fix in a file you already have
      open is cheaper to make than the task row describing it.

That keeps the real bound (a large or risky unrelated change still splits out,
for diff, land-coupling and revert-blast-radius reasons) while removing the
category test that currently decides it.

# Folding in is not done until the plan records it

A session that folds discovered work into the task already underway must also
**amend that task's plan and/or outcome** to say so. The commit message and the
reply to the user are both transient: the commit is found only by someone
already reading that diff, and the reply is gone the moment the session is
archived. The task row is what posterity reads, and a task whose plan describes
only its original scope is a lie about what shipped under it — which is the
same defect that made "reopening shipped work forces a re-read of the whole
plan to find the new part" a rule in the first place.

So the do-it-now branch has three obligations, not two: do the work, note it in
the commit, **and record the grown scope on the task**.

**This has a trap that must be spelled out in the instruction.** Writing plan
text onto a task in a terminal status re-specs it:

    $ endless task update E-2114 --text-file plan.md
    • Status: assumed -> revisit
    E-2114 was 'assumed'; plan text changed → status set to revisit
    (pass --keep-status to suppress for a typo/formatting-only edit)

and `revisit` cannot go back: reachable from `revisit` are untriaged,
submitted, underway, declined, obsolete — **not** `assumed`. So a session that
obeys the new rule the obvious way destroys the verification state its user just
granted, and the only way back is a full claim/verify cycle the user has to
re-close. Hit live on E-2114 while writing this analysis.

The instruction must therefore carry `--keep-status`, not merely mention that
it exists — and it is worth asking whether recording delivered scope on a done
task should be a re-spec at all, or whether `--keep-status` is the wrong
default for a plan edit that only appends history.

# Secondary: the handoff drops the framing and the override

`docs/guide/tasks.md` opens the discovery section with **"Filing is one of four
answers, not the default"** and closes it with an override:

> One case overrides test 1's bound: a drive-by you genuinely cannot complete
> the task without — a broken build, **a test that fails for an unrelated
> reason**. Fix the minimum that unblocks you even when it is otherwise out of
> scope, and say so explicitly in your report.

`internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/_mechanics.tmpl:28-36` compresses the
four tests into three bullets and keeps neither. `otherwise file it` is left as
the terminal branch, and nothing puts the filing *decision* in front of the
user.

# The missing branch: ASK, don't decide

The branch to add is not "tell your user and file nothing". A session that
decides unilaterally not to file is as wrong as one that files reflexively —
it just fails in the direction that loses real findings silently instead of the
direction that inflates the backlog. The agent has the context to explain a
finding; it does not have the standing to rule on whether that finding earns a
row.

So the branch is a **question**, and it has a shape:

- **Enough detail to understand the purpose, and no more.** What was observed,
  and why it would matter to someone who was not in this session. Not a repro
  transcript, not a diff, not a plan.
- **The case FOR filing.** What goes unfixed or unremembered if this is
  dropped; who trips over it next; whether it compounds.
- **The case AGAINST filing.** Review and scheduling cost; whether an existing
  task already owns the area; whether it is a symptom of something already
  filed; whether it is small enough that noticing it again later costs less
  than carrying the row.
- **A recommendation**, so the user is ratifying a judgement rather than doing
  the triage themselves.

The user answers; the session files or drops on that answer. This keeps
ED-1550's arithmetic — filing stays the exception — without making "drop it"
a decision the agent makes alone.

# Third: the override's condition contradicts its own example

The condition is "you genuinely cannot complete the task without"; the example
is "a test that fails for an unrelated reason". Those are not the same set — an
unrelated red test usually does *not* block completion. E-2114 landed clean
with `test_no_self_dev_ids` red for a reason that had nothing to do with it.

So even a session that reads the full guide finds the example matching and the
condition not matching, and falls through to filing. The condition wants
rewording around the *regression the session is obliged to run and report*,
not around being blocked.

# Live case

E-2114's project-wide regression turned up a stray self-dev id in
`docs/guide/orchestration.md` — one sentence, in a tree already open, in a
suite the session had just run. It was filed as E-2119 instead of folded in,
which cost an extra worktree, an extra task row, a partial-state `task claim`
error, and two round trips with Mike. E-2119 was then obsoleted and the fix
folded into E-2114 by hand.

# Constraint

Keep test 1's real bound intact. The guide is right that a *large* unrelated
drive-by inflates the reviewed diff, couples two changes into one land, and
widens a revert's blast radius. The fix is to change what the bound is measured
in — cost and reviewer confusion, not topical kinship — and to route the
residue to the user as a question rather than straight into `task add`.

---

# Second root cause: the status-change surface trains narration

Same session, different file, same shape — what the agent is told at a decision
point determines what it does next.

Every status-affecting `task update` prints two things: the field render
(`• Status: assumed -> revisit`) and an advisory naming `--keep-status`. Both
are addressed to the agent. The agent relays them to the user as if they were
news, which spends the user's attention — the scarcest resource in the loop —
on a completed, correct transition it can do nothing about.

This is not a first offence and not a wording problem. A comment beside the
`auto_untriage` emitter in `task_cmd.py` records a previous session diagnosing
the identical loop — *"observed four times in one session"* — and fixing it by
**rewording** the advisory. It did not take: the reworded line was relayed twice
more in this session alone. The stimulus is the presence of agent-addressed
output, not its phrasing, so a third rewrite would fail the same way.

## Fix, two halves, landed together

**1. Audience-gate the output.** Keep everything exactly as it is for a human
running the command interactively — the status change and both advisories are
genuinely useful there. For an agent, print only the field changes it asked
for. Nothing about status it did not ask about, and no advisory.

Reuse `agent_help.agent_view()`. That predicate is already the consolidated
answer to "is an agent reading this" — E-1966, E-2006 and E-2097 each folded a
competing spelling into it, so a fourth spelling is the specific mistake this
module's history warns against. `--help` and refusals already gate on it; the
status-change output becomes a third caller.

**2. Narrow the transition that fires under it.** A plan-text edit on a
terminal status (`confirmed` / `assumed` / `completed`) must not move the
status. Today it auto-flips to `revisit`, inferring "the work needs redoing"
from an edit that, on a finished task, usually records what shipped — which is
exactly the obligation the fold-in branch above now imposes.

No new flag for the inverse: `{From: Assumed, To: Revisit, Actor: ActorUser,
Label: "reopens — shipped work found wrong"}` already exists in
`internal/taskstatus/transitions.go`, alongside the same edge from `Confirmed`
and `Completed`. Reopening is already user-owned and already spelled
`--status revisit`; the defect is the system firing a user's edge on an
inference. Non-terminal statuses keep today's behaviour, where the auto-flip is
cheap and usually right.

## Why both, not either

Half 1 alone hides a transition the agent caused: it would silently knock a task
off `assumed` and not know. Half 2 alone leaves the field render and the
advisory in place for the agent to narrate. Together there is no wrong
transition to hide and nothing agent-addressed left to relay.

`--keep-status` itself survives untouched. Its other job — skipping the
re-triage model call on a cosmetic description edit — is a real spend control
and unrelated to this.

## Live case

Recording E-2114's grown scope in its plan — obeying the rule this very task
adds — flipped it `assumed → revisit`, and `revisit` cannot reach `assumed`
again. The verification Mike had granted an hour earlier was destroyed by the
act of documenting what shipped, and had to be walked back through
`underway → unverified` for him to re-close by hand.

fields.title: Fix the two agent-facing surfaces that cause over-filing and status-change narration
fields.description: Two root causes, same shape: what the agent is told at a decision point decides what it does next. (1) The spawn handoff's 'could it reasonably be done now, inside the work already underway?' reads as a topical purity test, so a cheap unrelated fix falls through to 'otherwise file it'; restate the axis as cost and reviewer confusion, add the missing branch that ASKS the user whether to file with pros and cons, and require the fold-in branch to record grown scope on the task. (2) Every status-affecting task update prints a status change plus a --keep-status advisory, both addressed to the agent, which relays them and spends user attention; keep all of it for a human, show an agent only the field changes it asked for, and stop a plan edit on a terminal status auto-flipping to revisit. Rewording (2) was tried before and failed. Both surfaced live on E-2114.

triage.rationale: The exact wording/placement of the new user-facing ask (pros/cons prompt) and the precise output format split between agent-visible field changes and human-visible status/keep-status text are not specified, and (2) explicitly notes a prior rewording attempt failed without stating what different approach must be taken instead.

fields.text:
# Plan

Two independent halves. Either can land alone; B's two steps must land
together.

---

## A. The handoff / guide wording

**A1. `internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/_mechanics.tmpl`**, the
`handoff_focus` define, non-brainstorm branch. Rewrite the discovery bullets:

- Bullet 1 states the axis and names the failure mode: the test is **cost and
  reviewer confusion**, not topical kinship. Say outright that "not a pure
  example of this task" is not a reason to file, and that a fix cheaper than
  the task row describing it gets folded in.
- Bullet 1 gains its third obligation: do the work, note it in the commit,
  **and record the grown scope on the task** (`task update <id> --text-file`,
  with `--keep-status` so recording delivered history does not re-spec a
  finished task). This obligation is why B2 exists — see below.
- New branch before "file it": **ask the user whether to file**, with the shape
  in the analysis — what was observed and why it matters to someone not in the
  session, the case for, the case against, and a recommendation. The session
  files or drops on the answer.
- Keep the existing bound: a *large* unrelated change still splits out.

**A2. `docs/guide/tasks.md`**, the "Work you discover mid-task" section. Same
restatement of test 1; add the ask branch as a peer answer; fix the override
clause whose **condition** ("cannot complete the task without") contradicts its
own **example** ("a test that fails for an unrelated reason") — reword around
*a check the session is obliged to run and report*, not around being blocked.

**A3. Tests.** `internal/templatecmd/claim_handoff_test.go` and
`internal/hookcmd/claim_handoff_test.go` assert on brief text; update the
expectations. Add one asserting the ask branch is present, so a future
compression cannot silently drop it again — which is how the override clause
went missing.

---

## B. The status-change surface

**B1. Audience-gate the output** — `task_cmd.py`'s update path.

Human behaviour is unchanged: status line, `auto_revisit` advisory,
`auto_untriage` advisory, all exactly as today. For an agent, print **only the
field changes it asked for**:

- suppress both advisories,
- filter the `status` tuple out of `changes` before `_emit_field_changes`
  when the status entry was *not* requested — i.e. it came from `auto_revisit`
  / `auto_untriage`, not from an explicit `--status`. An explicit
  `--status` is a field the agent asked for and still renders.

Gate on `agent_help.agent_view()`. Do not introduce a new predicate: that
module's history (E-1966, E-2006, E-2097) is three separate folds of competing
spellings of this same question into that one function.

**B2. Stop inferring `revisit` from a plan edit.**

Note the mechanics: `auto_revisit` already fires *only* from
`_REOPENABLE_TERMINAL_STATUSES`, so "don't fire on a terminal status" is not a
narrowing — it removes E-1762's auto-flip entirely. State that plainly rather
than smuggling it in as a tweak.

The argument for removing it: E-1762 was calibrated when a plan edit on a
finished task was rare and therefore suspicious. A1 makes such edits
**routine and benign** — every folded-in scope note is one. Once the common
case inverts, an inference tuned to the old base rate is wrong more often than
right, and it fires a *user-owned* edge: `{From: Assumed, To: Revisit, Actor:
ActorUser, Label: "reopens — shipped work found wrong"}` in
`internal/taskstatus/transitions.go`, with twins from `Confirmed` and
`Completed`. Reopening already has an explicit spelling — `--status revisit` —
and it belongs to the user.

**This is the one judgement call in the plan and the reason it wants approval
rather than just review.** The alternative — keep the auto-flip and lean on
`--keep-status` in A1 — is defensible; it just leaves a trap armed for anyone
who forgets the flag, which is what happened on E-2114.

If removed: delete the `auto_revisit` predicate and its emission, leave the
transition-table edges alone (they are the explicit path), and check whether
`docs/status-lifecycle.mmd` renders a system-actor edge that must be
regenerated with `just lifecycle-index`.

**B3. Tests.** Python: an agent-view update renders field changes without the
unrequested status line or either advisory; a human-view update renders all of
it; an explicit `--status` still renders under agent view. Plus: a plan-text
edit on an `assumed` task leaves it `assumed`. Go: `just lifecycle-check` if
the table or the diagram moves.

---

## Verification

`just test`, `just test-go`, `just build`, `just guide-check`,
`just lifecycle-check`, plus a suite at `.endless/tasks/e-2120/verify.sh`
driving a real `task update` under both audiences.

# E-2095 — Plan

Make it visible whether a task's work has reached the project's default branch,
and whether its record is still authoritative. Four parts, one problem: a reader cannot see the facts that
decide whether to trust a row.

## Scope

**In:** parts 1, 2, 4, 5 of the analysis, plus a data-repair pass (§6).

**Out:** part 3 (record supersession automatically when an excision deletes
another task's landed files). It is blocked on a recording change that does not
exist: `task_landings` stores a merge SHA but no base, so a landing's commit
range cannot be reconstructed, and `task_files` stopped recording 2026-07-11.
Its full spec stays in this task's `--analysis`; file a successor when the
recording change is actually wanted rather than parking a speculative task in
the backlog (ED-1550 rule 1).

**Depends on E-2087**, which has landed. It shipped the content-based probe this
task consumes — do not write a second one.

**Blocked by E-2108** (`unverified`). It renames worktree branches to
`task/<id>` and retires `task_landings.branch`. The block is real, not
bookkeeping: this plan says to DERIVE a branch name from the task id, and that
derivation is false until E-2108 lands — today's branches still carry a title
slug. Landing E-2095 first would mean either deriving a name that does not
exist, or reading a column about to be removed. Either way it breaks on the
other side of E-2108.

## Decisions already taken (do not relitigate)

- Landedness is measured by CONTENT, not SHA. E-2087's `unlandedCommits`
  short-circuits on `countRevs` when HEAD is an ancestor of base, and only then
  runs `git range-diff`. Reuse it; never reach for `git cherry`.
- Branch names are DERIVED from the task id, never read from a column. E-2108
  retires `task_landings.branch`; anything here that reads it lands broken.
- The base branch is RESOLVED, never assumed. No surface in this task may write
  the word `main` into a message, a query or a rev-range. Call
  `monitor.DefaultBranch` (Go) or `worktree_cmd._default_base_branch` (Python),
  which E-1940 built for exactly this after two probes hardcoded `main` and
  "exit 128 forever" on any repo that used another name. `unlandedCommits`
  already takes `base` as a parameter, so the probe is clean — the risk is
  reintroducing the bug in the RENDERING, which is where this task lives.
- No date-scoped filter anywhere. An earlier draft proposed excluding tasks
  created before the project's first landing record. That is Endless's own
  biography, not product behaviour, and it would have hidden real unlanded work.
  §2's two sections replace it.
- New verb, not a flag. `task landed --not-on-main` reads as a contradiction.
- Part 4's banner follows E-2097's shipped shape exactly.

---

## 1. `task show` states landedness instead of implying it

Today the `Landed:` line renders only when a `task_landings` row exists, so
"landed before landings were recorded" and "the branch still holds the work"
both render as nothing. Absence is doing work it cannot do.

For a task in a terminal status, always render a landing line, one of:

```
Landed:     2026-08-30 10:16 pm  421726c          (40)
Landed:     never                                 (17)
Landed:     never — 320 unlanded commits          (42)
Landed:     unknown — base branch unresolved      (46)
```

**Hard budget: 50 characters including the label.** Not a guideline. These lines
are read in split panes, and a status field that wraps looks broken in a way a
long TITLE does not — a title is user content and obviously continues, a field
value is not. Every form above is at or under 46. Any future case that cannot
fit sheds detail to a drill-down command rather than wrapping.

This line is a SUMMARY and must never wrap. It carries neither the branch name
nor the base branch, and the reason is NOT length:

- **The branch name is derivable from the id.** E-2108 (`unverified`, implements
  ED-1587) renames worktree branches to `task/<id>` with no title slug, "so a
  branch name is derivable from the id instead of looked up", and RETIRES
  `task_landings.branch`. Once that lands, printing the branch in a task's own
  detail view repeats the `ID:` line three rows above it. Do not read
  `task_landings.branch` and do not render a branch name here; derive it where
  one is needed. The full breakdown — `Branch:`, `Worktree:`, verdict, and the
  commits themselves — already belongs to `task unsettled <id>`.

  (Length reinforces this but does not decide it. Under today's slug branches
  the long form is 103 characters and wraps; under E-2108's convention it is 68
  and fits. The redundancy argument holds either way, which is why it is the one
  stated here.)
- **The base branch is named once per report, never per row.** `task unsettled`
  already sets the precedent with its `Unlanded — N commit(s) not on <base>`
  section header. §2's report does the same in its header, which is what keeps
  the claim falsifiable without paying for the name on every line.
- **`unlanded` is the load-bearing word** and it is a defined term as of E-2087:
  a commit with no counterpart on the resolved base. It carries "not on the base
  branch" without spelling it, which is why the short form loses no meaning.

`never` stays in BOTH negative cases on purpose, rather than being dropped from
one. It is the VALUE of the field; the clause after the dash is a qualifier on
it. A reader scanning a column of these matches one word to learn the verdict
and only then reads the detail — and the two cases must not look like different
verdicts when they are the same one.

Cost: the third case needs the probe, the first two do not. E-2087's
short-circuit makes the common case a `rev-list --count`; only a branch that
genuinely differs pays for `range-diff`. Do NOT add an opt-in flag to request
the probe — an opt-in probe is one nobody remembers to pass.

Edge cases that must render distinctly rather than collapsing into "clean":

- **No branch** (reaped, or never created). The probe cannot run. Say "no
  landing recorded", never "nothing outstanding".
- **Base branch unresolved.** `DefaultBranch` returns
  `ErrDefaultBranchUnresolved` rather than guessing, because "substituting
  `main` here is exactly the bug this resolver exists to remove". Render that as
  its own state — the landedness of this task is unknown, not clean — and name
  the remedy: set `default_branch` in the project's `.endless/config.json`.
- **Probe failure.** `unlandedCommits` returns a `gitProbeError` naming the git
  command. Surface that, do not swallow it into a clean reading.
- **Uncommitted changes are a different axis** and belong to `task unsettled`.
  This line reports commits only.

## 2. `endless task unlanded`

A sibling verb to `task landed`, sharing one implementation.

**Wiring.** Put the query in `task_cmd.py` beside `landed_list`, and register
two Click commands that differ only in the mode they pass. Bundle the shared
options with a decorator the way `rowcap.limit_options_for` already does — its
own docstring gives the reason: "One factory so the two flags cannot appear on
one command and not another, and so their help text is written once." E-967's
`task_cmd.add_command(task_show, name="detail")` is the precedent for a second
name over one callback. Nothing is duplicated; there is no Click obstacle.

**Two sections, because they need different actions.** Measured 2026-09-06:
109 shipped-terminal tasks have no landing row, 3 have a branch at all, and 1
holds anything main lacks.

- **Unlanded work** — a branch exists and the probe reports commits the base
  branch lacks. Actionable: land it, or reset the branch in place. This is the
  list that should be driven to zero.
- **No landing record** — no branch, or the branch holds nothing. Nothing to
  land; the record is missing. Not actionable by landing.

Rank the first section above the second and label both. Collapsing them into one
count would report ~109 outstanding items when 1 is actionable.

**Help text must contrast with its neighbour.** `task unlanded` and
`task unsettled` sit adjacent and look alike. Each opens by naming the
difference: `unsettled` asks whether a WORKTREE is modified or unlanded;
`unlanded` asks whether a TASK claims to be done while its work has not reached
the base branch.

**Reuse `--project`, `--all`, `--llm`, `--json` and the row cap.** Match
`task landed`'s option set exactly — that is the point of the shared decorator.

## 3. `project status` claim

One attention claim, counting the **first** section only. The second section is
a standing historical count and would become permanent furniture.

```
 ⊘ 3 unlanded (Run: task unlanded)
```

Glyph and one-word label join the legend beside the existing claims. Suppress
the row entirely at zero.

Keep this coupling THIN. `project status` is heading for major revisions in
another session; specify the claim (count, glyph, drill-down verb) and leave the
rendering to that work rather than designing a row about to be replaced.

## 4. The authority banner

`task show`, `decision show` and their siblings lead with a banner when the
record is not straightforwardly authoritative. The status line is already on
screen and is demonstrably not enough — it is read as provenance, not caveat.

**Triggers.** Task: `obsolete`, `declined`, or carrying a `replaced_by` or
`duplicated_by` relation. Decision: `rejected`, `superseded`, or `proposed`.
Current volume: of 1391 tasks, 270 are obsolete/declined, 84 replaced, 3
duplicated; of 179 decisions, 124 accepted, 36 proposed, 18 rejected, 1
superseded. Roughly one record in four triggers, so three in four stay clean and
the banner keeps meaning something.

**Two kinds, named as such.** "Not ever" (obsolete, declined, rejected,
replaced, superseded) and "not yet" (proposed). The wording must distinguish
them; a proposed decision is not a retired one.

**Shape follows E-2097, which has shipped.** Its rule: emit ONE dense line as
both the FIRST and LAST line, identical, not split, so whichever end survives a
`head -N` or `tail -N` is sufficient alone.

**Audience: agent-facing only.** Gate the whole banner on
`agent_help.agent_facing()`, which is `agent_env.present() or _AGENT_VIEW` — an
agent is reading, or a human passed `--agent-view` to see what one sees. Use
that function; do not re-spell the question. E-1966, E-2006 and E-2097 each
folded a separate spelling of it back into one place, and a fourth would undo
that.

A human running `task show` sees NOTHING new. The banner is not a caveat a human
needs — the status line and the `Replaced by:` link are already on screen and a
person reads them as the qualifiers they are. It exists because an agent does
not: it quotes the row as authoritative. So the banner is agent output, and a
human reaches it only by asking, with `--agent-view`, for debugging.

This is stricter than E-2097's split, and deliberately. There, the underlying
message is a REFUSAL that a human must see or the command fails silently, so
only the bracketing is agent-gated. Here there is no underlying message a human
is owed — the banner is additive — so the whole thing is gated.

Machine formats: `--json` carries the fact as a key rather than a repeated line,
since nothing truncates JSON by lines. `--llm` gets the bracketed form.

## 5. Guide

One paragraph next to §1's rendering, in the tasks section: a task status
answers "what did we decide about this work", never "where is the code". Point
at `task unlanded` for the latter, and at `task unsettled` for worktree state.

## 6. Data repair, same session

Fold this in rather than filing it (ED-1550 rule 2). Of the 109 shipped-terminal
tasks with no landing row, **20 have a commit on main attributed to them** and
should carry a landing record; 89 have no identifiable SHA and stay as they are.

Record each with `worktree land <id> --record-only --sha <sha>`.

**Verify every SHA before recording it.** The attribution came from grepping
commit messages, which over-credits: E-1048 was credited to a commit that merely
mentions it in the body while implementing E-1047. The bar is the one E-1150
met — its own description named the commit, and that commit is on main. A SHA
that cannot be verified to that standard is left unrecorded. Writing a
heuristic SHA into the table this report reads is the failure the report exists
to prevent.

This shrinks §2's second section. It does not affect the first.

## Verification

- `task show` on a terminal task with a landing row, without one and without a
  branch, and without one but with a branch holding commits — three distinct
  lines, no case rendering as blank.
- `task show` on a task whose branch is gone, and one whose probe errors —
  neither reads as clean.
- `task unlanded` sections ranked correctly, and `task unlanded --json` /
  `--llm` carrying the same split.
- `task unlanded --help` and `task unsettled --help` each name the other.
- On a repo whose default branch is NOT `main`, every rendering names that
  branch and none reports a false all-clear. `git grep -n '"main"'` over the
  code this task touches returns nothing.
- Banner appears on an obsolete task, a replaced task, a proposed decision, and
  a rejected decision; is absent on an accepted decision and a confirmed task;
  survives both `| head -3` and `| tail -3`.
- After §6, the 20 tasks appear under `task landed` and have left `task
  unlanded`'s second section.

# Plan

Two independent halves. Either can land alone; B's two steps must land
together.

---

## A. The handoff / guide wording

**A1. `internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/_mechanics.tmpl`**, the
`handoff_focus` define, non-brainstorm branch. Rewrite the discovery bullets:

- Bullet 1 states the axis and names the failure mode: the test is **cost and
  reviewer confusion**, not topical kinship. Say outright that "not a pure
  example of this task" is not a reason to file, and that a fix cheaper than
  the task row describing it gets folded in.
- Bullet 1 gains its third obligation: do the work, note it in the commit,
  **and record the grown scope on the task** (`task update <id> --text-file`,
  with `--keep-status` so recording delivered history does not re-spec a
  finished task). This obligation is why B2 exists — see below.
- New branch before "file it": **ask the user whether to file**, with the shape
  in the analysis — what was observed and why it matters to someone not in the
  session, the case for, the case against, and a recommendation. The session
  files or drops on the answer.
- Keep the existing bound: a *large* unrelated change still splits out.

**A2. `docs/guide/tasks.md`**, the "Work you discover mid-task" section. Same
restatement of test 1; add the ask branch as a peer answer; fix the override
clause whose **condition** ("cannot complete the task without") contradicts its
own **example** ("a test that fails for an unrelated reason") — reword around
*a check the session is obliged to run and report*, not around being blocked.

**A3. Tests.** `internal/templatecmd/claim_handoff_test.go` and
`internal/hookcmd/claim_handoff_test.go` assert on brief text; update the
expectations. Add one asserting the ask branch is present, so a future
compression cannot silently drop it again — which is how the override clause
went missing.

---

## B. The status-change surface

**B1. Audience-gate the output** — `task_cmd.py`'s update path.

Human behaviour is unchanged: status line, `auto_revisit` advisory,
`auto_untriage` advisory, all exactly as today. For an agent, print **only the
field changes it asked for**:

- suppress both advisories,
- filter the `status` tuple out of `changes` before `_emit_field_changes`
  when the status entry was *not* requested — i.e. it came from `auto_revisit`
  / `auto_untriage`, not from an explicit `--status`. An explicit
  `--status` is a field the agent asked for and still renders.

Gate on `agent_help.agent_view()`. Do not introduce a new predicate: that
module's history (E-1966, E-2006, E-2097) is three separate folds of competing
spellings of this same question into that one function.

**B2. Stop inferring `revisit` from a plan edit.**

Note the mechanics: `auto_revisit` already fires *only* from
`_REOPENABLE_TERMINAL_STATUSES`, so "don't fire on a terminal status" is not a
narrowing — it removes E-1762's auto-flip entirely. State that plainly rather
than smuggling it in as a tweak.

The argument for removing it: E-1762 was calibrated when a plan edit on a
finished task was rare and therefore suspicious. A1 makes such edits
**routine and benign** — every folded-in scope note is one. Once the common
case inverts, an inference tuned to the old base rate is wrong more often than
right, and it fires a *user-owned* edge: `{From: Assumed, To: Revisit, Actor:
ActorUser, Label: "reopens — shipped work found wrong"}` in
`internal/taskstatus/transitions.go`, with twins from `Confirmed` and
`Completed`. Reopening already has an explicit spelling — `--status revisit` —
and it belongs to the user.

**This is the one judgement call in the plan and the reason it wants approval
rather than just review.** The alternative — keep the auto-flip and lean on
`--keep-status` in A1 — is defensible; it just leaves a trap armed for anyone
who forgets the flag, which is what happened on E-2114.

If removed: delete the `auto_revisit` predicate and its emission, leave the
transition-table edges alone (they are the explicit path), and check whether
`docs/status-lifecycle.mmd` renders a system-actor edge that must be
regenerated with `just lifecycle-index`.

**B3. Tests.** Python: an agent-view update renders field changes without the
unrequested status line or either advisory; a human-view update renders all of
it; an explicit `--status` still renders under agent view. Plus: a plan-text
edit on an `assumed` task leaves it `assumed`. Go: `just lifecycle-check` if
the table or the diagram moves.

---

## Verification

`just test`, `just test-go`, `just build`, `just guide-check`,
`just lifecycle-check`, plus a suite at `.endless/tasks/e-2120/verify.sh`
driving a real `task update` under both audiences.


---

## Delivered — where the work went past the plan

Recorded here per the rule A1 adds, so the task row says what shipped under it.

**B1 covers the tier-1 advance too.** The plan's criterion is that a status
entry is filtered when it "was *not* requested", and it enumerated the two
sources it knew of. `--tier 1` on a pre-work task also writes a status the
agent did not name, so it is filtered under the same test — implemented as
`status is None`, which is the criterion itself rather than a list of
inferences a later one could escape. Asserted in both the unit tests and the
verify suite.

**A1's `--keep-status` is belt-and-braces after B2, not the trap-avoidance the
plan described.** With the auto-revisit gone, recording scope on a finished
task no longer moves it, so the flag is a no-op there. It stays in the
instruction because it is still correct on a task parked at a pre-judgment
status, and a test pins it as a harmless no-op rather than leaving it
undefined.

**B2 needed no diagram regeneration.** The auto-revisit was a Python-side
inference, not a table edge; the `Assumed/Confirmed/Completed → Revisit` edges
it drove are `ActorUser` and stay. `just lifecycle-check` is clean and the
verify suite asserts it.

**Doc surfaces the removal touched**, beyond the two the plan named: the
`--keep-status` inference table and its prose in `docs/guide/tasks.md`, the
same paragraph in `docs/guide/index.md`, the flag's `--help` text in
`cli.py`, and a stale comment in `internal/events/pre_judgment_test.go` that
cited the auto-revisit as the owner of the post-implementation statuses.

payload.title: Report what git actually said when worktree land's rebase fails
payload.description: `worktree land` treats any non-zero exit from `git rebase` as a content conflict, so a rebase that stopped for another reason reports 'rebase conflict' with 'Conflicting files: (none reported)' and recovery candidates for a cause it never established. Git's stderr, which names the real reason, is captured in CalledProcessError and discarded. Observed landing E-2107; a manual `git rebase main` immediately afterwards replayed every commit and exited 0.
payload.analysis:
## What was observed

`just land` on E-2107 failed with:

    Error: rebase conflict while rebasing your branch onto main.

    Your commit that failed to replay: d3cafc4b E-2107: attribute the blast
    radius per commit, not per range

    Conflicting files:
      (none reported)

Nothing conflicted. `(none reported)` is `_rebase_conflict_message` finding
zero unmerged paths — which is the signal that this was not a content conflict
at all. Nothing on the base had touched the one file that commit changes since
the branch forked, and re-running `git rebase main` by hand afterwards replayed
all four commits and exited 0.

The report was therefore wrong in three ways at once, and unactionable in a
fourth: it asserted a conflict that did not happen, named a commit as the cause
on evidence that does not establish one, listed no files, and then offered
recovery candidates for a cause it never determined.

## The defect

`worktree_cmd.py` Step 4:

    try:
        _git_run(["rebase", base_branch], cwd=worktree_path)
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        msg = _rebase_conflict_message(...)

Any non-zero exit from `git rebase` is treated as a conflict. `git rebase` also
exits non-zero when a commit becomes empty, when the working tree was dirtied
between picks, when it refuses to overwrite local changes, and on plain
operational failures. None of those produce unmerged paths, and none of them
are fixed by the recoveries the message offers.

Git says which one it was, on stderr, and `CalledProcessError.stderr` is
already holding it. It is discarded. That is the whole bug: the one fact that
would have identified the failure is captured and thrown away, and a guess is
printed in its place.

The Step 3.7 orphan-replay handler at the other call site has the same shape
and needs the same fix.

## A second, smaller wrongness

`REBASE_HEAD` is not cleared when a rebase ends, so it can survive from an
EARLIER rebase in the same worktree. `_rebase_conflict_message` reads it
unconditionally, so "Your commit that failed to replay: <x>" can name a commit
from a previous, unrelated operation. It should only be reported when the
current rebase is actually in progress — a `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply`
directory under the worktree's git dir — and omitted otherwise.

## Fix direction

- Claim a conflict only when `git diff --diff-filter=U` is non-empty. Otherwise
  report a rebase FAILURE, verbatim from git's stderr, and offer no recovery
  candidates — there is nothing to judge between when the cause is stated.
- Include git's stderr in both cases. In the conflict case it is context; in the
  non-conflict case it is the entire answer.
- Gate the REBASE_HEAD line on a rebase actually being in progress.
- E-1417 built this message to stop `land` misattributing every conflict to an
  auto-file. This is the same failure one layer up: the earlier fix reasoned
  correctly about WHICH conflict and never checked WHETHER one occurred.

## Note on reproducing

The specific trigger was not captured, because the stderr that would have named
it was discarded — which is the defect, not a gap in the report. Do not spend
effort reconstructing this one instance; make the failure self-describing and
the next occurrence will say what it is.

triage.rationale: The bug and root cause are precisely identified (discarded stderr from CalledProcessError treated uniformly as conflict), and the obvious fix is to surface git's actual stderr instead of assuming conflict when rebase fails.

payload.title: Finish the --text to --all-fields sweep across the spawn handoff templates
payload.description: The commit titled 'Change --text to --all-fields' changed 'endless task show <id> --text' to '--all-fields' in three places by hand, to stop spawned sessions reading only the plan and missing a populated --analysis. The sweep is incomplete in the way that matters: the handoff templates that render every spawn and claim prompt were not touched, so sessions are still told '--text'. One of the three changes, a string in a negative Go test asserting non-claim commands yield no handoff, is inert and should be reverted. Two assertions in tests/test_handoff.py pin the old wording and will fail when the templates change. Complicating the sweep: '--text' names two different flags — the 'task show' display toggle, which should change, and the 'task add'/'task update'/'lesson write' content flag, which must not; the claim handoff template carries both on one line. Review what was changed, finish what was missed, revert what should not have been touched.
payload.text:
# Audit and finish the `--text` → `--all-fields` sweep

## Problem

A task's design content routinely lives in `--analysis`, and many tasks have no
plan in `--text` at all. `endless task show <id> --text` renders analysis as a
one-line teaser (`Analysis: 3270 chars (--analysis to display)`), so a spawned
session that follows its handoff literally never reads it. Observed on E-2122:
the analysis held the fix direction, a second call site with the same defect, a
separate `REBASE_HEAD` defect, and an explicit "do not spend effort
reconstructing this one instance" that contradicted the handoff's "reproduce the
bug first" — none of it in the description. Tasks have been planned with
substantive content in `--analysis` and then spawned on the belief it was being
read. It was not.

The commit titled "Change --text to --all-fields" started the fix by hand.
This task audits that commit: finish what it missed, revert what it should not
have touched, and leave the write-flag sites alone.

Find the commit with `git log --oneline --all --grep='Change --text to --all-fields'`,
and read it with `git show --stat` before starting. Everything below was true of
that commit; re-derive it against current `main` rather than trusting it.

## The trap: two different flags spell themselves `--text`

- **Read flag** — `task show --text`, a display toggle. This is the one that
  should become `--all-fields`.
- **Write flag** — `task add`/`task update --text <content>`, `--text-file <path>`,
  `lesson write --text`. Sets `tasks.text`. Must **never** be touched.

The claim handoff template contains **both on one line**: it tells the session to
fold its context in with `task update ... --text <path> --db main` and then to read
the task with `task show ... --text --db main`. Any sweep that matches the string
`--text` without reading the verb in front of it will corrupt the write sites.
Do not do this with a blanket `sed`.

The discriminator is the verb: `show` → change, everything else → leave.

## Verified inventory

### A. Missed — must change (the actual bug)

The handoff templates under `internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/` render every
spawn and claim prompt. They are the reason sessions read `--text`, and the commit
did not touch any of them. Find them with:

    grep -rn 'task show' internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/

Expect six files: `todo`, `bugfix`, `research`, `epic`, `brainstorm`, `claim`
(all `.md.tmpl`). Each becomes:

    endless task show E-{{.spawned_id}} --all-fields --db main

Per-file notes:

- `brainstorm.md.tmpl` reads "to read the seed/framing" rather than "to read the
  plan" — change only the flag, keep the wording.
- `claim.md.tmpl` — change **only** the `task show` occurrence. The
  `task update ... --text <path>` on the same line stays exactly as it is.

Also missed, in `docs/guide/index.md`: the read-a-task-you-didn't-claim example
under the hand-off-to-another-session comment block, currently
`endless task show <id> --text --children --llm`. Find it with:

    grep -n 'task show <id> --text' docs/guide/index.md

`--all-fields` already includes children, so the recommended result is
`endless task show <id> --all-fields --llm`. If the reviewing session disagrees
about dropping `--children`, keeping it is harmless — say which was chosen.

### B. Correct as changed — keep

- `docs/guide/index.md`, happy-path step 1 ("read the task and any attached
  plan"). This is the guide instruction sessions are pointed at; correct.
- `docs/guide/tasks.md`, the `task show` example block — an additive
  `endless task show <id> --all-fields` line. Correct. Consider listing
  `--all-fields` first, as the default move.

### C. Should be reverted — inert

In `internal/hookcmd/claim_handoff_test.go`, inside
`TestHandlePostToolUseSession_NonClaimYieldsNoHandoff`. That test's fixture is a
list of commands that are **not** a claim and must yield `""`. The flag on that
string is arbitrary: changing it asserts nothing, fixes nothing, and makes the
commit look as though the handoff path was covered when it was not. Revert to
`--text`.

If the reviewing session judges the string better left as `--all-fields` for
consistency with the new guidance, that is defensible — but say so explicitly
rather than leaving it unexamined.

### D. Must NOT change — write-flag sites

Every other `--text` / `--text-file` hit in the repo is the write flag or prose
about it. Confirm they are left alone. The sites cluster in:
`src/endless/task_cmd.py`, `src/endless/cli.py`, `src/endless/lesson_cmd.py`,
`internal/hookcmd/claude.go`, `internal/events/`,
`internal/templatecmd/claim_handoff_test.go` (that one is
`task update --text <path>`), `docs/guide/tasks.md`,
`docs/guide/orchestration.md`, `docs/guide/reference.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the
`tests/` files that exercise the write flag.

### E. Judgment call — recommend keeping as `--text`

In `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py`, the plan-divergence message emitted when the DB's
`tasks.text` and the branch's plan file disagree. It offers
`View full: endless task show E-<id> --text`. Find it by searching for the
`View full:` literal. Here `--text` is the point — the operator is being shown the
one field under comparison, and widening it to every field dilutes the message.
Recommend keeping; state the decision either way.

## Coupled tests — will fail when A lands

`tests/test_handoff.py` pins the current wording in two assertions. Find them:

    grep -n 'task show E-.* --text' tests/test_handoff.py

Update both to `--all-fields`. These are the reason the template change cannot be
made blind: they pin the old string, so a green suite after touching only docs and
an inert test string is not evidence the handoff was fixed.

Before assuming those two are the whole set, check the Go side for golden or
template tests pinning the same strings:

    grep -rn 'task show E-' internal/ tests/

## Steps

1. Re-derive the inventory against current `main`. Find sites by reading the verb
   in front of the flag, never by matching the flag alone.
2. Apply A — the handoff templates, plus the `docs/guide/index.md` read example.
3. Apply C — revert the inert test change, or justify keeping it.
4. Update the `tests/test_handoff.py` assertions.
5. Confirm B and E, and confirm D is untouched: `git diff --stat` should show no
   churn in `src/endless/task_cmd.py`, `cli.py`, `lesson_cmd.py`, or
   `internal/events/`.
6. If the guide is generated or indexed, re-run `just guide-index` and commit the
   artifact.

## Verification

- `just test` and `just test-go` green.
- Render the handoff for each of the five spawn types plus claim; each shows
  `--all-fields --db main` and no bare `show ... --text`.
- `git diff main --stat` touches only: the handoff templates,
  `docs/guide/index.md`, `docs/guide/tasks.md` (if reordered),
  `tests/test_handoff.py`, and `internal/hookcmd/claim_handoff_test.go`.
- Grep the diff for `--text-file`: there must be zero hits.

## Out of scope

Whether `task show` should surface analysis by default, or warn when a populated
field is being hidden behind a flag, is a separate design question. This task only
makes the instructions we hand sessions point at every field.

fields.analysis:
## Note from E-2122 (2026-09-08) — the function this task edits has changed shape

E-2122 ("Report what git actually said when worktree land's rebase fails")
rewrote the surroundings of `_rebase_conflict_message`. Nothing here is
invalidated, but Deliverable 1 now lands on a smaller target than when this plan
was written.

### What changed

Both land call sites (Step 3.7 orphan replay, Step 4 main rebase) previously
caught `CalledProcessError` and called `_rebase_conflict_message`
unconditionally, so every non-zero `git rebase` exit was reported as a content
conflict. They now go through a dispatcher, `_rebase_failure_message`, which
picks one of three reports from evidence rather than from the exit code:

- a rebase that was ALREADY in progress before land started — reported as that,
  left running (land no longer aborts an operation it did not begin)
- unmerged paths present — a real conflict; delegates to
  `_rebase_conflict_message`, unchanged in substance
- anything else — "rebase failed", git's stderr verbatim, and NO recovery
  candidates

Git's stderr is now threaded from the exception into all three; it used to be
captured and discarded.

`_rebase_conflict_message` also had one internal change: the REBASE_HEAD read is
gated on a rebase actually being in progress. REBASE_HEAD is a plain ref, so a
rebase that never started could otherwise report a commit from an unrelated
operation as "your commit that failed to replay".

### What it means for Deliverable 1

Deliverable 1 ("delete the two numbered candidates, end with one instruction:
run `endless worktree diagnose`") still applies, and now applies ONLY to the
conflict branch. The other two branches already offer no candidates — the
