# Return populated field bodies from `task show --json`, and surface children

## The defect

`endless task show <id> --json` returns `"analysis": null` for a field holding
6503 characters. The display flags that gate the human renderer (`--analysis`,
`--text`, `--outcome`, `--all-fields`, `--no-description`) also gate the JSON
payload.

This was deliberate: E-1601's description says to apply the placeholder
treatment "consistently across human, `--llm`, and `--json` output", and it was
confirmed. This task revisits that for the machine format only.

Two things are wrong with it:

1. **A machine format withholds content by default.** A consumer that does not
   know to pass a display flag reads a populated task as an empty one. The
   terminal at least prints `Analysis: 6503 chars (--analysis to display)`;
   JSON prints nothing.

2. **`null` carries two meanings.** For `analysis`, `text` and `outcome` a
   consumer can disambiguate via the `_chars` sibling (populated when withheld,
   null when empty) — but only by knowing an undocumented convention. For
   `description` there is no `description_chars` key at all, so under
   `--no-description` withheld and empty are indistinguishable.

## Decided (with Mike, 2026-09-08)

- `--json` returns full bodies by default. Display flags stop affecting it.
- `--brief` opts into a light payload by **truncating, not omitting**. A
  populated field is always a string; a truncated one ends in `…`.
- **`null` acquires exactly one meaning: the field is empty** — in every format,
  under every flag combination. This is the fix; everything else is delivery.
- Truncation default is **256 characters**, overridable as `--brief=N`.
- `--llm`'s default is unchanged (counts only). `--brief` works there too,
  upgrading a bare count to a readable preview.
- Children are always advertised as a count, and the full list stays gated
  behind `--children`. This makes children consistent with the `_chars` pattern
  rather than an exception to it.

Truncation beats omission because omission keeps `null` doing double duty and
merely moves the ambiguity behind an opt-in flag. Truncation makes the type
stable and gives a consumer the gist of a field, which a char count cannot.

## Deliverable 1 — `--json` stops consulting the display flags

In the JSON branch of `task show` (search `task_cmd.py` for the dict literal
containing `"analysis_chars"`), the four body fields are built as
`item[f] if show_f else None`. They become `item[f]` unconditionally.

## Deliverable 2 — `--brief[=N]`

A new flag on `task show`. Truncates every long field to a preview. Applies to
human, `--llm` and `--json` alike: one flag, one meaning — previews, not bodies.

- Default length 256 characters. `--brief=N` overrides.
- Truncation counts characters, not lines, and appends a single `…`. In JSON,
  truncate the decoded string before serializing so no escape sequence is split.
- A field shorter than the limit renders whole with no ellipsis, so the absence
  of `…` reliably means "not truncated".
- `--brief` wins over the display flags. `--all-fields --brief` yields previews.
  One rule, no per-format exception; state it in the flag's help text.
- `--brief` does not affect children. They are short rows, not a long field.

## Deliverable 3 — `_chars` keys become universal

They stay, and gain a `description_chars` companion, because under `--brief`
they are the only way to know the true length behind a preview.

Uniform rule: `<field>_chars` is the true character count of the stored value,
present for all four body fields, and null only when the field is empty.

## Deliverable 4 — one spelling of absent

The same task can report `text` as `""` and `outcome` as `null` because the
column values differ; to a consumer both mean "no content". Normalize empty to
`null` for all four fields in the JSON payload, with `<field>_chars` null
alongside.

## Deliverable 5 — children before the long fields, and always counted

Two changes to the human renderer, plus their machine equivalents.

### 5a. A `Children:` line in the header block

Rendered beside the existing `Analysis:` / `Text:` / `Outcome:` placeholders,
immediately after `Outcome:`. Sourced from one grouped query
(`SELECT type, COUNT(*) ... WHERE parent_id = ? GROUP BY type`).

Format:

- No children — omit the line entirely, matching how the other placeholders
  behave when their field is empty.
- All children share one type: `Children: 3 todo`
- Mixed types: `Children: 5 tasks (3 todo, 2 bugfix)`

Breakdown order is descending count, ties broken alphabetically by type, so the
dominant kind reads first and the rendering is deterministic.

### 5b. The `— Children —` section moves earlier

Today it renders last, after `— Analysis —`, `— Text —` and `— Outcome —`. It
moves to directly after `— Description —` and before `— Analysis —`.

Rationale: description is the 30-second orientation and stays first; children
are structure and belong with it; the flag-gated long prose goes last where it
does not push the structure off-screen. `(none)` still renders when `--children`
is passed and there are none — the user asked a direct question and gets a
direct answer.

### 5c. Machine formats

- `--json`: `children_count` (integer, always present, `0` when none) and
  `children_by_type` (object, always present, `{}` when none). The `children`
  array remains gated behind `--children`.
- `--llm`: `children_count=5` and `children_by_type=todo:3,bugfix:2`, emitted
  only when the count is non-zero, matching how `analysis_chars=` behaves.

This costs one grouped query per task rendered. That is accepted: it is indexed
on `parent_id`, bounded, and it is what makes the count available without
fetching every child row.

## What must not change

- The human renderer's default body output. The placeholder line
  (`Analysis: NNNN chars (--analysis to display)`) is what a person reads, and
  E-1601 built it deliberately. `--brief` adds a mode; it replaces nothing.
- `--llm`'s default output, beyond the new children lines.
- The display flags' behavior in human and `--llm` output.

## Verification

- `task show <id> --json` on a task with a populated analysis returns the body
  with no flags passed. This is the reported defect; assert it directly.
- `task show <id> --json --brief` returns a truncated string ending in `…`,
  never null, with `analysis_chars` reporting the untruncated length.
- `--brief=N` honours N; a field shorter than N carries no ellipsis.
- A task with a genuinely empty field returns `null` for it and `null` for its
  `_chars` under every combination of `--brief`, `--all-fields` and the display
  flags. This invariant is what makes `null` unambiguous — test it as a matrix,
  not a single case.
- `--no-description --json` no longer loses the description, and
  `description_chars` is present.
- `--llm` with no flags is byte-identical to before the change except for the
  new children lines. Pin this; it is the regression most likely to go unseen.
- Children render after Description and before Analysis, for a task that has
  both.
- The `Children:` header line renders in all three shapes (single-type, mixed,
  absent) and `children_count` is `0` rather than missing on a childless task.

## Coupled tests

`tests/test_outcome.py` asserts the current JSON gating — search it for
`outcome_chars`. At least one case asserts the default `--json` payload
withholds the body; that assertion inverts. Read the surrounding test before
editing so the intent is preserved rather than the literal.

Search the whole test tree for `--json` assertions on `task show`, and for
tests asserting section order in the human renderer, before starting.

## Blast radius

No in-repo consumer reads these keys — a search for `_chars` across `src`,
`internal` and `cmd` finds only the producer. The consumers are agents and
external tooling, so the change is additive for anyone already passing display
flags, and a fix for anyone who was not.

## Out of scope

Whether `task list --json` has the same shape problem. Different code path,
different payload; check it and file separately rather than widening this task.

# Rework `task claim` output: hide the sandbox path, align labels, purge the `eswt` ghost

## Problems

### 1. The output instructs users to run a command that does not exist

Current output:

```
Updated E-1424 (Test foo):
• Status: needs_plan -> in_progress
• bound to session 1

• sandbox provisioned: ~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/worktree-e-1424
• worktree created: ~/Projects/endless/.endless/worktrees/e-1424

  To work on this task, choose one:
    1. Delegate to a fresh Claude session:
         endless task spawn E-1424
    2. Do it yourself (edit, run tests, etc.):
         eval "$(endless shell-init)"  # Adds eswt shell helper func
         eswt E-1424                   # Changes to Git worktree dir
```

`endless shell-init` defines exactly three helpers: `esu`, `esp`, `esf`. There is no `eswt`. The comment "Adds eswt shell helper func" is false, and `eswt E-1424` produces "command not found." The correct helper is `esu` (= `endless session use`), which cd's into the worktree AND exports `ENDLESS_SESSION_ID` — exactly the intended action.

### 2. The sandbox cache path is presented as if it were a cd target

The output lists `sandbox provisioned: ~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/worktree-e-1424` as a parallel line to `worktree created: ...`. Users scan for a path and cd into the first one — the sandbox cache dir — which is never where they should be. Subsequent endless commands then fail with `Error: Not in a registered project directory` because the cache dir is not a project. Hit by Mike 2026-05-19.

The sandbox path has no routine user-facing purpose (only a rare SQL-client-debug case). It should not appear in default output.

## Deliverables

### A. Hide the sandbox path from default output
Remove the sandbox cache path line. Add a dedicated command to retrieve it on demand:

> `endless worktree sandbox [E-NNN]` — prints the absolute sandbox cache directory path for a worktree's task, for the rare SQL-client-debug case. Matches the existing pattern of small print verbs (`endless session id`, `endless session cd`). With no arg, resolves from cwd if inside a worktree.

### B. Rewrite claim's output against what it actually prints

The original deliverable here was "adopt the aligned-label format", and its
sample was a two-option "To work on this task, choose one:" menu. That menu no
longer exists — E-2106 deleted it, along with the broken `eswt` line inside it,
and replaced it with one outcome per caller. So the old sample proposed a
format for output that is gone. What survives from it is the discipline it was
arguing for, and that is what this deliverable keeps: aligned labels,
scannable, and no path printed that is not a cd target.

#### What claim prints today

```
Updated E-1424 (Test foo):
• Status: ready -> underway
• bound to session 1                        (only when a session resolved)

• sandbox provisioned: ~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/worktree-e-1424
• worktree created: ~/Projects/endless/.endless/worktrees/e-1424
```

then exactly one of the four outcomes E-2106 gave it:

| caller | tail |
|---|---|
| inside a Claude session | `/cd <abs worktree>` |
| a shell that bound a sibling | `E-N is bound to session ES-1 … endless session goto ES-1` |
| a shell that bound nothing | `Started Claude on E-N in window 'E-N'` + the switch line |
| `--unattended` | nothing further |

#### The target

```
Updated E-1424 (Test foo):

  • Status:       ready -> underway
  • Git worktree: ~/Projects/endless/.endless/worktrees/e-1424

  /cd <the worktree, absolute>   # point Claude's working dir at the worktree

```

Aligned labels, the sandbox line gone (deliverable A), and the caller's one
outcome below them — not a menu, because E-2106 established that the caller
never had a choice to make.

#### The session id is NOT a labeled row

Settled here rather than left open. The `Session:` row the old sample proposed
does not exist, and neither does the `bound to session N` line it was replacing.
The id is printed exactly once, as `ES-N`, and only on the path where it is
news: a shell that bound a Claude session in ANOTHER pane, in the
`endless session goto ES-N` line E-2106 already prints there.

Why not a row:

- It prints a BARE INTEGER. `session_id_display` exists because sessions and
  tasks are separate id spaces that both rendered as `E-NNN` (E-1261), and
  `session goto` refuses a bare integer matching both — so the row spells an id
  in the one form the navigator rejects. On the sibling path the same number
  now appears twice, four lines apart, in two spellings.
- On the dominant path — a Claude session claiming its own task — it restates
  the caller's own identity.
- It sits ABOVE the worktree line and the next step, which are the only lines
  anyone acts on.

Why print it at all, on the one path:

- Since E-2106 the binding is no longer always "me": claim binds this session,
  binds a sibling in another pane, or starts a new one. Binding to a sibling
  you did not mean is what seeing the id catches, and under ED-1560
  `sessions.task_id` is write-once, so a wrong binding cannot be undone.

The other three paths print no id, and correctly: on a self-claim you ARE the
session, a launched session has no id yet (its window name is its identity),
and `--unattended` bound nothing.

### C. Apply the same labeling discipline to sibling commands
`endless task spawn` and `endless task release` have analogous multi-line output. Audit and bring them to the same aligned-label format. Verify their work-instruction blocks reference real helpers (no `eswt`-style ghosts).

### D. Purge `eswt` from the guide (absorbed from E-2124)

Deliverable C says "verify their work-instruction blocks reference real helpers
(no `eswt`-style ghosts)". The guide is the other place Endless tells a user how
to get into a worktree, and it carries the same ghost: the shell-helpers table
in `docs/guide/orchestration.md` calls `eswt` "(Planned, not yet shipped.)",
while `docs/guide/index.md`, `docs/guide/help/_topics.md` and
`docs/guide/help/shell-init.md` list it beside `esu` as if a reader had it.
Find every site with `grep -rn eswt docs/`.

That framing is now wrong rather than premature. Mike settled it on 2026-09-08
— "We don't want `eswt` anymore. `esu` is sufficient" — and E-1180, which
proposed shipping it, is obsolete, as is E-1254 (which wanted claim's `eswt`
line changed to `esu`, and whose subject E-2106 deleted). Remove the references;
where a reader is being pointed at a worktree, `esu` is the answer.

One task rather than two, per ED-1550: the broken helper reference in claim's
output and the same helper in the guide are two symptoms of one cause — `eswt`
was proposed, documented, and never shipped.

## Verification

1. `endless task claim E-NNNN` from main checkout → output uses the aligned format and shows no sandbox path.
2. Every command line the output prints can be pasted into a shell and runs — no helper that `endless shell-init` does not define, and no path that is not a cd target.
3. `endless worktree sandbox E-NNNN` → prints the sandbox cache path, exit 0.
4. `endless task spawn` / `endless task release` outputs → same aligned format, no broken helper references.
5. `grep -rn eswt docs/ src/` → no hits.
6. Claim from a Claude session, from a shell beside a Claude pane, from a shell alone, and with `--unattended` → the session id appears in exactly one of the four, as `ES-N`, in the `session goto` line; no `Session:` row and no `bound to session N` in any of them.

## Grown scope (recorded during implementation)

Three things folded in rather than filed, each cheaper to make than a task row
describing it would be:

1. **The re-claim-by-the-owner path.** `claim_item`'s "already active in
   session N" branch is a fifth output shape the plan's four-caller table does
   not name, and it had both defects the plan argues against: a BARE INTEGER
   session id — the caller's own — and no aligned block. It also returned
   without printing any next step, so a Claude session re-claiming its own task
   was handed a worktree and no `/cd`. It now reports in the same aligned shape,
   names no session, and ends on `_echo_claim_next_step` like every other path.

2. **`task bind`'s session ids.** Deliverable C names spawn and release; bind is
   the fourth verb in that family and the one claim's own refusal routes people
   to (`endless task bind E-<id>`). It printed the session as a bare integer in
   three places — the exact spelling `session goto` refuses, and the exact
   argument the plan makes for dropping claim's `bound to session N` row. Now
   `ES-N`, via the existing `session_id_display`.

3. **A red Go test, pre-existing on main.**
   `TestEventBackup_EnforcesTieredRetention` seeded two backups as "six days
   back" and "six days and ninety minutes back" and asserted they shared a
   DAILY bucket. Buckets are calendar periods, so that holds only when the
   suite runs after 01:30; before then the older one falls into the previous
   day and survives the sweep. It was failing at 00:44. The production
   retention code is correct — the fixture now anchors both stamps inside one
   calendar day. Repaired here because this task cannot report the project-wide
   suite red.

`task release` was audited under deliverable C and needed no change: it is a
tombstone whose whole output is a refusal in the established
prose-then-indented-command shape, and both commands it names exist.

## Observation, not filed

`task bind` still prints "bound to session ES-N **for display**", which
contradicts its own docstring — E-2093 rewrote that docstring specifically to
say the "display only" framing "understated the verb by a wide margin", since
bind sets `sessions.task_id` and under ED-1560 that column IS the ownership
record. Left alone: rewording it is a claim about what bind means, not output
discipline, and belongs to whoever decides that.

## The defect

`endless task show <id> --json` returns `"analysis": null` for a field holding
6503 characters. The display flags that gate the human renderer (`--analysis`,
`--text`, `--outcome`, `--all-fields`, `--no-description`) also gate the JSON
payload.

This was deliberate: E-1601's description says to apply the placeholder
treatment "consistently across human, `--llm`, and `--json` output", and it was
confirmed. This task revisits that for the machine format only.

Two things are wrong with it:

1. **A machine format withholds content by default.** A consumer that does not
   know to pass a display flag reads a populated task as an empty one. The
   terminal at least prints `Analysis: 6503 chars (--analysis to display)`;
   JSON prints nothing.

2. **`null` carries two meanings.** For `analysis`, `text` and `outcome` a
   consumer can disambiguate via the `_chars` sibling (populated when withheld,
   null when empty) — but only by knowing an undocumented convention. For
   `description` there is no `description_chars` key at all, so under
   `--no-description` withheld and empty are indistinguishable.

## Decided (with Mike, 2026-09-08)

- `--json` returns full bodies by default. Display flags stop affecting it.
- `--brief` opts into a light payload by **truncating, not omitting**. A
  populated field is always a string; a truncated one ends in `…`.
- **`null` acquires exactly one meaning: the field is empty** — in every format,
  under every flag combination. This is the fix; everything else is delivery.
- Truncation default is **256 characters**, overridable as `--brief=N`.
- The count keys keep the name `<field>_chars`, not `<field>_size`. `size`
  conventionally implies bytes; these count CHARACTERS, and this tree's content
  is full of multi-byte punctuation, so `_size` would invite a consumer to
  assume a number that is wrong for most tasks here. `_chars` also shares its
  unit with `--brief=N`, which counts characters — the two names reinforce each
  other. Keeping the existing name additionally costs no churn.
- A count key is **always an integer, `0` when its content field is empty** —
  never null. A nullable count forces every consumer to null-check before
  comparing or summing, and it would spend `null` on a second meaning inside
  the very change whose purpose is to give `null` exactly one.
- `--llm`'s default is unchanged (counts only). `--brief` works there too,
  upgrading a bare count to a readable preview.
- Children are always advertised as a count, and the full list stays gated
  behind `--children`. This makes children consistent with the `_chars` pattern
  rather than an exception to it.

Truncation beats omission because omission keeps `null` doing double duty and
merely moves the ambiguity behind an opt-in flag. Truncation makes the type
stable and gives a consumer the gist of a field, which a char count cannot.

## Deliverable 1 — `--json` stops consulting the display flags

In the JSON branch of `task show` (search `task_cmd.py` for the dict literal
containing `"analysis_chars"`), the four body fields are built as
`item[f] if show_f else None`. They become `item[f]` unconditionally.

## Deliverable 2 — `--brief[=N]`

A new flag on `task show`. Truncates every long field to a preview. Applies to
human, `--llm` and `--json` alike: one flag, one meaning — previews, not bodies.

- Default length 256 characters. `--brief=N` overrides.
- Truncation counts characters, not lines, and appends a single `…`. In JSON,
  truncate the decoded string before serializing so no escape sequence is split.
- A field shorter than the limit renders whole with no ellipsis, so the absence
  of `…` reliably means "not truncated".
- `--brief` wins over the display flags. `--all-fields --brief` yields previews.
  One rule, no per-format exception; state it in the flag's help text.
- `--brief` does not affect children. They are short rows, not a long field.

## Deliverable 3 — `_chars` keys become universal

They stay, and gain a `description_chars` companion, because under `--brief`
they are the only way to know the true length behind a preview.

Uniform rule: `<field>_chars` is the true character count of the stored value,
present for all four body fields, always an integer, and `0` when the field is
empty. It is never null.

The resulting invariant, which the tests pin: `<field>_chars == 0` if and only
if `<field>` is `null`. A consumer can branch on either one and get the same
answer, and needs no null-check to do arithmetic on a count.

## Deliverable 4 — one spelling of absent

The same task can report `text` as `""` and `outcome` as `null` because the
column values differ; to a consumer both mean "no content". Normalize empty to
`null` for all four body fields in the JSON payload, with `<field>_chars` set to
`0` alongside.

So `null` appears on body fields only, and only for empty. Counts never carry
it.

## Deliverable 5 — children before the long fields, and always counted

Two changes to the human renderer, plus their machine equivalents.

### 5a. A `Children:` line in the header block

Rendered beside the existing `Analysis:` / `Text:` / `Outcome:` placeholders,
immediately after `Outcome:`. Sourced from one grouped query
(`SELECT type, COUNT(*) ... WHERE parent_id = ? GROUP BY type`).

Format:

- No children — omit the line entirely, matching how the other placeholders
  behave when their field is empty.
- All children share one type: `Children: 3 todo`
- Mixed types: `Children: 5 tasks (3 todo, 2 bugfix)`

Breakdown order is descending count, ties broken alphabetically by type, so the
dominant kind reads first and the rendering is deterministic.

### 5b. The `— Children —` section moves earlier

The detail renderer emits a fixed sequence of multi-line sections. Children are
last today. The sequence becomes:

    1. Description
    2. Children      <- moved here
    3. Analysis
    4. Text
    5. Outcome

**Children occupy slot 2 — the position Analysis would occupy if it rendered —
whether or not Analysis, Description, Text or Outcome actually render.**

State it as slots rather than as "before Analysis" or "after Description"
because EVERY section in that list is conditional: each large field renders only
when its display flag is set and its content is non-empty, and Description is
additionally suppressed by `--no-description` and skipped when it merely repeats
the title. Naming a neighbour would make the spec depend on whether that
neighbour exists, which is exactly the ambiguity this wording removes. The
implementor needs no knowledge of which neighbours are present.

Rationale for the move: children are structure, and the flag-gated long prose
goes last where it cannot push the structure off-screen. `(none)` still renders
when `--children` is passed and there are none — the user asked a direct
question and gets a direct answer.

### 5c. Machine formats

- `--json`: `children_count` (integer, always present, `0` when none) and
  `children_by_type` (object, always present, `{}` when none). The `children`
  array remains gated behind `--children`.
- `--llm`: `children_count=5` and `children_by_type=todo:3,bugfix:2`, emitted
  only when the count is non-zero, matching how `analysis_chars=` behaves.

This costs one grouped query per task rendered. That is accepted: it is indexed
on `parent_id`, bounded, and it is what makes the count available without
fetching every child row.

## What must not change

- The human renderer's default body output. The placeholder line
  (`Analysis: NNNN chars (--analysis to display)`) is what a person reads, and
  E-1601 built it deliberately. `--brief` adds a mode; it replaces nothing.
- `--llm`'s default output, beyond the new children lines.
- The display flags' behavior in human and `--llm` output.

## Verification

- `task show <id> --json` on a task with a populated analysis returns the body
  with no flags passed. This is the reported defect; assert it directly.
- `task show <id> --json --brief` returns a truncated string ending in `…`,
  never null, with `analysis_chars` reporting the untruncated length.
- `--brief=N` honours N; a field shorter than N carries no ellipsis.
- A task with a genuinely empty field returns `null` for it and `0` for its
  `_chars`, under every combination of `--brief`, `--all-fields` and the display
  flags. Assert the biconditional directly — `<field>_chars == 0` if and only if
  `<field>` is `null` — as a matrix, not a single case. This is what makes
  `null` unambiguous.
- No `_chars` key is ever null, on any task, under any flags.
- `--no-description --json` no longer loses the description, and
  `description_chars` is present.
- `--llm` with no flags is byte-identical to before the change except for the
  new children lines. Pin this; it is the regression most likely to go unseen.
- The `— Children —` section renders in slot 2 across the full presence matrix:
  Description present or absent (`--no-description`, and a description equal to
  the title) crossed with Analysis present or absent (flag unset, and flag set
  with an empty field). Children must land in the same relative position in all
  of them, including the case where Children is the ONLY section that renders.
- The `Children:` header line renders in all three shapes (single-type, mixed,
  absent) and `children_count` is `0` rather than missing on a childless task.

## Coupled tests

`tests/test_outcome.py` asserts the current JSON gating — search it for
`outcome_chars`. At least one case asserts the default `--json` payload
withholds the body; that assertion inverts. Read the surrounding test before
editing so the intent is preserved rather than the literal.

Search the whole test tree for `--json` assertions on `task show`, and for
tests asserting section order in the human renderer, before starting.

## Blast radius

No in-repo consumer reads these keys — a search for `_chars` across `src`,
`internal` and `cmd` finds only the producer. The consumers are agents and
external tooling, so the change is additive for anyone already passing display
flags, and a fix for anyone who was not.

## Out of scope

Whether `task list --json` has the same shape problem. Different code path,
different payload; check it and file separately rather than widening this task.

# Rework `task claim` output: hide the sandbox path, align labels, purge the `eswt` ghost

## Problems

### 1. The output instructs users to run a command that does not exist

Current output:

```
Updated E-1424 (Test foo):
• Status: needs_plan -> in_progress
• bound to session 1

• sandbox provisioned: ~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/worktree-e-1424
• worktree created: ~/Projects/endless/.endless/worktrees/e-1424

  To work on this task, choose one:
    1. Delegate to a fresh Claude session:
         endless task spawn E-1424
    2. Do it yourself (edit, run tests, etc.):
         eval "$(endless shell-init)"  # Adds eswt shell helper func
         eswt E-1424                   # Changes to Git worktree dir
```

`endless shell-init` defines exactly three helpers: `esu`, `esp`, `esf`. There is no `eswt`. The comment "Adds eswt shell helper func" is false, and `eswt E-1424` produces "command not found." The correct helper is `esu` (= `endless session use`), which cd's into the worktree AND exports `ENDLESS_SESSION_ID` — exactly the intended action.

### 2. The sandbox cache path is presented as if it were a cd target

The output lists `sandbox provisioned: ~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/worktree-e-1424` as a parallel line to `worktree created: ...`. Users scan for a path and cd into the first one — the sandbox cache dir — which is never where they should be. Subsequent endless commands then fail with `Error: Not in a registered project directory` because the cache dir is not a project. Hit by Mike 2026-05-19.

The sandbox path has no routine user-facing purpose (only a rare SQL-client-debug case). It should not appear in default output.

## Deliverables

### A. Hide the sandbox path from default output
Remove the sandbox cache path line. Add a dedicated command to retrieve it on demand:

> `endless worktree sandbox [E-NNN]` — prints the absolute sandbox cache directory path for a worktree's task, for the rare SQL-client-debug case. Matches the existing pattern of small print verbs (`endless session id`, `endless session cd`). With no arg, resolves from cwd if inside a worktree.

### B. Rewrite claim's output against what it actually prints

The original deliverable here was "adopt the aligned-label format", and its
sample was a two-option "To work on this task, choose one:" menu. That menu no
longer exists — E-2106 deleted it, along with the broken `eswt` line inside it,
and replaced it with one outcome per caller. So the old sample proposed a
format for output that is gone. What survives from it is the discipline it was
arguing for, and that is what this deliverable keeps: aligned labels,
scannable, and no path printed that is not a cd target.

#### What claim prints today

```
Updated E-1424 (Test foo):
• Status: ready -> underway
• bound to session 1                        (only when a session resolved)

• sandbox provisioned: ~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/worktree-e-1424
• worktree created: ~/Projects/endless/.endless/worktrees/e-1424
```

then exactly one of the four outcomes E-2106 gave it:

| caller | tail |
|---|---|
| inside a Claude session | `/cd <abs worktree>` |
| a shell that bound a sibling | `E-N is bound to session ES-1 … endless session goto ES-1` |
| a shell that bound nothing | `Started Claude on E-N in window 'E-N'` + the switch line |
| `--unattended` | nothing further |

#### The target

```
Updated E-1424 (Test foo):

  • Status:       ready -> underway
  • Git worktree: ~/Projects/endless/.endless/worktrees/e-1424

  /cd <the worktree, absolute>   # point Claude's working dir at the worktree

```

Aligned labels, the sandbox line gone (deliverable A), and the caller's one
outcome below them — not a menu, because E-2106 established that the caller
never had a choice to make.

#### The session id is NOT a labeled row

Settled here rather than left open. The `Session:` row the old sample proposed
does not exist, and neither does the `bound to session N` line it was replacing.
The id is printed exactly once, as `ES-N`, and only on the path where it is
news: a shell that bound a Claude session in ANOTHER pane, in the
`endless session goto ES-N` line E-2106 already prints there.

Why not a row:

- It prints a BARE INTEGER. `session_id_display` exists because sessions and
  tasks are separate id spaces that both rendered as `E-NNN` (E-1261), and
  `session goto` refuses a bare integer matching both — so the row spells an id
  in the one form the navigator rejects. On the sibling path the same number
  now appears twice, four lines apart, in two spellings.
- On the dominant path — a Claude session claiming its own task — it restates
  the caller's own identity.
- It sits ABOVE the worktree line and the next step, which are the only lines
  anyone acts on.

Why print it at all, on the one path:

- Since E-2106 the binding is no longer always "me": claim binds this session,
  binds a sibling in another pane, or starts a new one. Binding to a sibling
  you did not mean is what seeing the id catches, and under ED-1560
  `sessions.task_id` is write-once, so a wrong binding cannot be undone.

The other three paths print no id, and correctly: on a self-claim you ARE the
session, a launched session has no id yet (its window name is its identity),
and `--unattended` bound nothing.

### C. Apply the same labeling discipline to sibling commands
`endless task spawn` and `endless task release` have analogous multi-line output. Audit and bring them to the same aligned-label format. Verify their work-instruction blocks reference real helpers (no `eswt`-style ghosts).

### D. Purge `eswt` from the guide (absorbed from E-2124)

Deliverable C says "verify their work-instruction blocks reference real helpers
(no `eswt`-style ghosts)". The guide is the other place Endless tells a user how
to get into a worktree, and it carries the same ghost: the shell-helpers table
in `docs/guide/orchestration.md` calls `eswt` "(Planned, not yet shipped.)",
while `docs/guide/index.md`, `docs/guide/help/_topics.md` and
`docs/guide/help/shell-init.md` list it beside `esu` as if a reader had it.
Find every site with `grep -rn eswt docs/`.

That framing is now wrong rather than premature. Mike settled it on 2026-09-08
— "We don't want `eswt` anymore. `esu` is sufficient" — and E-1180, which
proposed shipping it, is obsolete, as is E-1254 (which wanted claim's `eswt`
line changed to `esu`, and whose subject E-2106 deleted). Remove the references;
where a reader is being pointed at a worktree, `esu` is the answer.

One task rather than two, per ED-1550: the broken helper reference in claim's
output and the same helper in the guide are two symptoms of one cause — `eswt`
was proposed, documented, and never shipped.

## Verification

1. `endless task claim E-NNNN` from main checkout → output uses the aligned format and shows no sandbox path.
2. Every command line the output prints can be pasted into a shell and runs — no helper that `endless shell-init` does not define, and no path that is not a cd target.
3. `endless worktree sandbox E-NNNN` → prints the sandbox cache path, exit 0.
4. `endless task spawn` / `endless task release` outputs → same aligned format, no broken helper references.
5. `grep -rn eswt docs/ src/` → no hits.
6. Claim from a Claude session, from a shell beside a Claude pane, from a shell alone, and with `--unattended` → the session id appears in exactly one of the four, as `ES-N`, in the `session goto` line; no `Session:` row and no `bound to session N` in any of them.

## Grown scope (recorded during implementation)

Three things folded in rather than filed, each cheaper to make than a task row
describing it would be:

1. **The re-claim-by-the-owner path.** `claim_item`'s "already active in
   session N" branch is a fifth output shape the plan's four-caller table does
   not name, and it had both defects the plan argues against: a BARE INTEGER
   session id — the caller's own — and no aligned block. It also returned
   without printing any next step, so a Claude session re-claiming its own task
   was handed a worktree and no `/cd`. It now reports in the same aligned shape,
   names no session, and ends on `_echo_claim_next_step` like every other path.

2. **`task bind`'s session ids.** Deliverable C names spawn and release; bind is
   the fourth verb in that family and the one claim's own refusal routes people
   to (`endless task bind E-<id>`). It printed the session as a bare integer in
   three places — the exact spelling `session goto` refuses, and the exact
   argument the plan makes for dropping claim's `bound to session N` row. Now
   `ES-N`, via the existing `session_id_display`.

3. **A red Go test, pre-existing on main.**
   `TestEventBackup_EnforcesTieredRetention` seeded two backups as "six days
   back" and "six days and ninety minutes back" and asserted they shared a
   DAILY bucket. Buckets are calendar periods, so that holds only when the
   suite runs after 01:30; before then the older one falls into the previous
   day and survives the sweep. It was failing at 00:44. The production
   retention code is correct — the fixture now anchors both stamps inside one
   calendar day. Repaired here because this task cannot report the project-wide
   suite red.

`task release` was audited under deliverable C and needed no change: it is a
tombstone whose whole output is a refusal in the established
prose-then-indented-command shape, and both commands it names exist.

4. **`task bind`'s stale "for display" wording.** The same line, one turn
   later. It said the binding was "for display", which is the understatement
   E-2093 rewrote bind's docstring to reject — bind sets `sessions.task_id`,
   and under ED-1560 that column IS the ownership record. The docstring had
   also kept a leftover of the same framing further down ("nothing for the
   status bar to display"), so both halves said it.

   I first reported this as a contradiction needing Mike's ruling, and he
   corrected the framing: one side was checkable, so nothing needed deciding —
   only repairing. Both now drop the claim and keep everything a reader used
   (what bound to what, and that the status did not move). Folded in here
   rather than filed, per ED-1550, since the session that landed E-1428 is
   still live. Lesson recorded.

  `null` unambiguous.
- No `_chars` key is ever null, on any task, under any flags.
- `--no-description --json` no longer loses the description, and
  `description_chars` is present.
- `--llm` with no flags is byte-identical to before the change except for the
  new children lines. Pin this; it is the regression most likely to go unseen.
- The `— Children —` section renders in slot 2 across the full presence matrix:
  Description present or absent (`--no-description`, and a description equal to
  the title) crossed with Analysis present or absent (flag unset, and flag set
  with an empty field). Children must land in the same relative position in all
  of them, including the case where Children is the ONLY section that renders.
- The `Children:` header line renders in all three shapes (single-type, mixed,
  absent) and `children_count` is `0` rather than missing on a childless task.

## Coupled tests

`tests/test_outcome.py` asserts the current JSON gating — search it for
`outcome_chars`. At least one case asserts the default `--json` payload
withholds the body; that assertion inverts. Read the surrounding test before
editing so the intent is preserved rather than the literal.

Search the whole test tree for `--json` assertions on `task show`, and for
tests asserting section order in the human renderer, before starting.

## Blast radius

No in-repo consumer reads these keys — a search for `_chars` across `src`,
`internal` and `cmd` finds only the producer. The consumers are agents and
external tooling, so the change is additive for anyone already passing display
flags, and a fix for anyone who was not.

## Out of scope

Whether `task list --json` has the same shape problem. Different code path,
different payload; check it and file separately rather than widening this task.

---

## Grown scope, recorded at implementation (ES-1193)

Four things the plan did not name, folded in because each is cheaper to make
than a task row describing it would be.

### 1. `--brief` reveals a gated field, it does not merely shorten a shown one

The plan said "`--brief` wins over the display flags" and, for `--llm`,
"upgrading a bare count to a readable preview". A bare count is what an UNSHOWN
field emits, so `--brief` has to make a hidden field visible — as a preview.
Implemented as one rule in all three formats: under `--brief`, all four body
fields render truncated regardless of which display flags were passed,
`--no-description` included. That is what makes `--brief` mean exactly one
thing, and it matches what `--json` does unconditionally after deliverable 1.

### 2. A child with no type counts as `untyped`, not as the empty string

`type_id` is nullable and older rows really do carry NULL — four of E-968's
children do. The `COALESCE(tt.slug, '')` the rest of `task show` uses renders
those as `4 ` in the header line and as a `""` key in `children_by_type`, both
of which read as a bug rather than as a fact about the data. The grouped query
coalesces to `untyped` instead; no task type slug can collide with it.

### 3. `--brief` names the fix when it swallows a task id

An optional-value option consumes whatever token follows it, so
`task show --brief E-101` offers the task id as the length. A bare integer-range
failure would show the reader their own task id being called a bad number.
`BriefLenType` (src/endless/cli.py) recognizes that shape and names both fixes —
`--brief=N <id>`, or a bare `--brief` after the id. `--brief=0` is refused in
the same voice; a negative N would silently truncate from the wrong end.

### 4. Guide documentation

`docs/guide/tasks.md` listed every other `task show` flag and would have been
the one place a reader looks for `--brief`. It now carries the flag, the rule
that display flags do not reach `--json`, the `<field>_chars == 0` iff
`<field> is null` invariant, and what `--brief` means.

## The out-of-scope check the plan asked for

`task list --json` does NOT have the same shape problem. Its payload carries no
body fields at all — id, phase, status, tier, title, parent, created, confirmed,
replaced_by, duplicates — so there is no field whose `null` could mean
"withheld", and no `_chars` key to disagree with one. Nothing to file.

# E-2095 — Plan

Make it visible whether a task's work has reached the project's default branch,
and whether its record is still authoritative. Four parts, one problem: a reader cannot see the facts that
decide whether to trust a row.

## Scope

**In:** parts 1, 2, 4, 5 of the analysis, plus a data-repair pass (§6).

**Out:** part 3 (record supersession automatically when an excision deletes
another task's landed files). It is blocked on a recording change that does not
exist: `task_landings` stores a merge SHA but no base, so a landing's commit
range cannot be reconstructed, and `task_files` stopped recording 2026-07-11.
Its full spec stays in this task's `--analysis`; file a successor when the
recording change is actually wanted rather than parking a speculative task in
the backlog (ED-1550 rule 1).

**Depends on E-2087**, which has landed. It shipped the content-based probe this
task consumes — do not write a second one.

**Blocked by E-2108** (`unverified`). It renames worktree branches to
`task/<id>` and retires `task_landings.branch`. The block is real, not
bookkeeping: this plan says to DERIVE a branch name from the task id, and that
derivation is false until E-2108 lands — today's branches still carry a title
slug. Landing E-2095 first would mean either deriving a name that does not
exist, or reading a column about to be removed. Either way it breaks on the
other side of E-2108.

## Decisions already taken (do not relitigate)

- Landedness is measured by CONTENT, not SHA. E-2087's `unlandedCommits`
  short-circuits on `countRevs` when HEAD is an ancestor of base, and only then
  runs `git range-diff`. Reuse it; never reach for `git cherry`.
- Branch names are DERIVED from the task id, never read from a column. E-2108
  retires `task_landings.branch`; anything here that reads it lands broken.
- The base branch is RESOLVED, never assumed. No surface in this task may write
  the word `main` into a message, a query or a rev-range. Call
  `monitor.DefaultBranch` (Go) or `worktree_cmd._default_base_branch` (Python),
  which E-1940 built for exactly this after two probes hardcoded `main` and
  "exit 128 forever" on any repo that used another name. `unlandedCommits`
  already takes `base` as a parameter, so the probe is clean — the risk is
  reintroducing the bug in the RENDERING, which is where this task lives.
- No date-scoped filter anywhere. An earlier draft proposed excluding tasks
  created before the project's first landing record. That is Endless's own
  biography, not product behaviour, and it would have hidden real unlanded work.
  §2's two sections replace it.
- New verb, not a flag. `task landed --not-on-main` reads as a contradiction.
- Part 4's banner follows E-2097's shipped shape exactly.

---

## 1. `task show` states landedness instead of implying it

Today the `Landed:` line renders only when a `task_landings` row exists, so
"landed before landings were recorded" and "the branch still holds the work"
both render as nothing. Absence is doing work it cannot do.

For a task in a terminal status, always render a landing line, one of:

```
Landed:     2026-08-30 10:16 pm  421726c          (40)
Landed:     never                                 (17)
Landed:     never — 320 unlanded commits          (42)
Landed:     unknown — base branch unresolved      (46)
```

**Hard budget: 60 characters including the label.** Not a guideline. These lines
are read in split panes, and a status field that wraps looks broken in a way a
long TITLE does not — a title is user content and obviously continues, a field
value is not. Every form above is at or under 46. Any future case that cannot
fit sheds detail to a drill-down command rather than wrapping.

This line is a SUMMARY and must never wrap. It carries neither the branch name
nor the base branch, and the reason is NOT length:

- **The branch name is derivable from the id.** E-2108 (`unverified`, implements
  ED-1587) renames worktree branches to `task/<id>` with no title slug, "so a
  branch name is derivable from the id instead of looked up", and RETIRES
  `task_landings.branch`. Once that lands, printing the branch in a task's own
  detail view repeats the `ID:` line three rows above it. Do not read
  `task_landings.branch` and do not render a branch name here; derive it where
  one is needed. The full breakdown — `Branch:`, `Worktree:`, verdict, and the
  commits themselves — already belongs to `task unsettled <id>`.

  (Length reinforces this but does not decide it. Under today's slug branches
  the long form is 103 characters and wraps; under E-2108's convention it is 68
  and fits. The redundancy argument holds either way, which is why it is the one
  stated here.)
- **The base branch is named once per report, never per row.** `task unsettled`
  already sets the precedent with its `Unlanded — N commit(s) not on <base>`
  section header. §2's report does the same in its header, which is what keeps
  the claim falsifiable without paying for the name on every line.
- **`unlanded` is the load-bearing word** and it is a defined term as of E-2087:
  a commit with no counterpart on the resolved base. It carries "not on the base
  branch" without spelling it, which is why the short form loses no meaning.

`never` stays in BOTH negative cases on purpose, rather than being dropped from
one. It is the VALUE of the field; the clause after the dash is a qualifier on
it. A reader scanning a column of these matches one word to learn the verdict
and only then reads the detail — and the two cases must not look like different
verdicts when they are the same one.

Cost: the third case needs the probe, the first two do not. E-2087's
short-circuit makes the common case a `rev-list --count`; only a branch that
genuinely differs pays for `range-diff`. Do NOT add an opt-in flag to request
the probe — an opt-in probe is one nobody remembers to pass.

Edge cases that must render distinctly rather than collapsing into "clean":

- **No branch** (reaped, or never created). The probe cannot run. Say "no
  landing recorded", never "nothing outstanding".
- **Base branch unresolved.** `DefaultBranch` returns
  `ErrDefaultBranchUnresolved` rather than guessing, because "substituting
  `main` here is exactly the bug this resolver exists to remove". Render that as
  its own state — the landedness of this task is unknown, not clean — and name
  the remedy: set `default_branch` in the project's `.endless/config.json`.
- **Probe failure.** `unlandedCommits` returns a `gitProbeError` naming the git
  command. Surface that, do not swallow it into a clean reading.
- **Uncommitted changes are a different axis** and belong to `task unsettled`.
  This line reports commits only.

## 2. `endless task unlanded`

A sibling verb to `task landed`, sharing one implementation.

**Wiring.** Put the query in `task_cmd.py` beside `landed_list`, and register
two Click commands that differ only in the mode they pass. Bundle the shared
options with a decorator the way `rowcap.limit_options_for` already does — its
own docstring gives the reason: "One factory so the two flags cannot appear on
one command and not another, and so their help text is written once." E-967's
`task_cmd.add_command(task_show, name="detail")` is the precedent for a second
name over one callback. Nothing is duplicated; there is no Click obstacle.

**Two sections, because they need different actions.** Measured 2026-09-06:
109 shipped-terminal tasks have no landing row, 3 have a branch at all, and 1
holds anything main lacks.

- **Unlanded work** — a branch exists and the probe reports commits the base
  branch lacks. Actionable: land it, or reset the branch in place. This is the
  list that should be driven to zero.
- **No landing record** — no branch, or the branch holds nothing. Nothing to
  land; the record is missing. Not actionable by landing.

Rank the first section above the second and label both. Collapsing them into one
count would report ~109 outstanding items when 1 is actionable.

**Help text must contrast with its neighbour.** `task unlanded` and
`task unsettled` sit adjacent and look alike. Each opens by naming the
difference: `unsettled` asks whether a WORKTREE is modified or unlanded;
`unlanded` asks whether a TASK claims to be done while its work has not reached
the base branch.

**Reuse `--project`, `--all`, `--llm`, `--json` and the row cap.** Match
`task landed`'s option set exactly — that is the point of the shared decorator.

## 3. `project status` claim

One attention claim, counting the **first** section only. The second section is
a standing historical count and would become permanent furniture.

```
 ⊘ 3 unlanded (Run: task unlanded)
```

Glyph and one-word label join the legend beside the existing claims. Suppress
the row entirely at zero.

Keep this coupling THIN. `project status` is heading for major revisions in
another session; specify the claim (count, glyph, drill-down verb) and leave the
rendering to that work rather than designing a row about to be replaced.

## 4. The authority banner

`task show`, `decision show` and their siblings lead with a banner when the
record is not straightforwardly authoritative. The status line is already on
screen and is demonstrably not enough — it is read as provenance, not caveat.

**Triggers.** Task: `obsolete`, `declined`, or carrying a `replaced_by` or
`duplicated_by` relation. Decision: `rejected`, `superseded`, or `proposed`.
Current volume: of 1391 tasks, 270 are obsolete/declined, 84 replaced, 3
duplicated; of 179 decisions, 124 accepted, 36 proposed, 18 rejected, 1
superseded. Roughly one record in four triggers, so three in four stay clean and
the banner keeps meaning something.

**Two kinds, named as such.** "Not ever" (obsolete, declined, rejected,
replaced, superseded) and "not yet" (proposed). The wording must distinguish
them; a proposed decision is not a retired one.

**Shape follows E-2097, which has shipped.** Its rule: emit ONE dense line as
both the FIRST and LAST line, identical, not split, so whichever end survives a
`head -N` or `tail -N` is sufficient alone.

**Audience: agent-facing only.** Gate the whole banner on
`agent_help.agent_facing()`, which is `agent_env.present() or _AGENT_VIEW` — an
agent is reading, or a human passed `--agent-view` to see what one sees. Use
that function; do not re-spell the question. E-1966, E-2006 and E-2097 each
folded a separate spelling of it back into one place, and a fourth would undo
that.

A human running `task show` sees NOTHING new. The banner is not a caveat a human
needs — the status line and the `Replaced by:` link are already on screen and a
person reads them as the qualifiers they are. It exists because an agent does
not: it quotes the row as authoritative. So the banner is agent output, and a
human reaches it only by asking, with `--agent-view`, for debugging.

This is stricter than E-2097's split, and deliberately. There, the underlying
message is a REFUSAL that a human must see or the command fails silently, so
only the bracketing is agent-gated. Here there is no underlying message a human
is owed — the banner is additive — so the whole thing is gated.

Machine formats: `--json` carries the fact as a key rather than a repeated line,
since nothing truncates JSON by lines. `--llm` gets the bracketed form.

## 5. Guide

One paragraph next to §1's rendering, in the tasks section: a task status
answers "what did we decide about this work", never "where is the code". Point
at `task unlanded` for the latter, and at `task unsettled` for worktree state.

## 6. Data repair, same session

Fold this in rather than filing it (ED-1550 rule 2). Of the 109 shipped-terminal
tasks with no landing row, **20 have a commit on main attributed to them** and
should carry a landing record; 89 have no identifiable SHA and stay as they are.

Record each with `worktree land <id> --record-only --sha <sha>`.

**Verify every SHA before recording it.** The attribution came from grepping
commit messages, which over-credits: E-1048 was credited to a commit that merely
mentions it in the body while implementing E-1047. The bar is the one E-1150
met — its own description named the commit, and that commit is on main. A SHA
that cannot be verified to that standard is left unrecorded. Writing a
heuristic SHA into the table this report reads is the failure the report exists
to prevent.

This shrinks §2's second section. It does not affect the first.

## Verification

- `task show` on a terminal task with a landing row, without one and without a
  branch, and without one but with a branch holding commits — three distinct
  lines, no case rendering as blank.
- `task show` on a task whose branch is gone, and one whose probe errors —
  neither reads as clean.
- `task unlanded` sections ranked correctly, and `task unlanded --json` /
  `--llm` carrying the same split.
- `task unlanded --help` and `task unsettled --help` each name the other.
- On a repo whose default branch is NOT `main`, every rendering names that
  branch and none reports a false all-clear. `git grep -n '"main"'` over the
  code this task touches returns nothing.
- Banner appears on an obsolete task, a replaced task, a proposed decision, and
  a rejected decision; is absent on an accepted decision and a confirmed task;
  survives both `| head -3` and `| tail -3`.
- After §6, the 20 tasks appear under `task landed` and have left `task
  unlanded`'s second section.

payload.title: Additive agent-facing output is gated entirely to agents; only output a human is owed, such as a refusal, renders for both
payload.description: E-2097 established that an agent-facing refusal repeats its verdict at both ends, gated on agent_facing(), while the human still sees the underlying guidance byte for byte. Carrying that split to E-2095's authority banner was proposed and rejected: the two cases are not alike. A refusal has an underlying message a human is OWED — suppress it and the command fails silently. A banner is purely additive; a person reading task show already has the status line and the Replaced by link on screen and reads them as the qualifiers they are. The banner exists because an agent does not — it quotes the row as authoritative. So the audience test is not 'is this agent-facing?' but 'is a human owed the underlying message?'. Where they are not, the whole surface is gated and a human reaches it only by asking, with --agent-view, for debugging. The alternative — render it once for humans too — was the proposal on the table and was refused as unrequested output.

# Plan as shipped (2026-09-08)

The reopened task's remedy, per the analysis: stop writing the generated
per-worktree override into the tracked `.claude/settings.json`, and stop hiding
it with `git update-index --skip-worktree`. Write it to Claude Code's Local-tier
`.claude/settings.local.json`, which this repo already gitignores. Nothing
tracked is modified, so no rebase can ever be refused over it.

## The merge semantics were measured, not assumed

The analysis required this before implementing. A throwaway project with both
files and a hook in each, run under Claude Code 2.1.236:

    scope=local    MERGE_A=from-project MERGE_B=from-local MERGE_SHARED=from-local
    scope=project  MERGE_A=from-project MERGE_B=from-local MERGE_SHARED=from-local

`hooks` CONCATENATE across the two scopes (both fired). `env` merges per-key
with the local file winning. The committed `settings.json` ships no hooks, so
relocating the override leaves the effective hook set unchanged, and
`enabledPlugins` / `autoMemoryEnabled` keep coming from the committed file —
read natively rather than copied into the local one.

## What changed

- `internal/sandboxcmd/bind.go` — the `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` env block goes to
  `settings.local.json`; `markSettingsSkipWorktree` is gone.
- `justfile` `claude-settings-init` — the hook override and
  `worktree.bgIsolation` go to `settings.local.json`, merged over whatever that
  file already holds (the env block, hand-written `permissions`); no
  `update-index --skip-worktree`; no copying of committed keys.
- `internal/sandboxcmd/claudesettings.go` (new) — `repairWorktreeClaudeSettings`
  and `endless-go sandbox claude-settings-repair [--all] [<worktree> ...]`.
- `internal/hookcmd/claude.go` — `worktreeOverrideRegistered` reads
  `settings.local.json` first and still recognises the legacy `settings.json`
  location, so a not-yet-repaired worktree keeps self-skipping correctly.
- `.gitignore`, `internal/monitor/worktree_anomalies.go`,
  `.endless/hooks/post-worktree-create.sh`, `src/endless/task_cmd.py` — comments
  that asserted the old arrangement.

## Migration: Mike's call, 2026-09-08

Changing the writers only helps worktrees created afterwards; 135 already on
disk carry the bit. Asked, and the answer was a one-shot repair command run on
E-1347's own land — so `.endless/hooks/post-land/e-1347.sh` invokes
`sandbox claude-settings-repair --all` once, right after the merge advances main.

The repair lives in Go rather than the Python CLI because of version skew: at
post-land time the globally installed `endless` is still the PRE-land build, so
a Python subcommand added by this branch would not exist yet. E-1347's own
worktree binary is rebuilt by `just land` before the land, so the script probes
`sandbox --help` and picks the first build that actually has the subcommand.

Per worktree the repair: salvages every top-level key whose working value
differs from HEAD into `settings.local.json` (existing local values win — the
salvage fills gaps, it never overwrites), clears the bit, then restores the
tracked file. The skip-worktree bit is the ONLY trigger: without it a modified
`.claude/settings.json` is visible user work, and reverting that would be data
loss. That guard is what makes the fleet sweep and repeat runs safe.

## PRODUCT

`sandbox bind` now warns once, and changes nothing, when a project does not
gitignore `.claude/settings.local.json` — a downstream project would otherwise
see it as untracked work and as a worktree anomaly at handoff. Endless's own
`.gitignore` already covers it. Endless does not edit the user's ignore rules.

## Dogfooded

This worktree was itself repaired with the shipped command: bit cleared, tracked
file back to its committed content, `git status` clean, and all three generated
keys (`env`, six hook events, `worktree.bgIsolation`) intact in the local file —
the effective merged config is byte-identical to what it was before.

fields.title: Output that sits on top of a complete answer is shown only to agents; output that IS the answer is shown to everyone
fields.description: Two kinds of extra output need opposite rules, and sorting them by audience gets it wrong because agents read both. When a command rejects your input — task add turning down an over-long description — that error is its entire output; hide it from a person and the command looks like it did nothing, with no way to tell why. E-2097 therefore shows it to everyone, and only repeats the one line saying what was wrong at top and bottom for agents, whose head -3 / tail -3 would otherwise drop it. E-2095's caution is different: it sits on top of output that is already complete. A person reading task show already has the status line and the Replaced-by link and reads them as qualifications; an agent does not, and quotes the row as authoritative. So the caution is agent-only, reachable by a person with --agent-view. Test for anything added later: remove it for a person. Less than the command's answer left, it renders for everyone. Same complete answer left, it is agent-only.
