`never` stays in BOTH negative cases on purpose, rather than being dropped from
one. It is the VALUE of the field; the clause after the dash is a qualifier on
it. A reader scanning a column of these matches one word to learn the verdict
and only then reads the detail — and the two cases must not look like different
verdicts when they are the same one.

Cost: the third case needs the probe, the first two do not. E-2087's
short-circuit makes the common case a `rev-list --count`; only a branch that
genuinely differs pays for `range-diff`. Do NOT add an opt-in flag to request
the probe — an opt-in probe is one nobody remembers to pass.

Edge cases that must render distinctly rather than collapsing into "clean":

- **No branch** (reaped, or never created). The probe cannot run. Say "no
  landing recorded", never "nothing outstanding".
- **Base branch unresolved.** `DefaultBranch` returns
  `ErrDefaultBranchUnresolved` rather than guessing, because "substituting
  `main` here is exactly the bug this resolver exists to remove". Render that as
  its own state — the landedness of this task is unknown, not clean — and name
  the remedy: set `default_branch` in the project's `.endless/config.json`.
- **Probe failure.** `unlandedCommits` returns a `gitProbeError` naming the git
  command. Surface that, do not swallow it into a clean reading.
- **Uncommitted changes are a different axis** and belong to `task unsettled`.
  This line reports commits only.

## 2. `endless task unlanded`

A sibling verb to `task landed`, sharing one implementation.

**Wiring.** Put the query in `task_cmd.py` beside `landed_list`, and register
two Click commands that differ only in the mode they pass. Bundle the shared
options with a decorator the way `rowcap.limit_options_for` already does — its
own docstring gives the reason: "One factory so the two flags cannot appear on
one command and not another, and so their help text is written once." E-967's
`task_cmd.add_command(task_show, name="detail")` is the precedent for a second
name over one callback. Nothing is duplicated; there is no Click obstacle.

**Two sections, because they need different actions.** Measured 2026-09-06:
109 shipped-terminal tasks have no landing row, 3 have a branch at all, and 1
holds anything main lacks.

- **Unlanded work** — a branch exists and the probe reports commits the base
  branch lacks. Actionable: land it, or reset the branch in place. This is the
  list that should be driven to zero.
- **No landing record** — no branch, or the branch holds nothing. Nothing to
  land; the record is missing. Not actionable by landing.

Rank the first section above the second and label both. Collapsing them into one
count would report ~109 outstanding items when 1 is actionable.

**Help text must contrast with its neighbour.** `task unlanded` and
`task unsettled` sit adjacent and look alike. Each opens by naming the
difference: `unsettled` asks whether a WORKTREE is modified or unlanded;
`unlanded` asks whether a TASK claims to be done while its work has not reached
the base branch.

**Reuse `--project`, `--all`, `--llm`, `--json` and the row cap.** Match
`task landed`'s option set exactly — that is the point of the shared decorator.

## 3. `project status` claim

One attention claim, counting the **first** section only. The second section is
a standing historical count and would become permanent furniture.

```
 ⊘ 3 unlanded (Run: task unlanded)
```

Glyph and one-word label join the legend beside the existing claims. Suppress
the row entirely at zero.

Keep this coupling THIN. `project status` is heading for major revisions in
another session; specify the claim (count, glyph, drill-down verb) and leave the
rendering to that work rather than designing a row about to be replaced.

## 4. The authority banner

`task show`, `decision show` and their siblings lead with a banner when the
record is not straightforwardly authoritative. The status line is already on
screen and is demonstrably not enough — it is read as provenance, not caveat.

**Triggers.** Task: `obsolete`, `declined`, or carrying a `replaced_by` or
`duplicated_by` relation. Decision: `rejected`, `superseded`, or `proposed`.
Current volume: of 1391 tasks, 270 are obsolete/declined, 84 replaced, 3
duplicated; of 179 decisions, 124 accepted, 36 proposed, 18 rejected, 1
superseded. Roughly one record in four triggers, so three in four stay clean and
the banner keeps meaning something.

**Two kinds, named as such.** "Not ever" (obsolete, declined, rejected,
replaced, superseded) and "not yet" (proposed). The wording must distinguish
them; a proposed decision is not a retired one.

**Shape follows E-2097, which has shipped.** Its rule: emit ONE dense line as
both the FIRST and LAST line, identical, not split, so whichever end survives a
`head -N` or `tail -N` is sufficient alone.

**Audience: agent-facing only.** Gate the whole banner on
`agent_help.agent_facing()`, which is `agent_env.present() or _AGENT_VIEW` — an
agent is reading, or a human passed `--agent-view` to see what one sees. Use
that function; do not re-spell the question. E-1966, E-2006 and E-2097 each
folded a separate spelling of it back into one place, and a fourth would undo
that.

A human running `task show` sees NOTHING new. The banner is not a caveat a human
needs — the status line and the `Replaced by:` link are already on screen and a
person reads them as the qualifiers they are. It exists because an agent does
not: it quotes the row as authoritative. So the banner is agent output, and a
human reaches it only by asking, with `--agent-view`, for debugging.

This is stricter than E-2097's split, and deliberately. There, the underlying
message is a REFUSAL that a human must see or the command fails silently, so
only the bracketing is agent-gated. Here there is no underlying message a human
is owed — the banner is additive — so the whole thing is gated.

Machine formats: `--json` carries the fact as a key rather than a repeated line,
since nothing truncates JSON by lines. `--llm` gets the bracketed form.

## 5. Guide

One paragraph next to §1's rendering, in the tasks section: a task status
answers "what did we decide about this work", never "where is the code". Point
at `task unlanded` for the latter, and at `task unsettled` for worktree state.

## 6. Data repair, same session

Fold this in rather than filing it (ED-1550 rule 2). Of the 109 shipped-terminal
tasks with no landing row, **20 have a commit on main attributed to them** and
should carry a landing record; 89 have no identifiable SHA and stay as they are.

Record each with `worktree land <id> --record-only --sha <sha>`.

**Verify every SHA before recording it.** The attribution came from grepping
commit messages, which over-credits: E-1048 was credited to a commit that merely
mentions it in the body while implementing E-1047. The bar is the one E-1150
met — its own description named the commit, and that commit is on main. A SHA
that cannot be verified to that standard is left unrecorded. Writing a
heuristic SHA into the table this report reads is the failure the report exists
to prevent.

This shrinks §2's second section. It does not affect the first.

## Verification

- `task show` on a terminal task with a landing row, without one and without a
  branch, and without one but with a branch holding commits — three distinct
  lines, no case rendering as blank.
- `task show` on a task whose branch is gone, and one whose probe errors —
  neither reads as clean.
- `task unlanded` sections ranked correctly, and `task unlanded --json` /
  `--llm` carrying the same split.
- `task unlanded --help` and `task unsettled --help` each name the other.
- On a repo whose default branch is NOT `main`, every rendering names that
  branch and none reports a false all-clear. `git grep -n '"main"'` over the
  code this task touches returns nothing.
- Banner appears on an obsolete task, a replaced task, a proposed decision, and
  a rejected decision; is absent on an accepted decision and a confirmed task;
  survives both `| head -3` and `| tail -3`.
- After §6, the 20 tasks appear under `task landed` and have left `task
  unlanded`'s second section.



---

## As landed — three departures from the plan above

**The E-2108 block dissolved rather than being worked around.** E-2108 landed
while this session was reading, so branches really are `task/<id>` and the
derivation this plan rests on is true. `worktree_cmd.task_branch(id)` is the one
construction site; nothing here reads a branch from a column or from git.

**§3 is SPECIFIED, not built** (Mike's call, asked and answered mid-session).
`project status`'s board deliberately carries no landedness marker today, and
computing the claim means a git probe per candidate task on a live-refreshing
view. The claim — count semantics (first section only), `⊘`, `task unlanded` as
the drill-down, suppressed at zero, and the measured cost — is recorded in
`internal/projectstatuscmd/board.go` beside the comment that currently explains
the marker's absence, which is where the session revising that board will read
it. No task was filed.

**§6 recorded ONE landing, not twenty.** The plan's figure came from grepping
commit messages, and the plan warned in the same breath that the grep
over-credits. Held to the bar the plan set — the commit's own subject names the
task, and the commit is on the base branch — exactly one of 129 candidates
qualifies: E-1186 at `e03b74e2`, whose subject is "Update E-971 plan: … (E-1186)"
and whose diff is the plan edit E-1186's own text describes. It is recorded.
Nothing else clears the bar: two candidates name a SHA in their own fields and
both point at another task's commit (E-1048 → E-787's, the over-credit the plan
names by example), and zero appear in a `Merge branch 'task/<id>'` subject. The
second section of `task unlanded` therefore stands at 122, not ~102.

**Also folded in, cheaper than the row describing it would be:** a
`shipped-terminal` group in the Go status registry (the population both surfaces
ask about, which no existing group named), and a `.endless/`-confined-commit
filter in the probe — without it the report lists one row per task branch in the
project (measured: 61 branches versus 3 holding source).

# Plan — one writer computes the unlanded verdict, every reader reads it

## The decision

The exact "does this branch hold work the base lacks?" verdict stops being
computed by its consumers and becomes **derived state owned by one background
job**. Consumers read a per-repo file cache. The reaper comes off the
PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook path entirely and becomes a job of its own.

This is one change, not two, because the reaper's periodic-sweep cost and the
monitor's continuous fan-out are the same defect: *the verdict is recomputed
from scratch by every consumer on every tick, with no shared derived state.*
Under ED-1550 §3 that is one cause, so it is one task.

## The invariant this rests on, and how it is checked rather than trusted

The unlanded set can only SHRINK as the base branch gains commits. The probe
asks, for each branch commit since the fork, whether a matching commit exists on
base since the fork. Adding commits to base only adds candidates to match
against: a commit that already matched keeps its match, and one that did not may
acquire one. Nothing that matched becomes unmatched.

Therefore:

- **A verdict of ZERO unlanded stays true as long as the BRANCH tip does not
  move**, no matter how far the base advances.
- **A verdict of N>0 is only valid while BOTH tips are unchanged**, because base
  movement can shrink it.

The invariant assumes the base is append-only. That assumption is CHECKED, not
trusted, by a repo-level watermark (below). An amended, reset, or force-pushed
base is detected and flushes the cache; a `--amend` on a task BRANCH moves the
branch tip and self-invalidates that one entry.

Two things the invariant deliberately does not cover, both pre-existing and
neither introduced here: work that landed and was later REVERTED still reads as
settled (the original landed commit is still in base's history to match
against), and uncommitted/untracked files are not commits at all — they are a
separate probe that stays live.

## The cache

**Location.** `<git-common-dir>/info/endless/unlanded/`

`git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` from inside any linked
worktree resolves to the main checkout's `.git`, so all worktrees of a repo
share one cache directory for free. Verified on git 2.52.0. `.git/info/` is
untracked, never pushed, per-clone, and survives `git gc` — the correct home for
derived state that describes this clone. No database involvement, so worktree
sandbox routing does not apply.

**One file per worktree**, named `<worktree-basename>-<8 hex of sha256(abs
path)>.json`. Per-file rather than one document so concurrent writers never
collide, pruning is an unlink, and a corrupt entry damages one worktree.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "worktree": "<absolute worktree path, stored for verification>",
  "branch_tip": "<OID of the worktree's HEAD when computed>",
  "base": "main",
  "base_tip": "<OID of base when computed>",
  "unlanded_count": 0,
  "unlanded_log": ["<short-sha> <subject>", "..."],
  "probe_error": "",
  "computed_at": "2026-09-09T04:12:33Z"
}
```

`unlanded_log` stays bounded by the existing `unlandedLogLimit`. `probe_error`
carries a failed compute so a reader reports undetermined rather than silently
clean — the fail-closed rule from E-1940 is preserved through the cache.

**Watermark**, `<git-common-dir>/info/endless/unlanded/watermark.json`:

```json
{ "version": 1, "base": "main", "base_tip": "<OID>", "verified_at": "..." }
```

**Validity protocol**, run once per process (not per row):

1. One call to `git worktree list --porcelain` yields every worktree path, every
   worktree's HEAD OID, and the base branch's own tip. **Measured: 14ms for 135
   worktrees on this repo.** This is the entire enumeration and tip-reading step.
2. Compare the base's current tip to `watermark.base_tip`.
   - Equal, and `watermark.base` equals the resolved base name → every entry is
     valid per its own rule below.
   - Different → `git merge-base --is-ancestor <watermark.base_tip> <current>`.
     - exit 0 → base only appended. Entries with `unlanded_count == 0` remain
       valid; entries with `unlanded_count > 0` are stale. The job advances the
       watermark; readers never write it.
     - exit 1 → base history was rewritten. Every entry is invalid; the job
       deletes the directory's entries and recomputes.
     - any other exit → fail closed. Treat every entry as a miss.
   - `watermark.base` differs from the resolved base name (config edit) → full
     invalidation, same as exit 1.
3. Per entry: valid iff `branch_tip` equals the worktree's current HEAD, AND
   (`unlanded_count == 0` OR `base_tip` equals the current base tip).

## Two jobs, not one

Different cadences, so splitting them is simpler than one job with internal
scheduling. Both follow the existing `internal/backupjob` shape — own package,
`init()` registers, `Name`/`Schedule`/`Run`.

**`internal/unlandedjob`** — name `worktree-unlanded`. `Interval: 60s`,
`LeaseTTL: 15m`. Runs the validity protocol, recomputes every invalid entry,
writes each atomically (temp file + rename in the same directory), advances the
watermark, and unlinks entries for worktrees git no longer lists. A cold pass
over 135 worktrees is ~1-2 min single-threaded; a warm pass is one 14ms git call
plus N small file reads. The lease generously exceeds the cold case.

`MaxBackoff` is zero, matching `backupjob`'s rationale: failures here are cheap
and idempotent, and backing off would leave the cache stale exactly when the
probe path is known to be sick. The runner's recorded fault is the alarm.

**`internal/reapjob`** — name `worktree-reap`. `Interval: 1h`,
`LeaseTTL: 15m`. Enumerates projects whose tracking is not off
(`monitor.GetTrackingMode(id) != "off"`) and calls the existing
`ReapWorktreesForProject` for each. `maybeReapWorktree` is unchanged except that
condition 4 reads the cache instead of running `reapNothingToLand` — and reads
it in COMPUTE-ON-MISS mode, because the reaper must never act on a guess.
Conditions 5 (`git status --porcelain`) and 3/5 (`WorktreeInUse`) stay live and
unchanged: a destructive decision re-verifies the filesystem itself.

This closes the leak the hotfix accepted. The reaper's condition 4 becomes the
exact content answer again, so a worktree whose work landed under rewritten SHAs
with no `task_landings` row is finally reclaimable — and ◆, `task unsettled` and
the reaper agree about "landed" again, which the hotfix broke on purpose.

## Who computes and who does not

**Never computes — cache-only:**
`monitor.AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` (the ◆ column in `session status` and
`session monitor`). A missing or invalid entry yields "not yet computed", never
a fabricated verdict. This is the change that removes the continuous range-diff
load: **measured 584ms per row for e-1077, gone from every tick of every pane.**

**Computes on a miss, and writes what it computed:**
- `session-query worktree-unsettled` (the Go entry point Python's `task
  unsettled` shells to) — a direct question deserves a real answer.
- `internal/reapjob` — it is the writer; a guess is not acceptable before a
  delete.
- `internal/unlandedjob` — likewise.

**Stays live everywhere, never cached:** `git status --porcelain`. Filesystem
state changes without any ref moving, so it has no honest cache key. Measured
15-27ms per worktree; a pane renders a handful of rows (this session's view
renders 2), so the live cost is tens of milliseconds per tick — three orders of
magnitude below the range-diff it replaces.

## The fourth marker state

`unsettledMark` currently has three states: `◆` unsettled, `⊙` no work product,
space settled. Cache-only reading introduces a fourth, transient state — "not
computed yet" — and collapsing it into either `◆` or space would be a lie the
column already refuses to tell.

New glyph: **`·` (U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT)**, width 1, meaning "not yet determined".
Within this column the distinction against `⊙` is ring versus no ring and
against `◆` is dot versus diamond — the same silhouette discipline E-2107 used.
Its faintness reads as absence of information rather than as a state, which is
what it is. It is visible only until the job's next pass, and the monitor tick
is what fires the job, so the window is one interval.

`buildLegend` documents it on any rendered row that bears it, like the other two.
Like `⊙`, it must not veto `dim`.

## Code changes

**`internal/monitor/unlanded_cache.go`** (new). The cache: entry type, path
resolution via `--git-common-dir`, `git worktree list --porcelain` parsing, the
watermark protocol, atomic write, prune, and the two read modes
(`CachedUnlanded` / `ComputeUnlandedAndCache`).

**`internal/monitor/worktree_unsettled.go`**. `worktreeUnsettledAt` gains a mode
parameter. `WorktreeUnsettledAt` (the ◆ path) becomes cache-only;
`WorktreeUnsettledDetailAt` (the on-demand path) computes on a miss.
`UnsettledDetail` gains `UnlandedKnown bool` and an accessor, distinct from the
existing `IsUndetermined()` — "not computed yet" is not "the probe failed".

**`internal/monitor/worktree_unlanded.go`**. `unlandedCommits` is unchanged; it
is now called only by the two computing paths.

**`internal/monitor/default_branch.go`**. Key `defaultBranchCache` on the git
COMMON dir rather than the worktree dir, so 135 worktrees share one memo within
a process instead of 135. Readers on the cache-only path get the base name from
`watermark.json` and do not resolve it at all — which removes the resolver from
the display path entirely, the ~60% the analysis measured.

**`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go`**. `maybeReapWorktree` condition 4 calls
the compute-on-miss cache read instead of `reapNothingToLand`; delete
`reapNothingToLand` and `landedSHAs` if nothing else uses them.
`AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` switches to the cache-only read.

**`internal/monitor/session_status.go`**. `SessionStatusRow` gains
`UnsettledKnown bool`.

**`internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go`**. `unsettledMark` gains the `·`
case; `buildLegend` learns it; `colorize` excludes it from vetoing dim.

**`internal/sessionstatuscmd/json.go`**. Add `"unsettled_known": bool`.
`"unsettled"` stays a bool (false when unknown) so existing consumers do not
break.

**`internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go`**. `newWorktreeUnsettledJSON`
carries the new field through to Python.

**`src/endless/task_cmd.py`**. `_unsettled_probe`'s no-worktree literal gains
`"unlanded_known": True`; `unsettled_item` renders "not yet computed" when it is
false. No SQLite added — this file already stays clear of it.

**`internal/hookcmd/claude.go`**. Remove all five `ReapWorktreesForProject`
calls (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd). Nothing
replaces them: the job runs on the existing `liveview` trigger, which already
fires `jobs.RunDue` on each monitor refresh behind a single-in-flight guard and
a database lease.

**`cmd/endless-go`**. Blank-import the two new job packages so their `init()`
registration runs, matching how the existing three are wired.

## Consequences accepted

- **No monitor running anywhere means nothing is reaped.** Reaping is a TTL-gated
  cleanup with a 14-day default; a machine with no monitor open for a while
  accumulates directories and reclaims them on the next monitor tick. On this
  project, jobs are suppressed inside self-dev worktrees, so it is the
  main-checkout monitor that drives both jobs — unchanged from how the existing
  three already behave. On a stranger's project `InSelfDevWorktree` is false and
  any monitor drives them.
- **A fresh clone shows `·` until the job's first pass.** One interval.
- **E-2113 still matters.** The job runs on a goroutine inside the monitor
  process, so Ctrl-C in a pane still kills in-flight git children and still
  records ERR-0010 against an innocent task. This change shrinks the window
  enormously — the probe is no longer running continuously — but does not close
  it. E-2113 is already filed and is not folded in.

## Not in scope

- **The shared per-repo patch-id index.** Filed separately as a `maybe` task. It
  would cut a cold miss from ~584ms to ~100ms, but every miss is now paid by a
  background job off any critical path, and a settled verdict survives base
  movement, so cold-miss storms are small. Measure before building it.
- **Reliable landing recording.** A fourth symptom, not this root cause. Worth
  doing for the ledger's own sake; not required to make this correct.
- **Rebasing worktrees onto the base to remove drift.** Reduces the cost of a
  miss by removing its input, but it is a separate mechanism with its own
  conflict and live-session hazards.

## Verification

- Go unit tests for the validity protocol against a fixture repo: append to base
  (settled entry survives, unsettled entry invalidates), amend base (full
  flush), amend the branch (that entry only), change the configured base name
  (full flush), missing watermark (everything a miss).
- A test asserting the cache-only read NEVER shells `git range-diff`, using the
  existing `test_seam.go` seam — this is the property the whole task exists for
  and it should fail loudly if a future edit reintroduces a compute on the
  display path.
- Existing `worktree_unsettled_test.go` / `reap_worktrees_test.go` suites must
  pass with condition 4 rewired.
- `TestUnsettledMark` extended for the fourth glyph's width and precedence.
- `tests/test_default_branch_parity.py` must still pass — the Python resolver is
  untouched.
- `just test` and `just test-go`.

payload.title: Share one per-repo patch-id index across worktrees instead of recomputing base patch-ids per probe
payload.description: The exact unlanded probe's cost is dominated by computing patch-ids for every commit the base gained since a worktree's fork, and every worktree recomputes them against substantially the same base history — measured 584ms for e-1077 against 135 worktrees that share one main. Build the index once per repo under <git-common-dir>/info/endless, appended incrementally as the base grows, so each worktree pays only for its own handful of commits: O(base commits + sum of branch commits) instead of O(worktrees x base commits). range-diff's similarity pairing, which is what catches a conflict-resolved landing, would run as a second stage over only the unmatched residue. Deferred from E-2111 deliberately: with the verdict computed by a background job and a settled verdict surviving base movement, every miss is off the critical path and cold-miss storms are small. Measure first; build only if misses actually hurt. Invalidation rides the same base-tip watermark E-2111 introduces.

triage.rationale: The on-disk index format/layout, incremental append protocol, and concurrency/locking model for multiple worktrees sharing and updating the same per-repo index are not specified.

payload.title: The exact unlanded verdict is derived state owned by one background job; no display surface ever computes it
payload.description: The exact 'does this branch hold work the base lacks?' answer (git range-diff, ~584ms/worktree) was recomputed by every consumer on every tick: the reaper on five hook branches including PreToolUse/PostToolUse, and thirteen session monitors re-probing every row every two seconds. One background job now computes it into a per-repo file cache under the git common dir; the reaper becomes a second, hourly job off the hook path; display surfaces read the cache and never compute, showing a distinct fourth marker state when no valid entry exists. It rests on an invariant — the unlanded set only shrinks as the base gains commits, so a zero verdict survives base movement while the branch tip holds — whose append-only premise is CHECKED by a base-tip watermark plus merge-base --is-ancestor, not assumed. Rejected: a cheaper inexact algorithm (git cherry misses conflict-resolved landings), and caching the working-tree dirty check (no honest cache key, and a delete must re-verify live).

```json
  "version": 1,
  "worktree": "<absolute worktree path, stored for verification>",
  "branch_tip": "<OID of the worktree's HEAD when computed>",
  "base": "main",
  "base_tip": "<OID of base when computed>",
  "unlanded_count": 0,
  "unlanded_log": ["<short-sha> <subject>", "..."],
  "probe_error": "",
  "computed_at": "2026-09-09T04:12:33Z"
}
```

`unlanded_log` stays bounded by the existing `unlandedLogLimit`. `probe_error`
carries a failed compute so a reader reports undetermined rather than silently
clean — the fail-closed rule from E-1940 is preserved through the cache.

**Watermark**, `<git-common-dir>/info/endless/unlanded/watermark.json`:

```json
{ "version": 1, "base": "main", "base_tip": "<OID>", "verified_at": "..." }
```

**Validity protocol**, run once per process (not per row):

1. One call to `git worktree list --porcelain` yields every worktree path, every
   worktree's HEAD OID, and the base branch's own tip. **Measured: 14ms for 135
   worktrees on this repo.** This is the entire enumeration and tip-reading step.
2. Compare the base's current tip to `watermark.base_tip`.
   - Equal, and `watermark.base` equals the resolved base name → every entry is
     valid per its own rule below.
   - Different → `git merge-base --is-ancestor <watermark.base_tip> <current>`.
     - exit 0 → base only appended. Entries with `unlanded_count == 0` remain
       valid; entries with `unlanded_count > 0` are stale. The job advances the
       watermark; readers never write it.
     - exit 1 → base history was rewritten. Every entry is invalid; the job
       deletes the directory's entries and recomputes.
     - any other exit → fail closed. Treat every entry as a miss.
   - `watermark.base` differs from the resolved base name (config edit) → full
     invalidation, same as exit 1.
3. Per entry: valid iff `branch_tip` equals the worktree's current HEAD, AND
   (`unlanded_count == 0` OR `base_tip` equals the current base tip).

## Two jobs, not one

Different cadences, so splitting them is simpler than one job with internal
scheduling. Both follow the existing `internal/backupjob` shape — own package,
`init()` registers, `Name`/`Schedule`/`Run`.

**`internal/unlandedjob`** — name `worktree-unlanded`. `Interval: 60s`,
`LeaseTTL: 15m`. Runs the validity protocol, recomputes every invalid entry,
writes each atomically (temp file + rename in the same directory), advances the
watermark, and unlinks entries for worktrees git no longer lists. A cold pass
over 135 worktrees is ~1-2 min single-threaded; a warm pass is one 14ms git call
plus N small file reads. The lease generously exceeds the cold case.

`MaxBackoff` is zero, matching `backupjob`'s rationale: failures here are cheap
and idempotent, and backing off would leave the cache stale exactly when the
probe path is known to be sick. The runner's recorded fault is the alarm.

**`internal/reapjob`** — name `worktree-reap`. `Interval: 1h`,
`LeaseTTL: 15m`. Enumerates projects whose tracking is not off
(`monitor.GetTrackingMode(id) != "off"`) and calls the existing
`ReapWorktreesForProject` for each. `maybeReapWorktree` is unchanged except that
condition 4 reads the cache instead of running `reapNothingToLand` — and reads
it in COMPUTE-ON-MISS mode, because the reaper must never act on a guess.
Conditions 5 (`git status --porcelain`) and 3/5 (`WorktreeInUse`) stay live and
unchanged: a destructive decision re-verifies the filesystem itself.

This closes the leak the hotfix accepted. The reaper's condition 4 becomes the
exact content answer again, so a worktree whose work landed under rewritten SHAs
with no `task_landings` row is finally reclaimable — and ◆, `task unsettled` and
the reaper agree about "landed" again, which the hotfix broke on purpose.

## Who computes and who does not

**Never computes — cache-only:**
`monitor.AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` (the ◆ column in `session status` and
`session monitor`). A missing or invalid entry yields "not yet computed", never
a fabricated verdict. This is the change that removes the continuous range-diff
load: **measured 584ms per row for e-1077, gone from every tick of every pane.**

**Computes on a miss, and writes what it computed:**
- `session-query worktree-unsettled` (the Go entry point Python's `task
  unsettled` shells to) — a direct question deserves a real answer.
- `internal/reapjob` — it is the writer; a guess is not acceptable before a
  delete.
- `internal/unlandedjob` — likewise.

**Stays live everywhere, never cached:** `git status --porcelain`. Filesystem
state changes without any ref moving, so it has no honest cache key. Measured
15-27ms per worktree; a pane renders a handful of rows (this session's view
renders 2), so the live cost is tens of milliseconds per tick — three orders of
magnitude below the range-diff it replaces.

## The fourth marker state

`unsettledMark` currently has three states: `◆` unsettled, `⊙` no work product,
space settled. Cache-only reading introduces a fourth, transient state — "not
computed yet" — and collapsing it into either `◆` or space would be a lie the
column already refuses to tell.

New glyph: **`·` (U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT)**, width 1, meaning "not yet determined".
Within this column the distinction against `⊙` is ring versus no ring and
against `◆` is dot versus diamond — the same silhouette discipline E-2107 used.
Its faintness reads as absence of information rather than as a state, which is
what it is. It is visible only until the job's next pass, and the monitor tick
is what fires the job, so the window is one interval.

`buildLegend` documents it on any rendered row that bears it, like the other two.
Like `⊙`, it must not veto `dim`.

## Code changes

**`internal/monitor/unlanded_cache.go`** (new). The cache: entry type, path
resolution via `--git-common-dir`, `git worktree list --porcelain` parsing, the
watermark protocol, atomic write, prune, and the two read modes
(`CachedUnlanded` / `ComputeUnlandedAndCache`).

**`internal/monitor/worktree_unsettled.go`**. `worktreeUnsettledAt` gains a mode
parameter. `WorktreeUnsettledAt` (the ◆ path) becomes cache-only;
`WorktreeUnsettledDetailAt` (the on-demand path) computes on a miss.
`UnsettledDetail` gains `UnlandedKnown bool` and an accessor, distinct from the
existing `IsUndetermined()` — "not computed yet" is not "the probe failed".

**`internal/monitor/worktree_unlanded.go`**. `unlandedCommits` is unchanged; it
is now called only by the two computing paths.

**`internal/monitor/default_branch.go`**. Key `defaultBranchCache` on the git
COMMON dir rather than the worktree dir, so 135 worktrees share one memo within
a process instead of 135. Readers on the cache-only path get the base name from
`watermark.json` and do not resolve it at all — which removes the resolver from
the display path entirely, the ~60% the analysis measured.

**`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go`**. `maybeReapWorktree` condition 4 calls
the compute-on-miss cache read instead of `reapNothingToLand`; delete
`reapNothingToLand` and `landedSHAs` if nothing else uses them.
`AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` switches to the cache-only read.

**`internal/monitor/session_status.go`**. `SessionStatusRow` gains
`UnsettledKnown bool`.

**`internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go`**. `unsettledMark` gains the `·`
case; `buildLegend` learns it; `colorize` excludes it from vetoing dim.

**`internal/sessionstatuscmd/json.go`**. Add `"unsettled_known": bool`.
`"unsettled"` stays a bool (false when unknown) so existing consumers do not
break.

**`internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go`**. `newWorktreeUnsettledJSON`
carries the new field through to Python.

**`src/endless/task_cmd.py`**. `_unsettled_probe`'s no-worktree literal gains
`"unlanded_known": True`; `unsettled_item` renders "not yet computed" when it is
false. No SQLite added — this file already stays clear of it.

**`internal/hookcmd/claude.go`**. Remove all five `ReapWorktreesForProject`
calls (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd). Nothing
replaces them: the job runs on the existing `liveview` trigger, which already
fires `jobs.RunDue` on each monitor refresh behind a single-in-flight guard and
a database lease.

**`cmd/endless-go`**. Blank-import the two new job packages so their `init()`
registration runs, matching how the existing three are wired.

## Consequences accepted

- **No monitor running anywhere means nothing is reaped.** Reaping is a TTL-gated
  cleanup with a 14-day default; a machine with no monitor open for a while
  accumulates directories and reclaims them on the next monitor tick. On this
  project, jobs are suppressed inside self-dev worktrees, so it is the
  main-checkout monitor that drives both jobs — unchanged from how the existing
  three already behave. On a stranger's project `InSelfDevWorktree` is false and
  any monitor drives them.
- **A fresh clone shows `·` until the job's first pass.** One interval.
- **E-2113 still matters.** The job runs on a goroutine inside the monitor
  process, so Ctrl-C in a pane still kills in-flight git children and still
  records ERR-0010 against an innocent task. This change shrinks the window
  enormously — the probe is no longer running continuously — but does not close
  it. E-2113 is already filed and is not folded in.

## Not in scope

- **The shared per-repo patch-id index.** Filed as E-2127 (`maybe`). It
  would cut a cold miss from ~584ms to ~100ms, but every miss is now paid by a
  background job off any critical path, and a settled verdict survives base
  movement, so cold-miss storms are small. Measure before building it.
- **Reliable landing recording.** A fourth symptom, not this root cause. Worth
  doing for the ledger's own sake; not required to make this correct.
- **Rebasing worktrees onto the base to remove drift.** Reduces the cost of a
  miss by removing its input, but it is a separate mechanism with its own
  conflict and live-session hazards.

## Verification

- Go unit tests for the validity protocol against a fixture repo: append to base
  (settled entry survives, unsettled entry invalidates), amend base (full
  flush), amend the branch (that entry only), change the configured base name
  (full flush), missing watermark (everything a miss).
- A test asserting the cache-only read NEVER shells `git range-diff`, using the
  existing `test_seam.go` seam — this is the property the whole task exists for
  and it should fail loudly if a future edit reintroduces a compute on the
  display path.
- Existing `worktree_unsettled_test.go` / `reap_worktrees_test.go` suites must
  pass with condition 4 rewired.
- `TestUnsettledMark` extended for the fourth glyph's width and precedence.
- `tests/test_default_branch_parity.py` must still pass — the Python resolver is
  untouched.
- `just test` and `just test-go`.

# Plan — an interrupted probe is not a failed probe

## The decision

A git child that died on **SIGINT** is not evidence about the worktree. The
probe stops recording ERR-0010 for it. Everything else about the verdict is
unchanged.

Three calls, all decided:

- **SIGINT only.** SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGKILL and every other signal keep
  recording. We have observed exactly one benign scenario — Ctrl-C in a pane
  reaching the git child through the shared foreground process group — so that
  is the one guarded. A SIGKILL is usually the OOM killer, and a `range-diff`
  big enough to be OOM-killed is a real operational fact. Widening the set later
  is a one-line change to `killedBySIGINT`; narrowing it after silence has hidden
  something is not.
- **Silent, but still `◆`.** No fault recorded; the verdict stays UNDETERMINED,
  so the row still marks and nothing is ever reported clean. E-1940's actual
  invariant — "a worktree nobody could inspect must not render as verified
  clean" — is preserved intact. What is removed is only the persistent incident.
- **Classification only.** No `context.Context`, no cancellation. See
  *Not in scope*.

## Why the classification lives in `runGit`

`runGit` is the single place every probe's git subprocess is created, so
classifying there means no caller can forget, and the resulting error carries
its own meaning to any depth via `errors.Is`. The alternative — a predicate
applied at each fault-recording site — spreads the same decision across four
call sites and grows a fifth the next time someone adds a probe.

`runGit` is a swappable `var` (`SetRunGitForTest`), so a stub bypasses the
classification. That is deliberate and useful: a stub returns an already-
classified error to exercise the guard, while `killedBySIGINT` is tested
directly against a real signalled process.

## What changes

### 1. Classify at the source

`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go`:

```go
// ErrGitInterrupted marks a git child that died on SIGINT rather than failing.
// A probe that was interrupted has said nothing about the worktree, so it is
// undetermined like any other unrunnable probe — but it is NOT an incident.
var ErrGitInterrupted = errors.New("git interrupted")

// killedBySIGINT reports that a child died on SIGINT specifically.
//
// Narrow on purpose (E-2113): SIGINT is the one signal observed reaching a
// probe benignly — Ctrl-C goes to the terminal's whole foreground process
// group, and monitor.runGit uses a plain exec.Command, so the git child is in
// it. SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGKILL still record; an OOM-killed probe is worth knowing
// about.
//
// On a platform whose ProcessState.Sys() is not a syscall.WaitStatus the type
// assertion fails and this returns false — the fault is recorded, which is
// today's behaviour and the safe direction.
func killedBySIGINT(err error) bool
```

`runGit` wraps: `err = fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrGitInterrupted, err)`.

### 2. Let the classification survive wrapping

`gitProbeError` (`worktree_unlanded.go`) stores `Detail string` and drops the
error chain, so `errors.Is` cannot reach through it. Add an `Err error` field
and `func (e gitProbeError) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }`, populated at the
three construction sites that wrap a real git failure (`merge-base`,
`rev-list` in `countRevs`, `range-diff`). The two synthetic ones — "no common
ancestor", "unparsable count" — leave it nil, which is correct: neither is a
subprocess failure.

### 3. Guard inside the recorders, not at their call sites

A guard at the call site is a rule each caller must remember. Put it in the
three functions that record a git-derived fault, so it cannot be forgotten:

- `recordProbeFault` — gains an `err error` parameter alongside the existing
  string detail, and returns early on `errors.Is(err, ErrGitInterrupted)`.
- `recordDefaultBranchFault` — already takes the error; add the check.
- `recordReapDefaultBranchFault` (`reap_worktrees.go`) — same.

The fourth `faults.Record` in the package (the worktree-lookup fault) is a
database error, not a subprocess, and is untouched.

### 4. Say "interrupted", not "failed"

`UndeterminedReason()` currently renders `git status failed: signal: interrupt`
— which is precisely the false statement this task exists to remove, on the one
surface (`task unsettled <id>`) whose whole job is explaining the marker.

`UnsettledDetail` gains `Interrupted bool`, set alongside the existing
`StatusErr`/`UnlandedErr`/`BaseErr`. `UndeterminedReason()` reads
`"<probe> interrupted"` when it is set.

**This is the one discretionary item in the plan.** It adds a field for a
wording fix and can be dropped without affecting the defect. It is included
because "failed" is the lie, not just the incident.

## What deliberately does not change

- The verdict. `IsUndetermined()` stays true, `Unsettled()` stays true, the row
  still reads `◆`.
- Any other signal. SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGKILL record exactly as today.
- The reaper's safety direction: an interrupted probe still refuses to reap.

## Not in scope

- **Cancellation.** Threading a `context.Context` so an interrupt cancels the
  sweep instead of racing it would touch `runGit`, `AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled`,
  `WorktreeUnsettledAt`, `TaskWorktreeUnsettledDetail`, `unlandedCommits`,
  `countRevs` and `DefaultBranch`, plus wiring `liveview`'s existing signal
  handler to a cancel func. It is a different change with a different risk
  profile, and E-2111 is underway on the same files.
- **E-2111's cache.** That work removes the git subprocess from the display path
  and so shrinks this window enormously — but does not close it: E-2111's plan
  says so itself, since its job runs on a goroutine inside the monitor process.
  The two are independent and either may land first.
- **`DefaultBranch` memoizing a failure.** `defaultBranchCache` stores errors as
  well as answers, so an interrupted resolve poisons the memo for the process
  lifetime. Harmless here (the process took SIGINT and is exiting) and
  pre-existing. Noted, not fixed.

## Verification

A new `internal/monitor/git_interrupt_test.go`:

- `killedBySIGINT` against **real** signalled processes — `sh -c 'kill -INT $$'`
  is true; `-TERM`, `-KILL` and `sh -c 'exit 3'` are false; a nil error and a
  non-`*exec.ExitError` are false. Real processes rather than a fabricated
  `os.ProcessState`, which is not constructible.
- The chain survives wrapping: a `gitProbeError` built over an interrupted
  error satisfies `errors.Is(err, ErrGitInterrupted)`, and one built over an
  ordinary failure does not.
- The guard, via a new `var recordFault = faults.Record` seam in
  `internal/monitor` — the same swappable-var idiom `runGit` and
  `hasLiveProcessInDir` already use in this package, and necessary because
  `faults.Record` writes straight to a database. With `runGit` stubbed to return
  a real interrupted error: **no fault recorded**, `IsUndetermined()` true,
  `Unsettled()` true. The contrast case — an ordinary git failure — records
  exactly one.
- `UndeterminedReason()` says "interrupted" for the interrupted case and keeps
  its existing wording for every other.

Regression: `go test ./internal/...`, `just test`, `go vet ./...`.

## Files touched

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go` | `ErrGitInterrupted`, `killedBySIGINT`, `runGit` wrap, `recordFault` seam, `recordReapDefaultBranchFault` guard |
| `internal/monitor/worktree_unlanded.go` | `gitProbeError.Err` + `Unwrap`, populated at three sites |
| `internal/monitor/worktree_unsettled.go` | `recordProbeFault`/`recordDefaultBranchFault` guards, `Interrupted` field, `UndeterminedReason` |
| `internal/monitor/git_interrupt_test.go` | new |

payload.title: Compute the exact unlanded verdict in one background job and read it from a content-addressed cache
payload.description: Implements ED-1589. The exact 'does this branch hold work the base lacks?' probe (git range-diff, measured 584ms per worktree) is recomputed by every consumer on every tick: the reaper on five hook branches including PreToolUse/PostToolUse, and every session monitor pane re-probing every rendered row every two seconds. Move it behind one background job that writes a content-addressed cache under the git common dir; add a second hourly job for the reaper and remove it from the hook path entirely; make the display path read-only with a fourth marker state for 'not yet determined'. Restores agreement between the reaper, the diamond marker and 'task unsettled' about what landed, which the E-2087 hotfix broke on purpose, and closes the reclamation leak it accepted. Plan attached.

triage.rationale: The description fully specifies the architecture (one background job, content-addressed cache under git common dir, hourly reaper job, hook path removal, read-only display with a new fourth marker state) with a plan attached, leaving no material design decision open.

fields.text:
# Plan — one writer computes the unlanded verdict, every reader reads it

Commits ED-1589. Defers the patch-id index to E-2127.

## The decision

The exact "does this branch hold work the base lacks?" verdict stops being
computed by its consumers and becomes **derived state owned by one background
job**. Consumers read a per-repo file cache. The reaper comes off the
PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook path entirely and becomes a job of its own.

This is one change, not two, because the reaper's periodic-sweep cost and the
monitor's continuous fan-out are the same defect: *the verdict is recomputed
from scratch by every consumer on every tick, with no shared derived state.*
Under ED-1550 §3 that is one cause, so it is one task.

## The invariant this rests on, and how it is checked rather than trusted

The unlanded set can only SHRINK as the base branch gains commits. The probe
asks, for each branch commit since the fork, whether a matching commit exists on
base since the fork. Adding commits to base only adds candidates to match
against: a commit that already matched keeps its match, and one that did not may
acquire one. Nothing that matched becomes unmatched.

Therefore:

- **A verdict of ZERO unlanded stays true as long as the BRANCH tip does not
  move**, no matter how far the base advances.
- **A verdict of N>0 is only valid while BOTH tips are unchanged**, because base
  movement can shrink it.

The invariant assumes the base is append-only. That assumption is CHECKED, not
trusted, by a repo-level watermark (below). An amended, reset, or force-pushed
base is detected and flushes the cache; a `--amend` on a task BRANCH moves the
branch tip and self-invalidates that one entry.

Two things the invariant deliberately does not cover, both pre-existing and
neither introduced here: work that landed and was later REVERTED still reads as
settled (the original landed commit is still in base's history to match
against), and uncommitted/untracked files are not commits at all — they are a
separate probe that stays live.

## The cache — content-addressed paths, no file format

**Location.** `<git-common-dir>/info/endless/unlanded/`

`git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` from inside any linked
worktree resolves to the main checkout's `.git`, so every worktree of a repo
shares one cache directory for free. Verified on git 2.52.0. `.git/info/` is
untracked, never pushed, per-clone, and survives `git gc` — the correct home for
derived state describing this clone. No database, so sandbox routing does not
apply and the probe stays DB-free (the property `_unsettled_probe` documents:
`--db main` from inside a worktree and a bare run agree by construction).

**Layout. There is no file format — every key is a path, and the only file with
contents holds exactly the bytes a consumer needs.**

```
<git-common-dir>/info/endless/unlanded/
  base-<name>                                  # 41 bytes: last-verified base tip OID
  settled/<branch-tip-oid>                     # EMPTY file. presence = fully landed.
  unsettled/<base-tip-oid>/<branch-tip-oid>    # unlanded commit lines, one per line
```

Why each piece carries no fields:

- **`settled/<branch-tip-oid>` is empty.** "Fully landed" is a property of the
  branch-tip OID and the base branch ALONE — same HEAD and same base give the
  same answer whichever directory the probe ran in — and the invariant above says
  it is permanent while the base is append-only. There is nothing left to qualify
  it with. Two worktrees at one OID legitimately share an entry.
- **`unsettled/<base-tip-oid>/<branch-tip-oid>` nests under the base tip.** A
  non-zero verdict is valid only until the base moves; nesting makes base movement
  render the whole directory unreachable, so INVALIDATION IS A PATH MISS requiring
  zero logic and zero stored field. Its contents are the exact lines
  `parseUnlandedRows` already produces, bounded by the existing `unlandedLogLimit`;
  the count is the line count.
- **`base-<name>` holds one OID.** The base NAME is in the filename, so editing
  `default_branch` in `.endless/config.json` orphans the old watermark
  automatically and reads as full invalidation.

Deliberately absent, each removable without breaking a rule: a format version
(the cache is rebuildable derived state, so an unreadable file is simply a miss
and no migration can ever be needed), the worktree path, a per-entry base name,
a stored probe error (absence already means unknown, and unknown already fails
closed — a failed compute writes nothing), and a computed-at timestamp (no
validity rule reads one). Nothing here can drift out of sync with git, because
every key IS a git object id.

**Validity protocol**, run once per process, not per row:

1. One call to `git worktree list --porcelain` yields every worktree path, every
   worktree's HEAD OID, and the base branch's own tip. **Measured: 14ms for 135
   worktrees on this repo.** That is the entire enumeration and tip-reading step.
2. Read `base-<name>`. Absent, or the name has changed → treat every `settled/`
   entry as a miss (the job then rebuilds). Equal to the current base tip →
   proceed. Different → `git merge-base --is-ancestor <stored> <current>`:
   - exit 0 → base only appended. Every `settled/` entry stands. The job writes
     the new tip; readers never write it.
   - exit 1 → base history was rewritten (amend, reset, force-push). Every
     `settled/` entry is invalid; the job empties `settled/` and recomputes.
   - any other exit → fail closed: every lookup is a miss.
3. Per worktree, with HEAD `B` and current base tip `T`: `settled/B` exists →
   settled. Else `unsettled/T/B` exists → unsettled, and its lines are the log.
   Else → not yet determined.

**Writes.** An empty `settled/` marker is a create-or-nothing operation with no
partial state. An `unsettled/` file is written temp-then-rename in the same
directory. The job prunes `settled/` entries matching no current worktree HEAD
and removes every `unsettled/` directory that is not the current base tip.

## Two jobs, not one

Different cadences, so splitting them is simpler than one job with internal
scheduling. Both follow the existing `internal/backupjob` shape — own package,
`init()` registers, `Name`/`Schedule`/`Run`.

**`internal/unlandedjob`** — name `worktree-unlanded`. `Interval: 60s`,
`LeaseTTL: 15m`. Runs the validity protocol, recomputes every invalid entry,
writes each atomically (temp file + rename in the same directory), advances the
watermark, and unlinks entries for worktrees git no longer lists. A cold pass
over 135 worktrees is ~1-2 min single-threaded; a warm pass is one 14ms git call
plus N small file reads. The lease generously exceeds the cold case.

`MaxBackoff` is zero, matching `backupjob`'s rationale: failures here are cheap
and idempotent, and backing off would leave the cache stale exactly when the
probe path is known to be sick. The runner's recorded fault is the alarm.

**`internal/reapjob`** — name `worktree-reap`. `Interval: 1h`,
`LeaseTTL: 15m`. Enumerates projects whose tracking is not off
(`monitor.GetTrackingMode(id) != "off"`) and calls the existing
`ReapWorktreesForProject` for each. `maybeReapWorktree` is unchanged except that
condition 4 reads the cache instead of running `reapNothingToLand` — and reads
it in COMPUTE-ON-MISS mode, because the reaper must never act on a guess.
Conditions 5 (`git status --porcelain`) and 3/5 (`WorktreeInUse`) stay live and
unchanged: a destructive decision re-verifies the filesystem itself.

This closes the leak the hotfix accepted. The reaper's condition 4 becomes the
exact content answer again, so a worktree whose work landed under rewritten SHAs
with no `task_landings` row is finally reclaimable — and ◆, `task unsettled` and
the reaper agree about "landed" again, which the hotfix broke on purpose.

## Who computes and who does not

**Never computes — cache-only:**
`monitor.AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` (the ◆ column in `session status` and
`session monitor`). A missing or invalid entry yields "not yet computed", never
a fabricated verdict. This is the change that removes the continuous range-diff
load: **measured 584ms per row for e-1077, gone from every tick of every pane.**

**Computes on a miss, and writes what it computed:**
- `session-query worktree-unsettled` (the Go entry point Python's `task
  unsettled` shells to) — a direct question deserves a real answer.
- `internal/reapjob` — it is the writer; a guess is not acceptable before a
  delete.
- `internal/unlandedjob` — likewise.

**Stays live everywhere, never cached:** `git status --porcelain`. Filesystem
state changes without any ref moving, so it has no honest cache key. Measured
15-27ms per worktree; a pane renders a handful of rows (this session's view
renders 2), so the live cost is tens of milliseconds per tick — three orders of
magnitude below the range-diff it replaces.

## The fourth marker state

`unsettledMark` currently has three states: `◆` unsettled, `⊙` no work product,
space settled. Cache-only reading introduces a fourth, transient state — "not
computed yet" — and collapsing it into either `◆` or space would be a lie the
column already refuses to tell.

New glyph: **`~` (U+007E TILDE)**, meaning "not yet determined".

`·` was the obvious pick and is WRONG: `sessionstatuscmd` already defines it as
`referencedGlyph` (in `relation_tier.go`) and `buildLegend` prints it as
`· referenced`. In a row, position disambiguates (unsettledMark precedes the id,
relationField follows it) — but the legend has no position, and a frame holding
both states would print `~ not yet determined  · referenced` on one line under
one glyph. Flagged by the E-2017 session.

`~` clears the whole vocabulary in play in a single frame — actions
`● ↑ ↩ ⟳ ▶ ⚑ ✎ ☑ ◷ ⏚ ⁇ ⇥ ◌`, unsettled `◆ ⊙`, phase `✓ ! 1 2 3 ?`, hidden `⊘`,
relation `⊕ ·`, block `⊗ ⏸`. Being ASCII it is display width 1 BY DEFINITION,
which sidesteps the East Asian Ambiguous trap that forced `⊙` to be asserted
rather than assumed (E-1765, E-2107) — the width test is still written, but it
cannot fail. Its silhouette is a horizontal wave, colliding with nothing in a
set of circles, diamonds, arrows and boxes; `◌` being taken is what rules out
every dotted-circle variant. "Approximate, unresolved" is the right reading.

It is visible only until the job's next pass, and the monitor tick is what fires
the job, so the window is one interval.

`buildLegend` documents it on any rendered row that bears it, like the other two.
Like `⊙`, it must not veto `dim`.

## Code changes

**`internal/monitor/unlanded_cache.go`** (new). Path resolution via
`--git-common-dir`, `git worktree list --porcelain` parsing, the watermark
protocol, marker write and prune, and the two read modes (`CachedUnlanded` /
`ComputeUnlandedAndCache`). No serialisation layer: there is no record type to
marshal.

**`internal/monitor/worktree_unsettled.go`**. `worktreeUnsettledAt` gains a mode
parameter. `WorktreeUnsettledAt` (the ◆ path) becomes cache-only;
`WorktreeUnsettledDetailAt` (the on-demand path) computes on a miss.
`UnsettledDetail` gains `UnlandedKnown bool` and an accessor, distinct from the
existing `IsUndetermined()` — "not computed yet" is not "the probe failed".

**`internal/monitor/worktree_unlanded.go`**. `unlandedCommits` is unchanged; it
is now called only by the two computing paths.

**`internal/monitor/default_branch.go`**. Key `defaultBranchCache` on the git
COMMON dir rather than the worktree dir, so 135 worktrees share one memo within
a process instead of 135. Readers on the cache-only path get the base name from
`watermark.json` and do not resolve it at all — which removes the resolver from
the display path entirely, the ~60% the analysis measured.

**`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go`**. `maybeReapWorktree` condition 4 calls
the compute-on-miss cache read instead of `reapNothingToLand`; delete
`reapNothingToLand` and `landedSHAs` if nothing else uses them.
`AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` switches to the cache-only read.

**`internal/monitor/session_status.go`**. `SessionStatusRow` gains
`UnsettledKnown bool`.

**`internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go`**. `unsettledMark` gains the `~`
case; `buildLegend` learns it; `colorize` excludes it from vetoing dim.

**`internal/sessionstatuscmd/json.go`**. Add `"unsettled_known": bool`.
`"unsettled"` stays a bool (false when unknown) so existing consumers do not
break.

**`internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go`**. `newWorktreeUnsettledJSON`
carries the new field through to Python.

**`src/endless/task_cmd.py`**. `_unsettled_probe`'s no-worktree literal gains
`"unlanded_known": True`; `unsettled_item` renders "not yet computed" when it is
false. No SQLite added — this file already stays clear of it.

**`internal/hookcmd/claude.go`**. Remove all five `ReapWorktreesForProject`
calls (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd). Nothing
replaces them: the job runs on the existing `liveview` trigger, which already
fires `jobs.RunDue` on each monitor refresh behind a single-in-flight guard and
a database lease.

**`cmd/endless-go`**. Blank-import the two new job packages so their `init()`
registration runs, matching how the existing three are wired.

## Consequences accepted

- **No monitor running anywhere means nothing is reaped.** Reaping is a TTL-gated
  cleanup with a 14-day default; a machine with no monitor open for a while
  accumulates directories and reclaims them on the next monitor tick. On this
  project, jobs are suppressed inside self-dev worktrees, so it is the
  main-checkout monitor that drives both jobs — unchanged from how the existing
  three already behave. On a stranger's project `InSelfDevWorktree` is false and
  any monitor drives them.
- **A fresh clone shows `·` until the job's first pass.** One interval.
- **E-2113 still matters.** The job runs on a goroutine inside the monitor
  process, so Ctrl-C in a pane still kills in-flight git children and still
  records ERR-0010 against an innocent task. This change shrinks the window
  enormously — the probe is no longer running continuously — but does not close
  it. E-2113 is already filed and is not folded in.

## Not in scope

- **The shared per-repo patch-id index.** Filed as E-2127 (`maybe`). It
  would cut a cold miss from ~584ms to ~100ms, but every miss is now paid by a
  background job off any critical path, and a settled verdict survives base
  movement, so cold-miss storms are small. Measure before building it.
- **Reliable landing recording.** A fourth symptom, not this root cause. Worth
  doing for the ledger's own sake; not required to make this correct.
- **Keeping worktrees in sync with the base.** Two jobs, filed separately:
  E-1881 (worktree metadata commits UP to main, which is what makes worktrees
  settle and become reapable) and its unfiled counterpart (main DOWN into idle
  worktrees, which collapses `baseRange` and is the only thing that removes the
  probe's cost at the source). E-1881 is a prerequisite for the second: it
  removes the overlapping-metadata commits that make a rebase conflict, which is
  the manual scenario E-1882 exists for. Both compose with this task rather than
  competing — a rebase moves the branch tip and invalidates that cache entry, but
  the recompute is then cheap by construction, because the drift it would have
  measured is exactly what the rebase removed.

## Verification

- Go unit tests for the validity protocol against a fixture repo: append to base
  (settled entry survives, unsettled entry invalidates), amend base (full
  flush), amend the branch (that entry only), change the configured base name
  (full flush), missing watermark (everything a miss).
- A test asserting the cache-only read NEVER shells `git range-diff`, using the
  existing `test_seam.go` seam — this is the property the whole task exists for
  and it should fail loudly if a future edit reintroduces a compute on the
  display path.
- Existing `worktree_unsettled_test.go` / `reap_worktrees_test.go` suites must
  pass with condition 4 rewired.
- `TestUnsettledMark` extended for the fourth glyph's width and precedence, and
  a legend test asserting no two rendered states share a glyph.
- `tests/test_default_branch_parity.py` must still pass — the Python resolver is
  untouched.
- `just test` and `just test-go`.

payload.title: Rebase idle worktree branches onto the base branch on a cadence to stop drift accumulating
payload.description: E-1881's counterpart and the other half of keeping worktrees in sync: E-1881 moves endless-managed metadata commits UP to main, which is what lets a worktree settle and become reclaimable; this is the DOWN direction, rebasing each idle worktree branch onto the base so the merge base moves forward. That collapses the range the exact unlanded probe pays for — its cost is proportional to how far the base drifted since the fork, not to what the branch holds — and makes a later land a fast-forward. Blocked by E-1881 rather than merely related: without it the branch still holds metadata commits main changed independently, so a rebase hits exactly the conflicts E-1882 exists to resolve by hand. Hard constraint: idle worktrees only, via the WorktreeInUse predicate the reaper shares with the other destructive path (E-1947).
payload.analysis:
## Why this is the other half, not a duplicate of E-1881

The two sync jobs fix opposite sides of the same subtraction, and neither
subsumes the other.

- **E-1881, worktree -> main.** Moves endless-managed metadata commits (plans,
  analyses, ledger) UP. Those commits are the bulk of what makes a long-lived
  branch read as holding unlanded work, so removing them is what lets a worktree
  SETTLE and become reclaimable. It does nothing for probe cost; by growing main
  faster it slightly increases the cost for every other worktree.
- **This task, main -> worktree.** Rebases an idle branch onto the base, moving
  the merge base forward. That collapses the range the exact unlanded probe
  actually pays for, and it settles nothing by itself.

## The cost model this exploits

The exact probe (`unlandedCommits`, via `git range-diff`) costs in proportion to
how far the base has drifted since the fork — the patch-ids it computes are for
every commit the BASE gained, not for what the branch holds. Measured on this
repo: a worktree 2251 commits behind costs 2.1s; e-1077, 648 commits behind,
costs 584ms. A branch sitting at the base tip has an empty base range and costs
almost nothing.

So this does not make the algorithm cheaper — it removes the input that makes
the algorithm expensive.

## Why E-1881 blocks this rather than merely relating to it

Without E-1881, the branch still holds metadata commits that main changed
independently. Rebasing then hits exactly the overlapping-edit conflicts that
E-1882 (`endless worktree reconcile`) exists to resolve by hand — the scenario
that cost ~20 minutes of manual investigation during the E-1537 land. E-1881
running continuously leaves little on the branch to conflict with, which is what
makes an unattended rebase safe.

## Hard constraint

Only worktrees with NO live session and no process holding cwd inside, via the
same `WorktreeInUse` predicate the reaper shares with the other destructive
path (E-1947). A rebase rewrites history underneath whoever is sitting in the
directory. This is not a tunable.

## Interactions

- **E-2128.** A rebase moves the branch tip, invalidating that worktree's cached
  verdict. They compose rather than fight: the recompute is cheap by
  construction, because the drift it would have measured is what the rebase just
  removed.
- **E-1109** (`merge-vs-rebase` config preference) decides the mechanism. Rebase
  matches what `worktree land` already does; a merge is gentler but leaves merge
  commits on every task branch.

triage.rationale: The cadence/trigger, conflict-handling policy when a rebase fails, and how the "exact unlanded probe" cost accounting integrates with the rebase are not specified beyond naming the goal and dependency.

fields.outcome:
# What the brainstorm determined

## The framing was one problem wearing two costumes

The task was filed about the reaper: an exact `git range-diff` probe on
PreToolUse/PostToolUse cost ~90s per sweep and stopped the product, so it was
reverted to the cheap SHA check and its known leak. Measurement during the
brainstorm found the larger load elsewhere — the DISPLAY path, where every
`session monitor` pane re-probes every rendered row every two seconds with no
sharing between processes, keeping 4-6 range-diffs in flight at every sampled
instant.

Those are one cause, not two: **the exact verdict is recomputed from scratch by
every consumer on every tick, with no shared derived state.** Under ED-1550 that
is one task. Accepted as ED-1589; implemented by E-2128.

## The invariant that makes exactness affordable

The unlanded set can only SHRINK as the base gains commits. The probe asks, per
branch commit since the fork, whether a matching commit exists on the base since
the fork; adding commits to the base only adds candidates to match against, so a
commit that matched keeps its match and one that did not may acquire one.

Therefore a verdict of ZERO stays true as long as the BRANCH tip does not move,
however far the base advances — which is the majority of worktrees and exactly
the population the reaper cares about. A verdict of N>0 is valid only while both
tips hold.

This collapsed most of the options in the seed analysis into one. The
cold-cache-after-a-land objection to caching largely evaporates, because a land
invalidates only the worktrees that were already unsettled.

The append-only premise it rests on is CHECKED, not assumed: a base-tip
watermark plus `git merge-base --is-ancestor` detects an amended, reset or
force-pushed base and flushes. An amend on a task BRANCH moves that branch's tip
and self-invalidates one entry. Two cases deliberately not covered, both
pre-existing: work that landed and was later reverted still reads as settled,
and uncommitted or untracked files are not commits at all — a separate probe
that stays live.

## Measurements that decided the design

- `git worktree list --porcelain` returns every worktree's HEAD **and** the base
  tip in **14ms for 135 worktrees**. One git call is the entire validity check
  for a whole repo, which is what makes a cache-only display path essentially
  free.
- `git range-diff` costs **584ms** for a worktree 648 commits behind the base,
  and 2.1s for one 2251 behind. The cost tracks DRIFT, not what the branch
  holds.
- `git status --porcelain` costs **15-27ms** per worktree. Three orders of
  magnitude below range-diff, so keeping the dirty check live is affordable and
  it has no honest cache key anyway.

## Decisions taken

1. **One writer, many readers.** A background job computes the verdict; the
   display path reads and never computes, rendering a fourth marker state when
   no valid entry exists. This is the seam the planned move away from tmux needs
   regardless, so it is infrastructure rather than an optimisation.
2. **The reaper comes off the hook path entirely** and becomes a second job on
   an hourly cadence, triggered by the existing `liveview` job runner. A
   destructive sweep does not belong before and after every tool call at any
   price. Accepted cost: with no monitor running anywhere, nothing is reclaimed
   until one is.
3. **No file format.** The cache is content-addressed paths under the git common
   dir — an empty `settled/<branch-tip-oid>` marker, an
   `unsettled/<base-tip-oid>/<branch-tip-oid>` file holding the commit lines,
   and one 41-byte watermark. Base movement makes stale entries unreachable, so
   invalidation is a path miss requiring no logic and no stored field. Nothing
   can drift out of sync because every key IS a git object id.
4. **Not the database.** A new runtime table would have been legitimate (`jobs`,
   `errors`, `triage_claims` are written directly and never enter the ledger),
   but E-2087 deliberately made this probe DB-free and `_unsettled_probe`
   documents what that buys: `--db main` from inside a worktree and a bare run
   agree by construction. A verdict in SQLite breaks it — from a worktree the
   read resolves the per-worktree sandbox and finds nothing. The tasks table is
   doubly wrong: `unsettled_item` explicitly serves worktrees with no task row,
   and `tasks` is ledger-projected, so a per-minute verdict would write
   permanent churn into the durable record.
5. **Keeping worktrees in sync needs BOTH directions.** E-1881 (worktree ->
   main) is what lets a worktree settle and become reclaimable; it does nothing
   for probe cost. E-2129 (main -> idle worktrees) collapses the drift the probe
   pays for; it settles nothing. E-1881 is a prerequisite, not an alternative:
   without it a rebase hits the overlapping-metadata conflicts E-1882 exists to
   resolve by hand.

## Directions weighed and set aside

- **A cheaper inexact algorithm.** `git cherry` is ~3x faster but misses
  conflict-resolved landings; subject-plus-author-date pairing is ~35x faster but
  disagrees with range-diff in BOTH directions. Neither is safe alone, and once
  exactness is cached the trade stops being necessary.
- **A shared per-repo patch-id index** (E-2127, `maybe`). Real, and it would cut
  a cold miss roughly tenfold — but every miss is now paid by a background job
  off any critical path, and settled verdicts survive base movement, so
  cold-miss storms are small. Measure before building.
- **Fixing the landing-recording gap.** The seed offered it as possibly the root
  cause. It is a fourth symptom: once exactness is cheap, unreliable
  `task_landings` rows stop being load-bearing for this question. Worth doing for
  the ledger's own sake, not to make this correct.

## Loose end left deliberately

E-2113 (a probe killed by a signal recorded as a fault) is unaffected. The job
runs on a goroutine inside the monitor process, so Ctrl-C still kills in-flight
git children. This work shrinks the window enormously — the probe stops running
continuously — but does not close it. Already filed; not folded in.

fields.text:
# Plan — an interrupted probe is not a failed probe

## The decision

A git child that died on **SIGINT** is not evidence about the worktree. The
probe stops recording ERR-0010 for it. Everything else about the verdict is
unchanged.

Three calls, all decided:

- **SIGINT only.** SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGKILL and every other signal keep
  recording. We have observed exactly one benign scenario — Ctrl-C in a pane
  reaching the git child through the shared foreground process group — so that
  is the one guarded. A SIGKILL is usually the OOM killer, and a `range-diff`
  big enough to be OOM-killed is a real operational fact. Widening the set later
  is a one-line change to `killedBySIGINT`; narrowing it after silence has hidden
  something is not.
- **Silent, but still `◆`.** No fault recorded; the verdict stays UNDETERMINED,
  so the row still marks and nothing is ever reported clean. E-1940's actual
  invariant — "a worktree nobody could inspect must not render as verified
  clean" — is preserved intact. What is removed is only the persistent incident.
- **Classification only.** No `context.Context`, no cancellation. See
  *Not in scope*.

## Why the classification lives in `runGit`

`runGit` is the single place every probe's git subprocess is created, so
classifying there means no caller can forget, and the resulting error carries
its own meaning to any depth via `errors.Is`. The alternative — a predicate
applied at each fault-recording site — spreads the same decision across four
call sites and grows a fifth the next time someone adds a probe.

`runGit` is a swappable `var` (`SetRunGitForTest`), so a stub bypasses the
classification. That is deliberate and useful: a stub returns an already-
classified error to exercise the guard, while `killedBySIGINT` is tested
directly against a real signalled process.

## What changes

### 1. Classify at the source

`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go`:

```go
// ErrGitInterrupted marks a git child that died on SIGINT rather than failing.
// A probe that was interrupted has said nothing about the worktree, so it is
// undetermined like any other unrunnable probe — but it is NOT an incident.
var ErrGitInterrupted = errors.New("git interrupted")

// killedBySIGINT reports that a child died on SIGINT specifically.
//
// Narrow on purpose (E-2113): SIGINT is the one signal observed reaching a
// probe benignly — Ctrl-C goes to the terminal's whole foreground process
// group, and monitor.runGit uses a plain exec.Command, so the git child is in
// it. SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGKILL still record; an OOM-killed probe is worth knowing
// about.
//
// On a platform whose ProcessState.Sys() is not a syscall.WaitStatus the type
// assertion fails and this returns false — the fault is recorded, which is
// today's behaviour and the safe direction.
func killedBySIGINT(err error) bool
```

`runGit` wraps: `err = fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrGitInterrupted, err)`.

### 2. Let the classification survive wrapping

`gitProbeError` (`worktree_unlanded.go`) stores `Detail string` and drops the
error chain, so `errors.Is` cannot reach through it. Add an `Err error` field
and `func (e gitProbeError) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }`, populated at the
three construction sites that wrap a real git failure (`merge-base`,
`rev-list` in `countRevs`, `range-diff`). The two synthetic ones — "no common
ancestor", "unparsable count" — leave it nil, which is correct: neither is a
subprocess failure.

### 3. Guard inside the recorders, not at their call sites

A guard at the call site is a rule each caller must remember. Put it in the
three functions that record a git-derived fault, so it cannot be forgotten:

- `recordProbeFault` — gains an `err error` parameter alongside the existing
  string detail, and returns early on `errors.Is(err, ErrGitInterrupted)`.
- `recordDefaultBranchFault` — already takes the error; add the check.
- `recordReapDefaultBranchFault` (`reap_worktrees.go`) — same.

The fourth `faults.Record` in the package (the worktree-lookup fault) is a
database error, not a subprocess, and is untouched.

### 4. Say "interrupted", not "failed"

`UndeterminedReason()` currently renders `git status failed: signal: interrupt`
— which is precisely the false statement this task exists to remove, on the one
surface (`task unsettled <id>`) whose whole job is explaining the marker.

`UnsettledDetail` gains `Interrupted bool`, set alongside the existing
`StatusErr`/`UnlandedErr`/`BaseErr`. `UndeterminedReason()` reads
`"<probe> interrupted"` when it is set.

**This is the one discretionary item in the plan.** It adds a field for a
wording fix and can be dropped without affecting the defect. It is included
because "failed" is the lie, not just the incident.

## What deliberately does not change

- The verdict. `IsUndetermined()` stays true, `Unsettled()` stays true, the row
  still reads `◆`.
- Any other signal. SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGKILL record exactly as today.
- The reaper's safety direction: an interrupted probe still refuses to reap.

## Not in scope

- **Cancellation.** Threading a `context.Context` so an interrupt cancels the
  sweep instead of racing it would touch `runGit`, `AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled`,
  `WorktreeUnsettledAt`, `TaskWorktreeUnsettledDetail`, `unlandedCommits`,
  `countRevs` and `DefaultBranch`, plus wiring `liveview`'s existing signal
  handler to a cancel func. It is a different change with a different risk
  profile, and E-2111 is underway on the same files.
- **E-2111's cache.** That work removes the git subprocess from the display path
  and so shrinks this window enormously — but does not close it: E-2111's plan
  says so itself, since its job runs on a goroutine inside the monitor process.
  The two are independent and either may land first.
- **`DefaultBranch` memoizing a failure.** `defaultBranchCache` stores errors as
  well as answers, so an interrupted resolve poisons the memo for the process
  lifetime. Harmless here (the process took SIGINT and is exiting) and
  pre-existing. Noted, not fixed.

## Verification

A new `internal/monitor/git_interrupt_test.go`:

- `killedBySIGINT` against **real** signalled processes — `sh -c 'kill -INT $$'`
  is true; `-TERM`, `-KILL` and `sh -c 'exit 3'` are false; a nil error and a
  non-`*exec.ExitError` are false. Real processes rather than a fabricated
  `os.ProcessState`, which is not constructible.
- The chain survives wrapping: a `gitProbeError` built over an interrupted
  error satisfies `errors.Is(err, ErrGitInterrupted)`, and one built over an
  ordinary failure does not.
- The guard, via a new `var recordFault = faults.Record` seam in
  `internal/monitor` — the same swappable-var idiom `runGit` and
  `hasLiveProcessInDir` already use in this package, and necessary because
  `faults.Record` writes straight to a database. With `runGit` stubbed to return
  a real interrupted error: **no fault recorded**, `IsUndetermined()` true,
  `Unsettled()` true. The contrast case — an ordinary git failure — records
  exactly one.
- `UndeterminedReason()` says "interrupted" for the interrupted case and keeps
  its existing wording for every other.

Regression: `go test ./internal/...`, `just test`, `go vet ./...`.

## Files touched

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go` | `ErrGitInterrupted`, `killedBySIGINT`, `runGit` wrap, `recordFault` seam, `recordReapDefaultBranchFault` guard |
| `internal/monitor/worktree_unlanded.go` | `gitProbeError.Err` + `Unwrap`, populated at three sites |
| `internal/monitor/worktree_unsettled.go` | `recordProbeFault`/`recordDefaultBranchFault` guards, `Interrupted` field, `UndeterminedReason` |
| `internal/monitor/git_interrupt_test.go` | new |
