## As built — two departures from the letter of this plan

Both are recorded here because a reviewer reading the plan against the diff
would otherwise have to work out whether they were deliberate.

### A fourth `gitProbeError` site, not three

The plan states the rule — populate `Err` at "the construction sites that wrap
a real git failure" — and then enumerates three (`merge-base`, `rev-list`,
`range-diff`). There are four: `commitLines`'s `git log`, taken when the base
branch has not moved since the fork, wraps a real git failure too. It was
populated along with the other three. Leaving it out would have left one probe
structurally unable to be recognised as interrupted, by the plan's own rule.

The two synthetic errors ("no common ancestor", "unparsable count") leave `Err`
nil exactly as planned.

### No `recordFault` seam

The plan proposed `var recordFault = faults.Record` so a test could observe
whether a fault was recorded. `internal/monitor` already has
`bindFaultsForTest` (worktree_unsettled_faults_test.go), which points the
faults package at a fresh in-memory store — E-1940's own dedup tests use it.
The new tests use that instead, which asserts against the REAL recorder and its
real persistence rather than a stub, and adds no production surface.

### Verification, as built

`.endless/tasks/e-2113/verify.sh` — 25 assertions. Every signal case drives a
REAL child (`os.ProcessState` is not constructible), and the end-to-end
sections build `cmd/endless-go` from the tree and run it against a scratch repo
with a `git` shim that interrupts, terminates, or fails on demand.

Each of the three guards was mutation-tested: removing the `recordProbeFault`
guard, the `Unwrap`, or the `runGit` wrap each turns the suite red, and the
first reproduces the reported incident verbatim — `E-1972: git range-diff
failed for its worktree`.

### Still not in scope, and now with a reason to state

`DefaultBranch` collapses every git error into `ErrDefaultBranchUnresolved`, so
an interrupted `symbolic-ref`/`rev-parse` during resolution surfaces as that
sentinel and the guards on `recordDefaultBranchFault` /
`recordReapDefaultBranchFault` cannot see the interrupt. Those guards are
therefore structural — correct however the resolver's error handling changes,
unreachable through it today. Making the resolver propagate would change the
fall-through contract of `branchIfExists`/`originHeadBranch`/`gitConfigValue`,
which is a different change with a different risk profile.

fields.title: A display never computes an expensive answer to paint a row — it reads a precomputed one, or shows that it is not known yet
fields.description: Checking whether a worktree still holds work that has not reached main takes about half a second, and costs more the further that worktree has drifted rather than the more it holds. Every status pane recomputed the check for every row it painted, every two seconds, so that half-second became a continuous multi-core load that multiplied with each pane opened — and the same check on the tool-call path had already made every tool call take ninety seconds. The rule: a surface that repaints on a timer reads an answer something else computed, and when no answer is available it says so with its own marker rather than blocking or guessing. Guessing is the part that matters — an unavailable answer used to render as 'nothing outstanding here', the one wrong answer that costs someone work. Rejected: keeping the check inline by making it cheap, since every faster algorithm was also wrong in ways that mattered; and letting a display fall back to an approximation, which leaves two surfaces disagreeing about one question.

payload.title: A destructive sweep runs on a schedule, never from a hook on the tool-call path
payload.description: The worktree reaper removes directories, and it ran from five branches of the hook handler including PreToolUse and PostToolUse — a delete sweep before and after every tool call in every session. Its cost scales with the number of worktrees, which is unbounded, so any change to what it checks re-prices every tool call: making the check exact took one sweep to ninety seconds and stopped the product. Reverting to the cheap check left it at 2.58 seconds, still paid twice per call. The rule is about shape rather than the current measurement — a sweep whose cost scales with an unbounded set, and whose failure mode is deleting a directory someone still needs, does not belong on a path that runs thousands of times a day. Rejected: debouncing inside the hook, since each hook invocation is a fresh process with nowhere to keep the debounce state. Accepted cost: where nothing triggers the schedule, directories accumulate until something does.

fields.description: Checking whether a worktree still holds work that has not reached main takes about half a second, and costs more the further that worktree has drifted from main rather than the more it holds. Every status pane recomputed the check for every row it painted, every two seconds, so that half-second became a continuous multi-core load that multiplied with each pane opened — and the same check on the tool-call path had already made every tool call take ninety seconds. The rule: a surface that repaints on a timer reads a value a background job wrote, and renders a distinct marker when no value is available. Before this, an unavailable answer rendered as 'nothing outstanding here' — a false all-clear on a worktree that still held unlanded work. Rejected: keeping the check inline by making it cheap, since every faster algorithm was also wrong in ways that mattered; and letting a display fall back to an approximation, which leaves two surfaces disagreeing about one question.

payload.reason: Mike, on review: overbroad and wrong on the mechanism. It generalises an absolute prohibition from one use case, and it prescribes a schedule for the reaper, which was never approved. The reaper should run on 'endless worktree land', where its output is visible to the person who caused the worktrees to become reclaimable — and worktree_cmd.land_worktree ALREADY does exactly that via _reap_stale_worktrees, so the mechanism this decision proposed was both unwanted and unnecessary. Removing the reaper from the five hook call sites remains part of E-2128; it needs no decision to justify it. A scheduled reap with an activity indicator may become right after Endless replaces the tmux UI, at which point it is a fresh decision made with more than one use case in hand.

fields.text:
# Plan — one writer computes the unlanded verdict, every reader reads it

Commits ED-1589. Defers the patch-id index to E-2127, and the two
worktree-sync jobs to E-1881 and E-2129.

## The decision

The exact "does this branch hold work the base lacks?" verdict stops being
computed by its consumers and becomes **derived state owned by one background
job**. Consumers read a per-repo file cache. The reaper comes off the
PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook path entirely and becomes a job of its own.

This is one change, not two, because the reaper's periodic-sweep cost and the
monitor's continuous fan-out are the same defect: *the verdict is recomputed
from scratch by every consumer on every tick, with no shared derived state.*
Under ED-1550 §3 that is one cause, so it is one task.

## The invariant this rests on, and how it is checked rather than trusted

The unlanded set can only SHRINK as the base branch gains commits. The probe
asks, for each branch commit since the fork, whether a matching commit exists on
base since the fork. Adding commits to base only adds candidates to match
against: a commit that already matched keeps its match, and one that did not may
acquire one. Nothing that matched becomes unmatched.

Therefore:

- **A verdict of ZERO unlanded stays true as long as the BRANCH tip does not
  move**, no matter how far the base advances.
- **A verdict of N>0 is only valid while BOTH tips are unchanged**, because base
  movement can shrink it.

The invariant assumes the base is append-only. That assumption is CHECKED, not
trusted, by a repo-level watermark (below). An amended, reset, or force-pushed
base is detected and flushes the cache; a `--amend` on a task BRANCH moves the
branch tip and self-invalidates that one entry.

Two things the invariant deliberately does not cover, both pre-existing and
neither introduced here: work that landed and was later REVERTED still reads as
settled (the original landed commit is still in base's history to match
against), and uncommitted/untracked files are not commits at all — they are a
separate probe that stays live.

## The cache — content-addressed paths, no file format

**Location.** `<git-common-dir>/info/endless/unlanded/`

`git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` from inside any linked
worktree resolves to the main checkout's `.git`, so every worktree of a repo
shares one cache directory for free. Verified on git 2.52.0. `.git/info/` is
untracked, never pushed, per-clone, and survives `git gc` — the correct home for
derived state describing this clone. No database, so sandbox routing does not
apply and the probe stays DB-free (the property `_unsettled_probe` documents:
`--db main` from inside a worktree and a bare run agree by construction).

**Layout. There is no file format — every key is a path, and the only file with
contents holds exactly the bytes a consumer needs.**

```
<git-common-dir>/info/endless/unlanded/
  base-<name>                                  # 41 bytes: last-verified base tip OID
  settled/<branch-tip-oid>                     # EMPTY file. presence = fully landed.
  unsettled/<base-tip-oid>/<branch-tip-oid>    # unlanded commit lines, one per line
```

Why each piece carries no fields:

- **`settled/<branch-tip-oid>` is empty.** "Fully landed" is a property of the
  branch-tip OID and the base branch ALONE — same HEAD and same base give the
  same answer whichever directory the probe ran in — and the invariant above says
  it is permanent while the base is append-only. There is nothing left to qualify
  it with. Two worktrees at one OID legitimately share an entry.
- **`unsettled/<base-tip-oid>/<branch-tip-oid>` nests under the base tip.** A
  non-zero verdict is valid only until the base moves; nesting makes base movement
  render the whole directory unreachable, so INVALIDATION IS A PATH MISS requiring
  zero logic and zero stored field. Its contents are the exact lines
  `parseUnlandedRows` already produces, bounded by the existing `unlandedLogLimit`;
  the count is the line count.
- **`base-<name>` holds one OID.** The base NAME is in the filename, so editing
  `default_branch` in `.endless/config.json` orphans the old watermark
  automatically and reads as full invalidation.

Deliberately absent, each removable without breaking a rule: a format version
(the cache is rebuildable derived state, so an unreadable file is simply a miss
and no migration can ever be needed), the worktree path, a per-entry base name,
a stored probe error (absence already means unknown, and unknown already fails
closed — a failed compute writes nothing), and a computed-at timestamp (no
validity rule reads one). Nothing here can drift out of sync with git, because
every key IS a git object id.

**Validity protocol**, run once per process, not per row:

1. One call to `git worktree list --porcelain` yields every worktree path, every
   worktree's HEAD OID, and the base branch's own tip. **Measured: 14ms for 135
   worktrees on this repo.** That is the entire enumeration and tip-reading step.
2. Read `base-<name>`. Absent, or the name has changed → treat every `settled/`
   entry as a miss (the job then rebuilds). Equal to the current base tip →
   proceed. Different → `git merge-base --is-ancestor <stored> <current>`:
   - exit 0 → base only appended. Every `settled/` entry stands. The job writes
     the new tip; readers never write it.
   - exit 1 → base history was rewritten (amend, reset, force-push). Every
     `settled/` entry is invalid; the job empties `settled/` and recomputes.
   - any other exit → fail closed: every lookup is a miss.
3. Per worktree, with HEAD `B` and current base tip `T`: `settled/B` exists →
   settled. Else `unsettled/T/B` exists → unsettled, and its lines are the log.
   Else → not yet determined.

**Writes.** An empty `settled/` marker is a create-or-nothing operation with no
partial state. An `unsettled/` file is written temp-then-rename in the same
directory. The job prunes `settled/` entries matching no current worktree HEAD
and removes every `unsettled/` directory that is not the current base tip.

## One job, plus the reap trigger that already exists

**`internal/unlandedjob`** — name `worktree-unlanded`. `Interval: 60s`,
`LeaseTTL: 15m`. Follows the existing `internal/backupjob` shape: own package,
`init()` registers, `Name`/`Schedule`/`Run`. It runs the validity protocol,
recomputes every invalid entry, writes each marker, advances the watermark, and
prunes entries for worktrees git no longer lists. A cold pass over 135
worktrees is ~1-2 min single-threaded; a warm pass is one 14ms git call plus N
path lookups. The lease exceeds the cold case.

`MaxBackoff` is zero, matching `backupjob`'s rationale: failures here are cheap
and idempotent, and backing off would leave the cache stale exactly when the
probe path is known to be sick. The runner's recorded fault is the alarm.

It is triggered by the existing `liveview` job runner, which already fires
`jobs.RunDue` on each monitor refresh behind a single-in-flight guard and a
database lease. Nothing new is wired.

**The reaper gets no job and no new trigger.** It already runs where it should:
`worktree_cmd.land_worktree` calls `_reap_stale_worktrees(main_root)` as a
post-land best-effort sweep, shelling to `endless-go event reap-worktrees` with
stderr forwarded so reaped directories are printed to the person who ran the
land. That is the right moment and the right visibility — a land is what makes
other worktrees reclaimable, and the person who caused the reclamation sees what
was reclaimed. This task neither moves it nor adds a cadence to it.

What DOES change in the reaper: `maybeReapWorktree`'s condition 4 reads the
cache in COMPUTE-ON-MISS mode instead of running `reapNothingToLand`, because a
delete must never act on a guess. Conditions 5 (`git status --porcelain`) and
3/5 (`WorktreeInUse`) stay live and unchanged — a destructive decision
re-verifies the filesystem itself.

That is what closes the leak the E-2087 hotfix accepted: condition 4 becomes the
exact content answer again, so a worktree whose work landed under rewritten SHAs
with no `task_landings` row is finally reclaimable, and the ◆ marker,
`task unsettled` and the reaper agree about "landed" once more.

**Removing the reaper from the hook path is the other half**, and it is
subtraction only: delete the five `ReapWorktreesForProject` calls in
`internal/hookcmd/claude.go` (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop,
SessionEnd). Nothing replaces them. Reaping was already happening at land; the
hook copies were duplicating it before and after every tool call.

## Who computes and who does not

**Never computes — cache-only:**
`monitor.AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` (the ◆ column in `session status` and
`session monitor`). A missing or invalid entry yields "not yet computed", never
a fabricated verdict. This is the change that removes the continuous range-diff
load: **measured 584ms per row for e-1077, gone from every tick of every pane.**

**Computes on a miss, and writes what it computed:**
- `session-query worktree-unsettled` (the Go entry point Python's `task
  unsettled` shells to) — a direct question deserves a real answer.
- The reaper's condition 4 — a guess is not acceptable before a delete.
- `internal/unlandedjob` — it is the writer.

**Stays live everywhere, never cached:** `git status --porcelain`. Filesystem
state changes without any ref moving, so it has no honest cache key. Measured
15-27ms per worktree; a pane renders a handful of rows (this session's view
renders 2), so the live cost is tens of milliseconds per tick — three orders of
magnitude below the range-diff it replaces.

## The fourth marker state

`unsettledMark` currently has three states: `◆` unsettled, `⊙` no work product,
space settled. Cache-only reading introduces a fourth, transient state — "not
computed yet" — and collapsing it into either `◆` or space would be a lie the
column already refuses to tell.

New glyph: **`~` (U+007E TILDE)**, meaning "not yet determined".

`·` was the obvious pick and is WRONG: `sessionstatuscmd` already defines it as
`referencedGlyph` (in `relation_tier.go`) and `buildLegend` prints it as
`· referenced`. In a row, position disambiguates (unsettledMark precedes the id,
relationField follows it) — but the legend has no position, and a frame holding
both states would print `~ not yet determined  · referenced` on one line under
one glyph. Flagged by the E-2017 session.

`~` clears the whole vocabulary in play in a single frame — actions
`● ↑ ↩ ⟳ ▶ ⚑ ✎ ☑ ◷ ⏚ ⁇ ⇥ ◌`, unsettled `◆ ⊙`, phase `✓ ! 1 2 3 ?`, hidden `⊘`,
relation `⊕ ·`, block `⊗ ⏸`. Being ASCII it is display width 1 BY DEFINITION,
which sidesteps the East Asian Ambiguous trap that forced `⊙` to be asserted
rather than assumed (E-1765, E-2107) — the width test is still written, but it
cannot fail. Its silhouette is a horizontal wave, colliding with nothing in a
set of circles, diamonds, arrows and boxes; `◌` being taken is what rules out
every dotted-circle variant. "Approximate, unresolved" is the right reading.

It is visible only until the job's next pass, and the monitor tick is what fires
the job, so the window is one interval.

`buildLegend` documents it on any rendered row that bears it, like the other two.
Like `⊙`, it must not veto `dim`.

## Code changes

**`internal/monitor/unlanded_cache.go`** (new). Path resolution via
`--git-common-dir`, `git worktree list --porcelain` parsing, the watermark
protocol, marker write and prune, and the two read modes (`CachedUnlanded` /
`ComputeUnlandedAndCache`). No serialisation layer: there is no record type to
marshal.

**`internal/monitor/worktree_unsettled.go`**. `worktreeUnsettledAt` gains a mode
parameter. `WorktreeUnsettledAt` (the ◆ path) becomes cache-only;
`WorktreeUnsettledDetailAt` (the on-demand path) computes on a miss.
`UnsettledDetail` gains `UnlandedKnown bool` and an accessor, distinct from the
existing `IsUndetermined()` — "not computed yet" is not "the probe failed".

**`internal/monitor/worktree_unlanded.go`**. `unlandedCommits` is unchanged; it
is now called only by the two computing paths.

**`internal/monitor/default_branch.go`**. Key `defaultBranchCache` on the git
COMMON dir rather than the worktree dir, so 135 worktrees share one memo within
a process instead of 135. Readers on the cache-only path get the base name from
`watermark.json` and do not resolve it at all — which removes the resolver from
the display path entirely, the ~60% the analysis measured.

**`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go`**. `maybeReapWorktree` condition 4 calls
the compute-on-miss cache read instead of `reapNothingToLand`; delete
`reapNothingToLand` and `landedSHAs` if nothing else uses them.
`AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` switches to the cache-only read.
`ReapWorktreesForProject` keeps its signature — `endless-go event
reap-worktrees` still calls it from the post-land sweep.

**`internal/monitor/session_status.go`**. `SessionStatusRow` gains
`UnsettledKnown bool`.

**`internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go`**. `unsettledMark` gains the `~`
case; `buildLegend` learns it; `colorize` excludes it from vetoing dim.

**`internal/sessionstatuscmd/json.go`**. Add `"unsettled_known": bool`.
`"unsettled"` stays a bool (false when unknown) so existing consumers do not
break.

**`internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go`**. `newWorktreeUnsettledJSON`
carries the new field through to Python.

**`src/endless/task_cmd.py`**. `_unsettled_probe`'s no-worktree literal gains
`"unlanded_known": True`; `unsettled_item` renders "not yet computed" when it is
false. No SQLite added — this file already stays clear of it.

**`internal/hookcmd/claude.go`**. Remove all five `ReapWorktreesForProject`
calls (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd). Nothing
replaces them: the job runs on the existing `liveview` trigger, which already
fires `jobs.RunDue` on each monitor refresh behind a single-in-flight guard and
a database lease.

**`cmd/endless-go`**. Blank-import `internal/unlandedjob` so its `init()`
registration runs, matching how the existing three jobs are wired.

## Consequences accepted

- **No monitor running anywhere means nothing is reaped.** Reaping is a TTL-gated
  cleanup with a 14-day default; a machine with no monitor open for a while
  accumulates directories and reclaims them on the next monitor tick. On this
  project, jobs are suppressed inside self-dev worktrees, so it is the
  main-checkout monitor that drives both jobs — unchanged from how the existing
  three already behave. On a stranger's project `InSelfDevWorktree` is false and
  any monitor drives them.
- **A fresh clone shows `·` until the job's first pass.** One interval.
- **E-2113 still matters.** The job runs on a goroutine inside the monitor
  process, so Ctrl-C in a pane still kills in-flight git children and still
  records ERR-0010 against an innocent task. This change shrinks the window
  enormously — the probe is no longer running continuously — but does not close
  it. E-2113 is already filed and is not folded in.

## Not in scope

- **The shared per-repo patch-id index.** Filed as E-2127 (`maybe`). It
  would cut a cold miss from ~584ms to ~100ms, but every miss is now paid by a
  background job off any critical path, and a settled verdict survives base
  movement, so cold-miss storms are small. Measure before building it.
- **Reliable landing recording.** A fourth symptom, not this root cause. Worth
  doing for the ledger's own sake; not required to make this correct.
- **Keeping worktrees in sync with the base.** Two jobs, filed separately:
  E-1881 (worktree metadata commits UP to main, which is what makes worktrees
  settle and become reapable) and its unfiled counterpart (main DOWN into idle
  worktrees, which collapses `baseRange` and is the only thing that removes the
  probe's cost at the source). E-1881 is a prerequisite for the second: it
  removes the overlapping-metadata commits that make a rebase conflict, which is
  the manual scenario E-1882 exists for. Both compose with this task rather than
  competing — a rebase moves the branch tip and invalidates that cache entry, but
  the recompute is then cheap by construction, because the drift it would have
  measured is exactly what the rebase removed.

## Verification

- Go unit tests for the validity protocol against a fixture repo: append to base
  (settled entry survives, unsettled entry invalidates), amend base (full
  flush), amend the branch (that entry only), change the configured base name
  (full flush), missing watermark (everything a miss).
- A test asserting the cache-only read NEVER shells `git range-diff`, using the
  existing `test_seam.go` seam — this is the property the whole task exists for
  and it should fail loudly if a future edit reintroduces a compute on the
  display path.
- Existing `worktree_unsettled_test.go` / `reap_worktrees_test.go` suites must
  pass with condition 4 rewired, and the post-land sweep must still reap:
  `worktree land` is the reaper's only trigger once the hook calls are gone.
- `TestUnsettledMark` extended for the fourth glyph's width and precedence, and
  a legend test asserting no two rendered states share a glyph.
- `tests/test_default_branch_parity.py` must still pass — the Python resolver is
  untouched.
- `just test` and `just test-go`.

fields.description: Implements ED-1589. The exact 'does this branch hold work the base lacks?' probe (git range-diff, measured 584ms per worktree) is recomputed by every consumer on every tick: the reaper on five hook branches including PreToolUse and PostToolUse, and every session monitor pane re-probing every rendered row every two seconds. Move it behind one background job that writes a content-addressed cache under the git common dir, and make the display path read-only with a fourth marker state for 'not yet determined'. Delete the five hook-path reaper calls; the reaper keeps its existing trigger, the post-land sweep worktree land already runs, and gains an exact condition 4 that reads the cache. Restores agreement between the reaper, the diamond marker and 'task unsettled' about what landed, which the E-2087 hotfix broke on purpose, and closes the reclamation leak it accepted.

triage.rationale: the content-addressed cache's key scheme, invalidation trigger, and the exact "condition 4" logic the sweep must implement are not specified, leaving material design decisions open.

fields.title: Stop worktrees drifting from main with one sync job: endless-managed commits up, then rebase down
fields.description: One job, one pass per worktree, two steps in a fixed order. Step 1, the original scope: sync endless-auto commits touching only .endless/plans, .endless/analyses and .endless/db-ledger from each worktree branch up to main — never code or tests, which stay gated by the normal land workflow. That is what lets a long-lived worktree settle and become reclaimable, and it shrinks the concurrent-append window for ledger shards. Step 2, absorbed from E-2129: rebase the worktree onto main, moving the merge base forward and collapsing the range the exact unlanded probe pays for, since that cost scales with drift rather than with what the branch holds. The order is not optional — rebasing first hits the overlapping-metadata conflicts E-1882 resolves by hand. Step 2 touches only worktrees with no live session and no process holding cwd, via the WorktreeInUse predicate. Runs on E-698's fire-once runner. Re-examine E-1882's remaining scope once this lands.
fields.analysis:
## One operation, two steps, fixed order

Absorbs E-2129. The two directions were filed as separate tasks with a blocker
between them; that blocker was not a dependency between two features but step
ordering inside one algorithm, which is what made them one task (ED-1550).

Per worktree, in this order:

1. **Up — endless-managed commits to main.** Sync the `endless-auto` commits
   touching only `.endless/plans`, `.endless/analyses` and `.endless/db-ledger`
   from the worktree branch to main. Never code, tests, or any non-`.endless`
   file: those stay gated by the normal land workflow.
2. **Down — rebase the worktree onto main.** Moves the merge base forward.

Neither step subsumes the other, and each does something the other cannot:

- Step 1 is what lets a long-lived worktree SETTLE and become reclaimable.
  Those metadata commits are the bulk of what makes a branch read as holding
  unlanded work. It does nothing for probe cost; by growing main faster it
  slightly increases the cost for every other worktree.
- Step 2 is what removes the probe's cost at the source, and it settles nothing.

## Why the order is not optional

Without step 1 first, the branch still holds metadata commits that main changed
independently, so the rebase hits exactly the overlapping-edit conflicts
E-1882 (`endless worktree reconcile`) exists to resolve by hand — the scenario
that cost ~20 minutes of manual investigation during the E-1537 land. Step 1
running first leaves little on the branch to conflict with, which is what makes
an unattended rebase safe.

## The cost model step 2 exploits

The exact unlanded probe (`unlandedCommits`, via `git range-diff`) costs in
proportion to how far the base has drifted since the fork — the patch-ids it
computes are for every commit the BASE gained, not for what the branch holds.
Measured on this repo: a worktree 2251 commits behind costs 2.1s; e-1077, 648
behind, costs 584ms. A branch sitting at the base tip has an empty base range
and costs almost nothing.

So step 2 does not make the algorithm cheaper — it removes the input that makes
the algorithm expensive.

## Hard constraint on step 2

Only worktrees with NO live session and no process holding cwd inside, via the
same `WorktreeInUse` predicate the reaper shares with the other destructive
path (E-1947). A rebase rewrites history underneath whoever is sitting in the
directory. This is not a tunable.

Step 1 has no such constraint — it reads commits from the branch and writes to
main, leaving the worktree untouched.

## Re-examine E-1882 once this lands

E-1882 (`endless worktree reconcile`) was filed to resolve drift AFTER it
accumulates, by classifying each unlanded commit and telling the operator what
would happen before doing anything destructive. If this job runs continuously,
the drift it resolves largely stops accumulating, and its remaining scope
shrinks to the cases this job cannot touch — worktrees held by a live session,
and branches whose metadata commits genuinely diverge rather than duplicate.

That may leave E-1882 worth keeping as a narrower manual escape hatch, worth
folding into this job's failure path, or obsolete. Decide it with measurements
after this lands, not before: the question is how often a land still hits a
rebase conflict once this job is running.

## Interaction with E-2128

Both steps move the branch tip, invalidating that worktree's cached unlanded
answer. They compose rather than fight — the cache is content-addressed and
self-invalidating, so there is nothing to coordinate, and the recompute is
cheap by construction because the drift it would have measured is exactly what
step 2 removed.

## Open mechanism question for the planning pass

Rebase versus merge is E-1109's config preference. Rebase matches what
`worktree land` already does; a merge is gentler but leaves a merge commit on
every task branch.

payload.outcome: Merged into E-1881, which now covers both sync directions. The blocked-by link between the two was not a dependency between features but step ordering inside one algorithm — push endless-managed commits up, then rebase down — which is what made them one task under ED-1550. E-1881 carries this task's analysis verbatim, including the cost model, the WorktreeInUse constraint on the rebase step, and the interaction with E-2128's cache. Nothing from this task is lost; read E-1881.

triage.rationale: the rebase step's conflict-handling and failure behavior (e.g. what happens when the rebase fails or hits non-metadata conflicts, and how it interacts with the in-progress E-1882 hand-resolution work) is not specified.

payload.title: Propagate an interrupted git child through DefaultBranch so a Ctrl-C does not record ERR-0011
payload.description: DefaultBranch collapses every git error into ErrDefaultBranchUnresolved, so a git child interrupted during default-branch resolution records ERR-0011 — the misclassification E-2113 removed for ERR-0010, surviving under a different error code. defaultBranchCache then memoizes that failure, so one Ctrl-C poisons every later probe in the process rather than costing one tick. E-2113's guards on the two default-branch fault recorders are correct but unreachable until the resolver stops swallowing the interrupt.
payload.analysis:
## What is left behind

E-2113 classified an interrupted git child at the source — `monitor.runGit`
wraps a child that died on SIGINT with `ErrGitInterrupted` — and put the guard
inside the three functions that record a git-derived fault, so a probe added
later inherits it rather than having to remember it. Two of those three,
`recordDefaultBranchFault` and `recordReapDefaultBranchFault`, are correct but
currently unreachable.

`resolveDefaultBranch`'s fall-through helpers — `originHeadBranch`,
`gitConfigValue`, `branchIfExists` — each swallow their `runGit` error and
return `""`. That is deliberate: a step that does not resolve is supposed to
fall through to the next, and E-1166's finding (origin/HEAD is unset on a fresh
clone) is why there are four steps rather than one. But it means the
classification is discarded there, and every caller sees only
`ErrDefaultBranchUnresolved`.

So a Ctrl-C landing during resolution still files an incident — ERR-0011 rather
than ERR-0010, about the same innocent worktree, for the same reason E-2113
removed.

## The memoized failure makes it outlive the signal

`defaultBranchCache` stores errors as well as answers. An interrupted resolve is
cached, so every later probe of that repoDir in the same process reads the
cached failure — a single interrupt poisons the rest of the process rather than
costing one tick. E-2113's plan noted this under "Not in scope" and called it
harmless *there*, because the process that took the SIGINT is exiting. It is not
harmless here: `session monitor` is not the only caller, and the reaper runs on
PreToolUse/PostToolUse in a process that keeps going.

## Fix direction

Let an interrupt SHORT-CIRCUIT the fall-through rather than be absorbed by it:
the three helpers return their error alongside the name, and
`resolveDefaultBranch` bails on `errors.Is(err, ErrGitInterrupted)` instead of
trying the next candidate. An interrupted probe has said nothing about which
branch is the default, and trying the next step is asking a question whose
answer was already lost. Everything else about the four-step order is unchanged.

Worth deciding alongside: whether `DefaultBranch` should decline to memoize an
interrupted resolve at all. The cached failure is not a fact about the
repository, and it outlives the signal that produced it.

## Why E-2113 did not fold this in

Two things make it more than a one-line guard.

The step order is mirrored by `endless.worktree_cmd._default_base_branch` on the
Python side, and `tests/test_default_branch_parity.py` asserts the two agree
case for case rather than trusting the comment. Changing what each step returns
has a cross-language contract to keep.

And E-2111 is live in the same files.

## Scale

This is the tail of E-2113's defect, not a second instance of it. `DefaultBranch`
is memoized and resolves once per repoDir; the probe E-2113 fixed re-runs on
every row every two seconds, which is why a Ctrl-C hit it with near-certainty.
The window here is much narrower — but it is the same misclassification, and the
memoization is the part that makes it worth closing rather than tolerating.

# Plan — one writer computes the unlanded verdict, every reader reads it

Commits ED-1589. Defers the patch-id index to E-2127, and the two
worktree-sync jobs to E-1881 and E-2129.

## The decision

The exact "does this branch hold work the base lacks?" verdict stops being
computed by its consumers and becomes **derived state owned by one background
job**. Consumers read a per-repo file cache. The reaper comes off the
PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook path entirely and becomes a job of its own.

This is one change, not two, because the reaper's periodic-sweep cost and the
monitor's continuous fan-out are the same defect: *the verdict is recomputed
from scratch by every consumer on every tick, with no shared derived state.*
Under ED-1550 §3 that is one cause, so it is one task.

## The invariant this rests on, and how it is checked rather than trusted

The unlanded set can only SHRINK as the base branch gains commits. The probe
asks, for each branch commit since the fork, whether a matching commit exists on
base since the fork. Adding commits to base only adds candidates to match
against: a commit that already matched keeps its match, and one that did not may
acquire one. Nothing that matched becomes unmatched.

Therefore:

- **A verdict of ZERO unlanded stays true as long as the BRANCH tip does not
  move**, no matter how far the base advances.
- **A verdict of N>0 is only valid while BOTH tips are unchanged**, because base
  movement can shrink it.

The invariant assumes the base is append-only. That assumption is CHECKED, not
trusted, by a repo-level watermark (below). An amended, reset, or force-pushed
base is detected and flushes the cache; a `--amend` on a task BRANCH moves the
branch tip and self-invalidates that one entry.

Two things the invariant deliberately does not cover, both pre-existing and
neither introduced here: work that landed and was later REVERTED still reads as
settled (the original landed commit is still in base's history to match
against), and uncommitted/untracked files are not commits at all — they are a
separate probe that stays live.

## The cache — content-addressed paths, no file format

**Location.** `<git-common-dir>/info/endless/unlanded/`

`git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` from inside any linked
worktree resolves to the main checkout's `.git`, so every worktree of a repo
shares one cache directory for free. Verified on git 2.52.0. `.git/info/` is
untracked, never pushed, per-clone, and survives `git gc` — the correct home for
derived state describing this clone. No database, so sandbox routing does not
apply and the probe stays DB-free (the property `_unsettled_probe` documents:
`--db main` from inside a worktree and a bare run agree by construction).

**Layout. There is no file format — every key is a path, and the only file with
contents holds exactly the bytes a consumer needs.**

```
<git-common-dir>/info/endless/unlanded/
  base-<name>                                  # 41 bytes: last-verified base tip OID
  settled/<branch-tip-oid>                     # EMPTY file. presence = fully landed.
  unsettled/<base-tip-oid>/<branch-tip-oid>    # unlanded commit lines, one per line
```

Why each piece carries no fields:

- **`settled/<branch-tip-oid>` is empty.** "Fully landed" is a property of the
  branch-tip OID and the base branch ALONE — same HEAD and same base give the
  same answer whichever directory the probe ran in — and the invariant above says
  it is permanent while the base is append-only. There is nothing left to qualify
  it with. Two worktrees at one OID legitimately share an entry.
- **`unsettled/<base-tip-oid>/<branch-tip-oid>` nests under the base tip.** A
  non-zero verdict is valid only until the base moves; nesting makes base movement
  render the whole directory unreachable, so INVALIDATION IS A PATH MISS requiring
  zero logic and zero stored field. Its contents are the exact lines
  `parseUnlandedRows` already produces, bounded by the existing `unlandedLogLimit`;
  the count is the line count.
- **`base-<name>` holds one OID.** The base NAME is in the filename, so editing
  `default_branch` in `.endless/config.json` orphans the old watermark
  automatically and reads as full invalidation.

Deliberately absent, each removable without breaking a rule: a format version
(the cache is rebuildable derived state, so an unreadable file is simply a miss
and no migration can ever be needed), the worktree path, a per-entry base name,
a stored probe error (absence already means unknown, and unknown already fails
closed — a failed compute writes nothing), and a computed-at timestamp (no
validity rule reads one). Nothing here can drift out of sync with git, because
every key IS a git object id.

**Validity protocol**, run once per process, not per row:

1. One call to `git worktree list --porcelain` yields every worktree path, every
   worktree's HEAD OID, and the base branch's own tip. **Measured: 14ms for 135
   worktrees on this repo.** That is the entire enumeration and tip-reading step.
2. Read `base-<name>`. Absent, or the name has changed → treat every `settled/`
   entry as a miss (the job then rebuilds). Equal to the current base tip →
   proceed. Different → `git merge-base --is-ancestor <stored> <current>`:
   - exit 0 → base only appended. Every `settled/` entry stands. The job writes
     the new tip; readers never write it.
   - exit 1 → base history was rewritten (amend, reset, force-push). Every
     `settled/` entry is invalid; the job empties `settled/` and recomputes.
   - any other exit → fail closed: every lookup is a miss.
3. Per worktree, with HEAD `B` and current base tip `T`: `settled/B` exists →
   settled. Else `unsettled/T/B` exists → unsettled, and its lines are the log.
   Else → not yet determined.

**Writes.** An empty `settled/` marker is a create-or-nothing operation with no
partial state. An `unsettled/` file is written temp-then-rename in the same
directory. The job prunes `settled/` entries matching no current worktree HEAD
and removes every `unsettled/` directory that is not the current base tip.

**When the cache directory cannot be created or written** — a read-only checkout,
a permissions problem — every lookup is a permanent miss: displays show the
uncomputed marker and on-demand callers recompute each time. Correct, just not
fast. Record ONE fault fingerprinted on the directory so the condition is
visible, matching how `recordDefaultBranchFault` handles a resolver that will
never succeed; do not fault per worktree per pass.

## Cancellation, on top of what E-2113 landed

E-2113 landed the classification but not a context: `runGit` still builds its
child with `exec.Command`, and `killedBySIGINT` tags a SIGINT death as
`ErrGitInterrupted` so an interrupted probe is undetermined rather than an
incident. The pool needs cancellation, and `jobs.Job` requires `Run` to honour
the lease deadline its ctx carries.

Add `runGitContext(ctx, dir, args...)` alongside `runGit`, built with
`exec.CommandContext`. `runGit` keeps its signature so its ~20 existing call
sites do not churn; it becomes a thin wrapper passing `context.Background()`.

The trap to avoid: `exec.CommandContext` kills with SIGKILL on cancellation, and
E-2113 deliberately keeps SIGKILL faultable because a SIGKILL is usually the OOM
killer and worth knowing about. A cancelled lease would therefore record a fault
per in-flight worktree. So `runGitContext` checks `ctx.Err() != nil` after Wait
and classifies as `ErrGitInterrupted` in that case — extending E-2113's rule to
a second benign death rather than widening `killedBySIGINT`, which would lose
the OOM signal it was narrowed to keep.

With that in place the job records probe faults exactly like every other caller.
No consecutive-failure counter: the noise it would have suppressed was
E-2113's bug, and E-2113 has landed.

## One job, plus the reap trigger that already exists

**`internal/unlandedjob`** — name `worktree-unlanded`. `Interval: 60s`,
`LeaseTTL: 15m`. Follows the existing `internal/backupjob` shape: own package,
`init()` registers, `Name`/`Schedule`/`Run`. It runs the validity protocol,
recomputes every invalid entry through the bounded pool, writes each marker,
advances the watermark, and prunes entries for worktrees git no longer lists.

It covers EVERY worktree git lists, ordered by the worktree directory's mtime,
newest first. Ordering matters more than scope: the cache converges on the
worktrees someone has actually been working in within the first seconds of a
cold pass, and the long tail of dormant directories fills in behind them without
anyone waiting on it. Directory mtime is one `stat` per worktree and reads no
database, which keeps the probe DB-free — the property E-2087 established and
`_unsettled_probe` documents. It is a slightly noisy signal (any write touches
it, including a build artifact) and that is acceptable for an ordering heuristic
that affects nothing but warm-up order.

A cold pass over 135 worktrees is ~10-20s through the pool; a warm pass is one
14ms git call plus N path lookups. The lease exceeds the cold case comfortably.

`MaxBackoff` is zero, matching `backupjob`'s rationale: failures here are cheap
and idempotent, and backing off would leave the cache stale exactly when the
probe path is known to be sick. The runner's recorded fault is the alarm.

It is triggered by the existing `liveview` job runner, which already fires
`jobs.RunDue` on each monitor refresh behind a single-in-flight guard and a
database lease. Nothing new is wired.

**The reaper gets no job and no new trigger.** It already runs where it should:
`worktree_cmd.land_worktree` calls `_reap_stale_worktrees(main_root)` as a
post-land best-effort sweep, shelling to `endless-go event reap-worktrees` with
stderr forwarded so reaped directories are printed to the person who ran the
land. That is the right moment and the right visibility — a land is what makes
other worktrees reclaimable, and the person who caused the reclamation sees what
was reclaimed. This task neither moves it nor adds a cadence to it.

What DOES change in the reaper: `maybeReapWorktree`'s condition 4 reads the
cache in COMPUTE-ON-MISS mode instead of running `reapNothingToLand`, because a
delete must never act on a guess. Conditions 5 (`git status --porcelain`) and
3/5 (`WorktreeInUse`) stay live and unchanged — a destructive decision
re-verifies the filesystem itself.

That is what closes the leak the E-2087 hotfix accepted: condition 4 becomes the
exact content answer again, so a worktree whose work landed under rewritten SHAs
with no `task_landings` row is finally reclaimable, and the ◆ marker,
`task unsettled` and the reaper agree about "landed" once more.

**Removing the reaper from the hook path is the other half**, and it is
subtraction only: delete the five `ReapWorktreesForProject` calls in
`internal/hookcmd/claude.go` (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop,
SessionEnd). Nothing replaces them. Reaping was already happening at land; the
hook copies were duplicating it before and after every tool call.

## Who computes and who does not

**Never computes — cache-only:**
`monitor.AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` (the ◆ column in `session status` and
`session monitor`). A missing or invalid entry yields "not yet computed", never
a fabricated verdict. This is the change that removes the continuous range-diff
load: **measured 584ms per row for e-1077, gone from every tick of every pane.**

**Computes on a miss, and writes what it computed:**
- `session-query worktree-unsettled` (the Go entry point Python's `task
  unsettled` shells to) — a direct question deserves a real answer.
- The reaper's condition 4 — a guess is not acceptable before a delete.
- `internal/unlandedjob` — it is the writer.

**Misses are computed CONCURRENTLY through one bounded pool**, shared by the
batch probe and the job's cold pass. `task unsettled --all` batches every active
worktree into a single `session-query` call, so a cold cache would otherwise
cost ~0.6s per worktree serially — over a minute of silence before the first row
prints. With the pool it is bounded by pool size instead.

Pool size is `min(8, runtime.NumCPU())`: git is CPU-bound here (patch-ids) and
oversubscribing one repo buys nothing. Serial callers — the reaper computing one
condition-4 answer, `task unsettled <id>` on one worktree — do not enter the
pool.

**Stays live everywhere, never cached:** `git status --porcelain`. Filesystem
state changes without any ref moving, so it has no honest cache key. Measured
15-27ms per worktree; a pane renders a handful of rows (this session's view
renders 2), so the live cost is tens of milliseconds per tick — three orders of
magnitude below the range-diff it replaces.

## The fourth marker state

`unsettledMark` currently has three states: `◆` unsettled, `⊙` no work product,
space settled. Cache-only reading introduces a fourth, transient state — "not
computed yet" — and collapsing it into either `◆` or space would be a lie the
column already refuses to tell.

New glyph: **`~` (U+007E TILDE)**, meaning "not yet determined".

`·` was the obvious pick and is WRONG: `sessionstatuscmd` already defines it as
`referencedGlyph` (in `relation_tier.go`) and `buildLegend` prints it as
`· referenced`. In a row, position disambiguates (unsettledMark precedes the id,
relationField follows it) — but the legend has no position, and a frame holding
both states would print `~ not yet determined  · referenced` on one line under
one glyph. Flagged by the E-2017 session.

`~` clears the whole vocabulary in play in a single frame — actions
`● ↑ ↩ ⟳ ▶ ⚑ ✎ ☑ ◷ ⏚ ⁇ ⇥ ◌`, unsettled `◆ ⊙`, phase `✓ ! 1 2 3 ?`, hidden `⊘`,
relation `⊕ ·`, block `⊗ ⏸`. Being ASCII it is display width 1 BY DEFINITION,
which sidesteps the East Asian Ambiguous trap that forced `⊙` to be asserted
rather than assumed (E-1765, E-2107) — the width test is still written, but it
cannot fail. Its silhouette is a horizontal wave, colliding with nothing in a
set of circles, diamonds, arrows and boxes; `◌` being taken is what rules out
every dotted-circle variant. "Approximate, unresolved" is the right reading.

**Precedence: `~` is tested FIRST.** If the expensive answer has not been
computed, the row says so rather than reporting a state derived from something
else — so `~` outranks `◆`, `⊙` and blank:

```
case !r.UnsettledKnown: "~"
case r.Unsettled:       "◆"
case !Shipped:          "⊙"
default:                " "
```

Two refinements keep `~` from swallowing rows whose answer IS known, and both
fall out of what each probe costs rather than being policy:

- **A task with no worktree is KNOWN**, not unknown. There is nothing to land
  and no git ran, so `UnsettledKnown` is true and the row resolves to `⊙` or
  blank as it does today.
- **A dirty worktree is KNOWN to be unsettled.** `git status --porcelain` stays
  live, so modifications are visible every tick without the cache. A row whose
  working tree is modified is `◆` even with no cached commit answer. `~`
  therefore means specifically: the worktree is CLEAN, and whether its commits
  reached the base has not been computed yet.

That makes `~` rarer than the precedence rule alone suggests — it appears on
clean worktrees during the first job pass after a cold start, and on a machine
where nothing fires the job. It is visible only until the job's next pass, and
the monitor tick is what fires the job, so the window is normally one interval.

`buildLegend` documents it on any rendered row that bears it, like the other two.
Like `⊙`, it must not veto `dim`.

## Code changes

**`internal/monitor/unlanded_cache.go`** (new). Path resolution via
`--git-common-dir`, `git worktree list --porcelain` parsing, the watermark
protocol, marker write and prune, and the two read modes (`CachedUnlanded` /
`ComputeUnlandedAndCache`). No serialisation layer: there is no record type to
marshal.

**`internal/monitor/worktree_unsettled.go`**. `worktreeUnsettledAt` gains a mode
parameter. `WorktreeUnsettledAt` (the ◆ path) becomes cache-only;
`WorktreeUnsettledDetailAt` (the on-demand path) computes on a miss.
`UnsettledDetail` gains `UnlandedKnown bool` and an accessor, distinct from the
existing `IsUndetermined()` — "not computed yet" is not "the probe failed".

**`internal/monitor/worktree_unlanded.go`**. `unlandedCommits` takes a context
and calls `runGitContext`, so a cancelled lease stops its git children instead
of racing them. Its logic is otherwise unchanged; it is now reached only from
the computing paths.

**`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go`** (also). Add `runGitContext` beside
`runGit` and reduce `runGit` to a wrapper over it, so the ~20 existing call
sites keep their signature. Classify a cancelled context as
`ErrGitInterrupted`, alongside E-2113's `killedBySIGINT`.

**`internal/monitor/unlanded_pool.go`** (new). The bounded worker pool
(`min(8, runtime.NumCPU())`) shared by the batch probe and the job's cold pass,
and the mtime-descending ordering of worktrees.

**`internal/monitor/default_branch.go`**. Key `defaultBranchCache` on the git
COMMON dir rather than the worktree dir, so 135 worktrees share one memo within
a process instead of 135. Readers on the cache-only path get the base name from
`watermark.json` and do not resolve it at all — which removes the resolver from
the display path entirely, the ~60% the analysis measured.

**`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go`**. `maybeReapWorktree` condition 4 calls
the compute-on-miss cache read instead of `reapNothingToLand`; delete
`reapNothingToLand` and `landedSHAs` if nothing else uses them.
`AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` switches to the cache-only read.
`ReapWorktreesForProject` keeps its signature — `endless-go event
reap-worktrees` still calls it from the post-land sweep.

**`internal/monitor/session_status.go`**. `SessionStatusRow` gains
`UnsettledKnown bool`.

**`internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go`**. `unsettledMark` gains the `~`
case; `buildLegend` learns it; `colorize` excludes it from vetoing dim.

**`internal/sessionstatuscmd/json.go`**. Add `"unsettled_known": bool`.
`"unsettled"` stays a bool (false when unknown) so existing consumers do not
break.

**`internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go`**. `newWorktreeUnsettledJSON`
carries the new field through to Python.

**`src/endless/task_cmd.py`**. `_unsettled_probe`'s no-worktree literal gains
`"unlanded_known": True`; `unsettled_item` renders "not yet computed" when it is
false. No SQLite added — this file already stays clear of it.

**`src/endless/worktree_cmd.py`**. After a successful land, warm the cache for
the worktree just landed. The rebase-then-fast-forward leaves its branch tip
equal to the base, so the answer is known to be "settled" without running any
probe; writing the marker costs one file create and spares the next monitor tick
a recompute for the one worktree whose state definitely just changed. Best
effort, next to the existing post-land reap sweep, and never fatal to the land.

**`internal/hookcmd/claude.go`**. Remove all five `ReapWorktreesForProject`
calls (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd). Nothing
replaces them: the job runs on the existing `liveview` trigger, which already
fires `jobs.RunDue` on each monitor refresh behind a single-in-flight guard and
a database lease.

**`cmd/endless-go`**. Blank-import `internal/unlandedjob` so its `init()`
registration runs, matching how the existing three jobs are wired.

## Consequences accepted

- **No monitor running anywhere means nothing is reaped.** Reaping is a TTL-gated
  cleanup with a 14-day default; a machine with no monitor open for a while
  accumulates directories and reclaims them on the next monitor tick. On this
  project, jobs are suppressed inside self-dev worktrees, so it is the
  main-checkout monitor that drives both jobs — unchanged from how the existing
  three already behave. On a stranger's project `InSelfDevWorktree` is false and
  any monitor drives them.
- **A fresh clone shows `·` until the job's first pass.** One interval.
- **E-2113 still matters.** The job runs on a goroutine inside the monitor
  process, so Ctrl-C in a pane still kills in-flight git children and still
  records ERR-0010 against an innocent task. This change shrinks the window
  enormously — the probe is no longer running continuously — but does not close
  it. E-2113 is already filed and is not folded in.

## Not in scope

- **The shared per-repo patch-id index.** Filed as E-2127 (`maybe`). It
  would cut a cold miss from ~584ms to ~100ms, but every miss is now paid by a
  background job off any critical path, and a settled verdict survives base
  movement, so cold-miss storms are small. Measure before building it.
- **Reliable landing recording.** A fourth symptom, not this root cause. Worth
  doing for the ledger's own sake; not required to make this correct.
- **Keeping worktrees in sync with the base.** Two jobs, filed separately:
  E-1881 (worktree metadata commits UP to main, which is what makes worktrees
  settle and become reapable) and its unfiled counterpart (main DOWN into idle
  worktrees, which collapses `baseRange` and is the only thing that removes the
  probe's cost at the source). E-1881 is a prerequisite for the second: it
  removes the overlapping-metadata commits that make a rebase conflict, which is
  the manual scenario E-1882 exists for. Both compose with this task rather than
  competing — a rebase moves the branch tip and invalidates that cache entry, but
  the recompute is then cheap by construction, because the drift it would have
  measured is exactly what the rebase removed.

## Verification

- Go unit tests for the validity protocol against a fixture repo: append to base
  (settled entry survives, unsettled entry invalidates), amend base (full
  flush), amend the branch (that entry only), change the configured base name
  (full flush), missing watermark (everything a miss).
- A test asserting the cache-only read NEVER shells `git range-diff`, using the
  existing `test_seam.go` seam — this is the property the whole task exists for
  and it should fail loudly if a future edit reintroduces a compute on the
  display path.
- Existing `worktree_unsettled_test.go` / `reap_worktrees_test.go` suites must
  pass with condition 4 rewired, and the post-land sweep must still reap:
  `worktree land` is the reaper's only trigger once the hook calls are gone.
- `TestUnsettledMark` extended for the fourth glyph's width and precedence —
  including that a no-worktree row and a dirty worktree never render `~` — and a
  legend test asserting no two rendered states share a glyph.
- A cancellation test: cancel the context mid-probe and assert the error is
  `ErrGitInterrupted` and that NO fault was recorded, the same guarantee
  E-2113 landed for SIGINT. `internal/monitor/git_interrupt_test.go` already has
  the harness for the SIGINT half.
- A pool test asserting concurrency is bounded and that a cold batch over N
  fixture worktrees completes without exceeding the cap.
- `tests/test_default_branch_parity.py` must still pass — the Python resolver is
  untouched.
- `just test` and `just test-go`.
